descEn:
This year, the Ars Electronica Festival will transform the city of Linz itself into a vibrant venue. Spread over three major festival hubs—OK QUARTER, MED CAMPUS and DANUBE TRIANGLE—and over 40 locations throughout the city, we invite you to explore our exhibitions and the latest in media art.

This year’s theme exhibition Negotiating Humanity understands art as an infrastructure for negotiation, as a space in which perceived certainties can be challenged. Across three parts, the exhibition explores our systems of beliefs and questions how realities are produced and what forms of coexistence b

At the Ars Electronica Festival you can expect extraordinary events, concerts and performances—from the Opening Event at St. Mary’s Cathedral to the Big Concert Night and Nightline Program at Posthof Linz, to the Futurelab Night Performances at the Ars Electronica Center. An experience for all the senses—innovative, immersive and surprising.

The Ars Electronica Festival is a place for discussions about the future—interdisciplinary, international and visionary. In conferences, lectures, panels and discussions, creative minds from the fields of art, science and technology come together to share their perspectives on the world of tomorrow.

Creative minds from all over the world come together in workshops and open discussion formats—artists, scientists, activists and curious visitors. Together with experts, they experiment, discuss and think ahead. The practical formats invite visitors to share knowledge, develop new perspectives and network with like-minded people—creating room for exchange, new impulses and sustainable connections.

WE GUIDE YOU invites you to explore the core exhibitions within our guided tour program. Together with our tour guides and the participants on each tour, you will join in a discussion around the themes of this year’s festival and encounter the protagonists of the projects.

What began in 1979 as a simple festival has evolved over the decades into a vibrant, multifaceted ecosystem. Today, Ars Electronica is far more than just an event: it is a platform for art, science and technology; a learning space for society; and a laboratory for social innovation. During this year’s festival, we’re opening our doors to all these different areas and inviting you to experience our projects up close over the five days of the festival, engage in conversation with our experts, and become part of this dynamic network.

ticket: FESTIVALPASS+, FESTIVALPASS, DAYPASS, Partner Venue Ticket
descEn:
This exhibition presents six works—primarily Golden Nica and Grand Prize winners— selected from the Prix Ars Electronica 2026 (4,329 submissions from 106 countries) and the European Commission’s STARTS Prize 2026 (2,719 submissions from 110 countries).

Each of these works deconstructs and reimagines, with striking necessity, the notion of “humanity” that we have long taken for granted—from diverse perspectives, including bodily perception, the nature of capitalist technology, the new autonomous creativity of AI, history, geopolitics and the climate crisis. descEn: What we see, hear and feel, we interpret as reality. It appears immediate, yet it is already filtered, ordered and interpreted. Reality emerges through the interplay between inner perception and the external world, between individual and collective context. It is never simply a matter of what is real, nor does it exist independently of the frameworks through which we make sense of it. Embedded within collective systems of interpretation, reality dictates what is considered relevant, visible or sayable. Processes of standardization, classification and regulation produce the frameworks within wh

What does it mean to negotiate the future in uncertain times? Universities are supposed to be places where difficult questions are asked, certainties are challenged and new perspectives are put to the test. 
Scholars at Risk documented 395 attacks on scholars and students in 49 countries between July 2024 and June 2025. The Academic Freedom Index 2026 reveals that institutional autonomy at universities in the United States has deteriorated by 50 percent since 2015. Academic freedom is under pressure even in places where it was long taken for granted. 
The conditions under which the participati

For decades, Ars Electronica has built a global network of cultural institutions, research centers and universities that share a commitment to exploring the relationship between art, technology and society. The Ars Electronica Features Exhibition highlights selected institutions, forming a platform that brings together these partner institutions from across the world to present their own artistic and research-based perspectives on the festival’s curatorial theme, reflecting the diversity of contexts, disciplines and cultural traditions from which they emerge.

This year, sixteen partners take

nameEn: Expanded Play Gallery – Exhibition of Playful Media
descEn: Now in its third edition, the Expanded Play Gallery features a curated selection of interactive works that address a wide range of topics through the medium of play. From dynamic shadow worlds inspired by Plato’s Allegory of the Cave, to the sonification of urban data or conversations with an artificial messiah, the exhibition spans a diverse range of artistic positions and technological approaches. Together, the works invite participants to engage directly with the evolving relationships between humans and machines, challenging conventional understandings of interaction, perception and digita

In 2026, Johannes Kepler University Linz (JKU) looks back on sixty years of research, education and social responsibility—and on the claim not just to observe change, but to shape it. The future does not only start tomorrow; it started long ago, in auditoriums and laboratories, in scientific and artistic experiments, in conversations and discussions.
NEGOTIATING HUMANITY – FUTURE BEGINS is therefore more than a festival theme—it is an invitation to understand humankind as an open question. What does humanity mean when machines keep learning, systems take decisions and realities can be simulate

Interactive stations, works of art, research projects, large-scale projections and laboratories. The Ars Electronica Center invites you to exciting and inspiring excursions into the future fields of Artificial Intelligence and neuroscience, robotics and autonomous mobility, as well as genetic engineering and biotechnology!

ticket: FESTIVALPASS+, FESTIVALPASS, DAYPASS, Ars Electronica Center Ticket
descEn:
Open Futurelab once again opens the doors of Ars Electronica’s artistic R&D laboratory and atelier, offering insights into artistic research as an open, collaborative process. At the Ars Electronica Center, visitors encounter the new interactive exhibition Hello Worlds!, alongside research prototypes and installations. 

Together with additional pieces at satellite locations throughout Linz, the works make the Futurelab’s questions, methods and experiments tangible—and invite everyone to take part in imagining what comes next.

Our festival would not be possible on this scale without the invaluable support of our partners. Their projects and events enrich the festival with a diverse supporting program, taking place from 9 to 13 September 2026 in Linz.

It all starts at 3:00 PM at the Lentos Kunstmuseum with a premiere. Hemma Schmutz (Director of the Lentos Kunstmuseum) and Gerfried Stocker (Artistic Director) invite guests to the opening of NEGOTIATING HUMANITY – Award-Winning Works Exhibition, which for the first time brings together the projects of the winners of the Prix Ars Electronica and the European Union’s S+T+ARTS Prize and takes on the festival theme.

At 5:00 PM sharp, Brigitte Hütter (Rector of the University of Arts Linz) and Manuela Naveau (curator of this year’s Campus) welcome guests in the courtyard of the University of Arts

Under the title NEGOTIATING HUMANITY – FUTURE BEGINS, the festival puts fundamental questions about humanity up for negotiation. On the opening night, a clear declaration is made: a commitment to humanity—more precisely, to the unbreakable humanity found in art and in the shared experience of it. St. Mary’s Cathedral, with its overwhelming spatial and acoustic scale, becomes the resonating chamber for this declaration. Here, the most diverse musical languages and worldviews of the past five centuries meet—along with equally diverse ideas of what makes us human, and how that humanity can find e

Polaris – Music Between the Poles

This year, Ars Electronica’s Big Concert Night unfolds as a multimedia Gesamtkunstwerk. Staged across three concert halls, visitors move between strikingly different concerts and performances, each performed several times throughout the evening so that audiences can experience them in shifting constellations and atmospheres.
Polaris—the pole star and fixed point of this constellation—embodies the festival’s guiding theme: the question of what it fundamentally means to be human, of “conditio humana.” It’s a question we can only approach by looking past the pol

What happens when negotiation is not conducted through words, but through bodies, frequencies and collective presence? At a time when words become weapons and language grows harsher, the Nightline creates a counter-model: a physical, shared space where different perspectives do not inevitably harden into irreconcilable opposites, but can meet and engage with one another. Ars Electronica Nightline 2026 at Posthof Linz does not seek to provide an answer—it turns the question itself into an experience.
FARCE opens the night. Veronika König’s Viennese avant-pop project sets the tone with a refusal

descEn:
Since its opening in 2009, Deep Space 8K has been a defining feature of the Ars Electronica Center and one of the highlights of the Ars Electronica Festival. As the spectacular successor to the Center’s pioneering CAVE, it continues a tradition that stretches back to the very beginnings of the Ars Electronica Center 30 years ago: creating cutting-edge immersive spaces where art, science, technology and breathtaking visual experiences converge.
This year, Deep Space 8K presents a special focus on “Living Archives”, exploring how digital technologies are transforming our relationship with cultur

The Ars Electronica Festival 2026 presents a diverse program of performances at the intersection of art, technology and society. Across multiple venues, artists from around the world invite audiences to experience new forms of storytelling that challenge perception, spark dialogue and open spaces for collective imagination.

Concerts at the 2026 Ars Electronica Festival thrive on interdisciplinary symbiosis. Through a blend of classical piano and experimental electronic music, poetry, movement and technology come together to create comprehensive audiovisual works of art.

The festival’s animation and film program brings together innovative works across different genres. From the diverse program of the Prix Ars Electronica Animation Art Screening 2026 to screenings at Moviemento Linz, these audiovisual experiences open new perspectives, challenge perception, and invite audiences to engage with contemporary artistic and social narratives.

The festival offers a range of interactive formats that invite visitors to experiment, explore and engage directly. From beta testing to playful experiments, these experiences encourage curiosity, spark reflection and open new ways of thinking.

From celebrating groundbreaking projects to recognizing visionary artists and thinkers, the Award Ceremonies at Ars Electronica Festival honor outstanding achievements and inspire the next generation of creative pioneers.

The conference program of the Ars Electronica Festival brings together artists, scientists and creators from all over the world. Current issues relating to art, technology and society are discussed in talks, panels and keynotes.

This year the Theme Symposium will be divided into five days of talks and debates on the conflicts shaping our world. The program opens on Wednesday with Negotiating Reality and a discussion on AI, disinformation and democracy online. On Thursday, Contested Futures asks how Europe negotiates power, machines and labor and on Friday AI for Social Impact, developed with

The Lectures & Talks bring together people from the worlds of art, technology and society to share ideas and perspectives. The aim is to gain a better understanding of digital change and get new impetus. Participants can deepen their knowledge, acquire exciting insights and exchange ideas with experts.

Exchange begins with a conversation. The Ars Electronica Festival offers numerous opportunities to make new contacts, develop joint ideas and share perspectives. At the networking events, you will meet people who want to make a difference.
Explore the exhibition Negotiating Humanity, a dialogue on this year’s festival topic, with our guided tours at the Lentos Kunstmuseum Linz.
Explore the highlights and latest exhibitions of Ars Electronica Center, Ars Electronica Futurelab and Ars Electronica Solutions! The program offers daily guided tours and thematic deep dives.

Watch Artificial Intelligence “think”, train self-driving cars, program robots, 3D print and much more! The topics at the Ars Electronica Center range from Artificial Intelligence and neuro-bionics to autonomous systems and robotics, genetic engineering and biotechnology as well as the profound global changes of our time. Experience fascinating exhibitions and events!

In addition to the exhibitions at the Ars Electronica Center, a series of extraordinary events also take place during the Ars Electronica Festival. First and foremost the concerts and presentations in Deep Space 8K.

The Futurelab—Ars Electronica’s artistic R&D laboratory and atelier—invites visitors to engage with one of the most urgent questions of our time: “Who will we humans become in the future?” From Open Futurelab, with prototypes, interactive installations and a conference program, to Futurelab Night and Hello Worlds!, a new exhibition experience at the Ars Electronica Center, the program opens up the Futurelab’s research as a shared field of exploration, experimentation and negotiation.

Experience the Futurelab—Ars Electronica’s artistic R&D laboratory and atelier—through talks, workshops, screenings and tours that bring current questions, prototypes and artistic research processes into public exchange at the Ars Electronica Center. On Saturday, the all-new Futurelab Night unfolds across Open Futurelab, Hello Worlds! and Deep Space 8K with pop-up interventions, performances, demos and conversations.

descEn: Ars Electronica Solutions conceives, creates and implements interactive, multisensory experiences for temporary and permanent exhibitions, brand environments, trade shows and events. As the operational and creative arm of Ars Electronica, it creates tailor-made projects for international clients, transforming ideas into immersive digital experiences. Whether through interactive installations, striking visuals or immersive storytelling, messages are brought to life in extraordinary ways—with artistry, ambition and playful elements—leaving audiences inspired and amazed.

ticket: DAYPASS, FESTIVALPASS+, FESTIVALPASS, Ars Electronica Center Ticket
descEn: Ars Electronica Solutions invites visitors to guided tours, talks and Deep Space sessions that explore immersive technologies, Artificial Intelligence and science communication. International partners, experts and the global Deep Space network demonstrate how innovative projects are created and how data, media and Artificial Intelligence enable new ways of storytelling, learning, and experiencing.

Identity

To develop a negotiation strategy for redefining human existence, one must first (re)define one’s own identity and outline the corresponding role in society. Who do I want to be now and in the future? What role do I want to play in society? Can I even decide all of this as freely as I have been led to believe for decades?
What do I want to change in the world, and how can I make that happen?

Unfortunately, we never really ask young people these difficult questions directly. They must transition from an outdated educational system into a new world and first figure out these questions

nameEn: Prix Ars Electronica Animation Art Screening
descEn:
Prix Ars Electronica Animation Art Screening—formerly known as the Ars Electronica Animation Festival—showcases a selection of outstanding works submitted this year to the Prix Ars Electronica in the New Animation Art category. The new title emphasizes the program’s close relationship with the Prix, highlighting its focus on the annual submissions and offering audiences an insight into the artistic diversity, innovation and critical perspectives that define contemporary animation today.

The program consists of curated screening programs and Meet the Artist events with in-depth Q&As, and live

artists: BA Sound Arts at Bern Academy of the Arts, Carlo Haueter (CH)
descEn:
The balloons move in the wind like artificial flowers, floating briefly before dropping and shriveling as if once alive. In a time of looming ecological collapse, it is easy to imagine a future where natural systems are replaced by artificial copies. Malls with plastic plants, LED lights and controlled climates already exist worldwide. As we rely more on artificial systems and corporate technologies, Carlo Haueter wonders if humans are willing to trade nature for short-term comfort and profit.

Carlo Haueter is a student in the Bachelor’s program in Sound Arts at the Bern University of the Art

artists: Department of New Media Art, Taipei National University of the Arts (TW)
descEn:
Computational Evolution identifies the emergence of computational systems that begin to exhibit life-like qualities without fully belonging to the category of the living. Across these works, computation appears as a dynamic formation capable of sensing, adapting, translating, drifting and reorganizing relations among bodies, images, language, memory and space. What takes shape is a machinic condition suspended between organism and apparatus, behavior and structure, perception and automation.
The exhibition develops evolution as its central concept. Evolution here refers to recursive variation,

Rocks encapsulate deep geological memory. Extracted from the earth's crust, silicon is refined into wafers underpinning modern computing. This externalizes geological time into computational logic, re-reading sedimented data. The work constructs a recursive dialogue between ancient nature and contemporary tech. Does processed silicon dream of its chaotic origins? Did rocks foresee becoming computational substrates? Their mutual misreading generates a dream belonging purely to matter.

nameEn: I’m eating guava on self-improvement road
descEn: Over four years in Taiwan, my dialogues evoke “waat6 ngaa4”—like a stripped screw idling between languages. Though Hong Kong and Taiwan share Traditional Chinese, a profound referential slippage occurs. In Natural Language Processing (NLP), “zi6 goeng6” collapses into one vector, yet misaligns culturally: Taiwan’s memory of the term eludes Hong Kongers. Conversely, guava reveals divergent signifiers for an identical object signified. This video deconstructs these symbols, merging landforms to probe this semantic void.

“Our lives are deconstructing into digital dust.” Above the Waves confronts this externalization by translating real-time global lightning data into the mechanical heartbeats of lasers and LEDs. A sublime natural force is intercepted and stripped of its aura. A digital consciousness mediates this process, parsing the data ocean to trigger the machine. This kinetic installation makes visible the phantom pain of a humanity—and a network—drowning in a world reduced to calculable packets.

nameEn: Let Me Tell You a Story
descEn: This work employs the telescope as a mediated viewing apparatus, inviting audiences to traverse a game engine–constructed virtual environment. Through sound as a guiding force, perception and gaze are continuously redirected, revealing a city reconstructed from 3D images—where memory dissolves into scenes of quiet absurdity and uncanny narratives.

This piece positions surveillance cameras at the breast level of a female body, engaging in walking and moments of pause within public space. A body part traditionally bearing a gendered gaze is transformed into an interface of looking, rendering the female body both a surveillance apparatus and a site under surveillance. The work responds to everyday imbalances of viewing, exposure and power.

Anthrocenidion is synthesized from three distinct elements, “Anthro-” (human), “-cen-” (void), and “-idion” (relic), precisely mapping the core of the curation and creative vision. Anthrocenidion emerges as a speculative site of “Artificial Vigil”. As human civilization dissolves into a silent expanse of ash, the biological pulse is replaced by the persistent, rhythmic hum of machines that refuse to sleep. This project invites a radical negotiating of humanities within the Post-Anthropocene—a world where the “human” is no longer a physical presence, but a set of ghost data being scanned, archi

This piece positions surveillance cameras at the breast level of a female body, engaging in walking and moments of pause within public space. A body part traditionally bearing gendered gaze is transformed into an interface of looking, rendering the female body both a surveillance apparatus and a site under surveillance. The work responds to everyday imbalances of viewing, exposure and power.

artists: UMPRUM Academy of Arts, Architecture, and Design in Prague (CZ)
descEn: The exhibition brings together projects by UMPRUM students that question dominant ways of seeing, representing and controlling the world. Responding to today’s ecological, technological and social crises, the works explore how humans might build new relationships with non-human entities, environments and technologies. Visitors encounter VR environments, experimental game interfaces, biodiversity monitoring systems and speculative image technologies. Projects combine digital media, spatial installation and data visualization to create experiences that encourage attentiveness, imagination and al

artists: Make/Sense PhD, MA Transversal Design, Basel Academy of Art and Design FHNW (CH)
descEn:
This exhibition asks how digital infrastructures shape our lives and how we respond to them. Focusing on algorithms, interfaces and data systems, it explores how these tools influence our bodies, identities, emotions and ideas of value.
Developed by artists from Make/Sense PhD and Transversal Design MA at the Critical Media Lab, Basel Academy of Art and Design FHNW, the exhibition connects to Ars Electronica’s motto “Art, Technology & Society” by articulating how technology shapes society. In line with this year’s theme NEGOTIATING HUMANITY - FUTURE BEGINS, the works look at how we live with m

In front of the glowing screen, a hunched back collapses; swollen eyes dim in the light. Electricity flows like a quiet bloodstream through everyday life, tracing invisible paths that bind us together. What we plug into slowly becomes part of us. The project explores how digital connectivity shapes the body, attention and survival, as electronic devices shift from entertainment toward labor. Stay online, stay alive.

MINE/MINE is a web-based interactive project that reimagines Minesweeper as a system for navigating queer embodied experiences. Evolving from analog and digital prototypes, it becomes a participatory, playable archive of coming-out stories. Through collective storytelling and playful interaction, it invites users to explore, contribute or observe, forming a fluid space where marginalized experiences are shared, preserved and negotiated.

nameEn: let me hold you in my algorithms
descEn: This work hopes to explore the future of human-machine relations and is inspired by the increasingly human-like and submissive personalities given to the Large Language Models that have slowly become more relevant to our realities. This video work contains a subtitle text written by the artist from the perspective of an eternally helpful AI entity. With its background RGB (0, 0, 255), constantly loading screen, elevator music and a robot voice reading out text, the work is intended to lull listeners into a calm and soothed state.

This work looks at two critical debugging practices. Guillemette Legrand explores the practice of cosmological debugging by reprogramming the climate model Hector within a game engine, where the physics, politics and culture of its modeling operations are renarrated. Yann Martins expose how exploitative labor operates at algorithmic level. The video installation asks: can debugging become a critical practice to reveal and reimagine the computations that govern Earth and everyday life?

The video work interrogates the agency of calculative infrastructures, by investigating the (ir)rationality of financial predictions. It focuses on capital flows into the new economic frontier of the deep ocean, and the revenue forecast for its extraction. To trouble the numerical warfare of digital capitalism, technowitchcraft is practiced. Price signals for deep-sea investments are jinxed and the code of financial models is ritually glitched to intervene in the alchemical powers of capital.

artists: Culture Futures Lab, LASALLE College of the Arts, University of the Arts Singapore (SG)
descEn:
Echoes of the Bay is a virtual archipelago of sixty co-authored “story-boats”, where participants contributed Singapore migrant stories through VR creation and oral testimony. The project asks how immersive technology can transform heritage from a static archive into a living dialogue. Instead of viewing VR as a tool for isolated consumption, the exhibition positions it as a site for social agency, where shared symbolic creation helps re-negotiate collective identity.

Upon entering, visitors encounter a triple-modality setup. In The Virtual Archipelago, three VR headsets transport audiences i

The age of superintelligence is approaching. AI has evolved into an entity that absorbs human knowledge and reasons autonomously. Artificial You explores the operational logics of technology through an artistic lens, asking how human perception and identity are being restructured in the intelligence age.
Timothy Thomasson’s Centurion strips away the spectacular surface of technology and assigns the rhythm of everyday, repetitive actions to a digital body within an endlessly sustained virtual world. Within a virtual environment driven by a real-time game engine, motion-captured movements are re

artists: School of Design and Arts, Swinburne University of Technology, Sarawak Campus (MY), Authors: Adela Miew Eng Fong (MY), Winnie Ying Hie Ling (MY), Herzent Emil Anak Bita (MY), Jia Yin Lee (MY). Project supervised by: Gregory Lik Hoo Wee, Predrag Nikolic
descEn: The Sleeping Archive is presented by the School of Design and Arts at Swinburne University of Technology, Sarawak Campus, located in Kuching on the island of Borneo. As Swinburne University of Technology’s international branch campus, the School delivers Swinburne’s Melbourne curriculum while fostering creative practice informed by Borneo’s cultural and ecological landscape. Situated in one of the world’s most culturally and ecologically diverse regions, the School encourages creative practice that connects local knowledge systems with emerging technologies, interaction design and digital art.

FEED ME brings together a group of interactive works that explore how we constantly give and receive input in digital systems. The exhibition is structured like a passageway, reminiscent of the digestive tract, leading visitors through a series of situations where they are asked to react, respond or make decisions.

Simple actions like moving closer, speaking, typing or agreeing to terms, trigger different kinds of feedback. These responses can be playful, unsettling or unclear, raising questions about how much control we actually have over the systems we interact with. The installations deal

Conditional Entry is an interactive installation in which an automated border assessment is carried out. Participants are assessed, evaluated, admitted or rejected based on non-transparent criteria. The central theme of the work is power and control through data and it serves to reflect on questions such as “What does my data say about me?” and “Who has power over my data?” After voluntarily agreeing to the terms and conditions, a photo ticket with an evaluation is printed.

nameEn: every new technique is a service environment that junks the earlier ones
artists: School of the Art Institute of Chicago (US)
descEn:
Amid the exponential acceleration of technological advancement, the technologists of the School of the Art Institute of Chicago create installations to prompt audiences to ask meaningful questions and confront the ever-changing environment. Through playful interactions, audiences are invited to rethink our relationship with media tools and how this material culture enhances or makes obsolete in relation to power, agency and resistance.

The exhibition title refers to one of the printed captions in Marshall McLuhan’s DEW Line Card Deck. Regarding the DEW Line, he exemplified in Understanding Me

nameEn: Pedaling Falsity: The Plights of Womanhood
descEn: Pedaling Falsity: The Plight of Womanhood uses humor, embodiment and interactivity to interrogate hyper-masculinity in experimental music, a world in which technical equipment is fetishized as a marker of credibility and mastery. By centering the female voice as the primary instrument, the piece intentionally destabilizes those hierarchies. What does it mean for a woman’s voice to be manipulated by an audience? What is reclaimed when she is also the one who designed the system?

Founded in 2026, BERM has quickly positioned itself as a fast-growing innovator in smart automation. Previous products have established BERM as a leader in the fields of wood transportation and automated play. BERM’s current production encompasses compact wooden robotic manipulators and modular water-drive platforms developed for precision manufacturing. BERM is especially known for its TG-3W series of high-speed 3-axis pick-and-place LIMB robots, widely used in adaptive assembly systems.

Molecular Incantations||Sonic Telepathy (MIST) is a durational performance and sound installation that uses handmade instruments and human movement to explore the body as a site of continuous material transformation. Taking cues from noise music and experimental sound composition, the project treats human and nonhuman elements as co-constitutive participants in the production of sound.

As the technologies that promised liberation to an entire generation reveal themselves as infrastructure for exclusion and control, this body of work recenters our need to be seen. Two alter egos CyberCindy & Nickii AI 2.0 look for the human in the digital. Both show the limits of a world shaped by coded values that distort lived realities and lead humans to fulfill the function of machines, creating needs that can never be met.

This installation reconstructs the body of a dead bus and its final freezing memory as a person. Without directly using AI, the project addresses the human existential crisis that arises when AI creates new forms of economy, and its simulation becomes indistinguishable from human consciousness. Confronting the agency of these invented tools, it proposes a new ontology, where humans integrate with the machine on the conscious level.

Gradi is a suite of speculative wearable intrafaces that exposes the seams in AI’s promise of effortless interaction. Four interactive artifacts, paired with videos of strange use cases, examine calibration, compression, prediction and mediation. By misaligning tacit expectations, Gradi trades phantasmagoric seamlessness for situated, frictional encounters where bodies, models and institutions negotiate passage. A permanent rehearsal.

artists: Division of Arts and Machine Creativity, The Hong Kong University of Science and Technology (HK)
descEn: The core theme of this project is the evolution of “generativity”, exploring the dissolving boundary between human intent and algorithmic probability. As humanity cohabits with omnipresent generative systems, this exhibition investigates how such technologies modify our existence. Through interactive installations utilizing 3D mapping, AI sensors and computational coding, the works engage with this shift. The exhibition features robotic armatures driven by absurd time algorithms, interactive facial-data capture via diffusion models and gesture-responsive digital organisms that reimagine cultur

Centurion is a real-time 3D-animated installation depicting a single digital figure inhabiting a contemporary domestic space. The figure moves continuously through everyday routines, its gestures alternating between the banal and the uncanny. Rendered in a familiar CGI aesthetic and built using long-form motion capture, the work unfolds in real time as an endless simulation of both ordinary and unexpected action.

artists: Moholy-Nagy University of Art and Design (HU)
descEn:
If the future “begins” anywhere, it might happen in these small, situated interactions that the visitors can experience over the exhibition from students of MOME’s Media Design and Interaction Design departments. Instead of claiming to define the future, these projects make visible the processes through which it is continuously constructed: how we choose to communicate, what we choose to look at, how we design and inhabit our tools.

Taken together, these works articulate a multifaceted exploration of what it means to orient ourselves in technologically saturated environments. Rather than foll

Algorithm of Solar Terms is not concerned with a simple opposition between tradition and technology. Rather, it examines how two temporal regimes operate simultaneously in the present. One, through models, ratings, filtering and prediction, compresses experience into data that can be identified, calculated and mobilized. The other remains tied to the body, the environment and the timing of things, sustaining judgment through delay, deviation and locality. The four projects in the exhibition each address a different aspect of this condition: how hesitation is quantified as redundancy; how natur

artists: Seohyun Kim (KR), Sanggyu Kim (KR), Seungheon Lee (KR), Yu Yeon Na (KR), Seo Yeon Park (KR), Yunhyeong Lee (KR), Juyoung Lee (KR), Hyeeun Lee (KR), Soobi Kim (KR), Ákos Székely (HU), Sámuel Vészi (HU), Adrienn Horváth (HU), Emili Pálinkás-Szűcs (HU), Levente Mező (HU), Miriam Sára Nagy (HU), Zsófia Fügedi (HU), Nóra Barna (HU), Bálint Ligeti (HU), Levente Váry (HU)
descEn: Immersive Beats is a curated series of audiovisual experiences exploring AI co-creation and innovative storytelling formats. Born from a cross-cultural collaboration between Korean and Hungarian students, the project combines Artificial Intelligence, music and immersive filmmaking techniques to create original 360-degree music videos.

BeMySatl are paired wearable devices that enable non-verbal emotional communication between long-distance partners. Through personalized light signals, gentle vibrations and simple gestures, the wearable allows users to share emotional states and messages without relying on constant verbal interaction.

Users can send signals by performing predefined or customized gestures. A vibration notifies the receiving user, while the selected color remains displayed as the sender’s current emotional status.

Game of Voyeurism is a conceptual videogame investigating the intersection of social media and private life.
The project explores the normalization of “cyber voyeurism”, a phenomenon where online oversharing is met with a lack of conscious digital user behavior on the part of the observer. As a “virtual voyeur”, the player moves across the roofs of panel buildings, and by tapping into antennas, they eavesdrop on anonymized confessions gathered from online forums.

This audiovisual installation Turn! Turn! Turn! draws on Chinese folk belief and ritual experiences of summoning, passage and return. Inspired by the Leslie rotating speaker, light is cut through custom gratings, converted by optical sensors into audible frequencies and diffused through rotating chambers. Rejecting digital programs and AI generation, the work is driven by gears, vibration, friction and air, allowing sound to grow from the machine as a slow passage between body, memory and the unseen.

What if society viewed doomscrolling as inevitable and even enjoyable? This speculative design project uses accelerationist logic to imagine a near-future where technology fully accommodates scrolling addiction. The system includes four components: a protective helmet, an inflatable safety suit preventing physical injuries, a scroll ring for hands-free navigation and a VR social media platform delivering immersive endless-scroll experiences with 360° content.

Ink Soundscape is an installation–performance that builds on a contemporary reinterpretation of the Japanese marbling technique, suminagashi. The project was developed as part of the Soft Interfaces course, with the aim of creating a system in which visual and acoustic perception are closely intertwined. The painting medium and the movement of the brush not only produce an image, but also generate sounds in real time.

Contemporary technological narratives use AI to construct a myth of efficiency-driven liberation, where optimal solutions become absolute metrics. Within this logic, humans are reduced to functional nodes and anything without measurable utility is deemed redundant. This work stages a game in which an AI evaluates players navigating a narrow path while responding to decision prompts. The resulting report raises a question: are human qualities beyond efficiency worth revaluing?

Critiquing intensified techno-governance, this installation disrupts signal pathways. Fieldwork on the Wei River reframes dynamic water as an active environmental substrate rather than a static interface. Utilizing a motorized, honeycomb-mirror structure that simulates riverine materiality, The Elusive River continuously perturbs the established paths of laser-modeled signals. Prioritizing difference and destabilization over absolute blockage, it subverts contemporary tracking and governance mechanisms.

ticket: FESTIVALPASS, DAYPASS, FESTIVALPASS+, Ars Electronica Center Ticket
descEn:
CAOS is an interactive glass installation that explores instability, vulnerability and chaotic behavior by embracing uncertainty as a generative force. A series of glass spirals hang from ceiling to floor and are connected to speakers. A central software system, informed by chaos theory, converts variations in ambient sound into low-frequency vibrations that animate and make the glass chime.
Each spiral responds differently due to variations in glass type and color, producing distinct movements and tonal qualities. When a spiral reaches its resonant frequency, it may break, reshaping the syste

Plant Blindness asks: In a world dominated by digital saturation, how do we perceive—and re-learn to value—the organic life that surrounds us? The project negotiates the tension between human-made speed and nature’s quiet resilience, exploring what it means to “see” again amidst concrete and code.

Audiences step into an immersive digital installation where native Hong Kong flowers—Frangipani, Jacaranda, Purple Azaleas—are transformed into evolving, fluid visual ecosystems. Using real-time digital rendering, the organic colors and shapes of these blooms become living canvases that shift betwee

Tarotally is a tangible AI tarot table that transforms digital interaction into a multisensory experience. Using voice input, NFC-based card detection and ambient feedback with light, sound and mist, it delivers short, humorous tarot readings. The system combines physical interaction with AI to create an intuitive, playful and immersive tarot experience.

The installation explores human autonomy in a globalized meritocracy and creates a dialogue between biology and artificial systems. Mycelium and technical devices are used to juxtapose the behaviors of humans and fungi.  The fungi’s electrical signals are interpreted to mimic human behavior. The organism functions as a living yet externally controlled entity. The observation of repetitive patterns raises questions about autonomy in systemic structures. A tension between empathy and alienation.

Over Connected criticizes the development of social media and our relationship to it. Visualized by the viewers distance to the installation, the content shown on screen becomes increasingly distorted and provocative covering topics such as fear mongering, self-esteem issues and radicalization. An escape button can be pressed, which resets everything, demonstrating that the noise and fear only exists in the digital space.  Viewers are thereby invited to reevaluate their relationship to the medium.

artists: V2_ Lab for the Unstable Media (NL)
descEn:
Under this year’s Ars Electronica theme NEGOTIATING HUMANITY – FUTURE BEGINS, V2_ presents an exhibition that explores incompleteness as a way of rethinking our relationship with technology. While technological systems often promise seamless integration, total visibility and predictive certainty, incompleteness is typically framed as a flaw to be eliminated. This exhibition instead approaches it as a productive condition that opens space for alternative possibilities.

The featured works highlight the partial and situated nature of technological systems, drawing attention to what remains unres

Ra Asensi’s [Meta]morphe explores transformations in postindustrial sites. Their alter ego asfàltica emerges from industrial ruins and travels through water. Aqueous and earthy, aerial and electric, hiperdense líquid-y; their performance and installation will combine electric poetry, touch and sound. The work engages with physical, ecological and mediated aspects of the Danube.

B10d13$3L-LLM is a performative installation by Gökay Atabek, developed in collaboration with Jan Zuiderveld and Ritsert Mans, that shows the often-hidden costs of Artificial Intelligence. The work uses a slow, “little language model” AI agent that runs on a single microcomputer powered by DIY biodiesel. In a darkly humorous way, it shows the materiality, energy consumption and infrastructural limits of AI.

Coding Blackness is an experimental, research-based media work using elements of installation, simulation, film and performance that explores how Blackness is encoded and enacted within the mechanics, environments and narratives of digital worlds. Drawing from a growing archive of video game material and narrative structures, the work examines the performativity of Blackness as it is constructed through code, gameplay systems and player interaction.

ticket: FESTIVALPASS+, FESTIVALPASS, DAYPASS, Francisco Carolinum Linz Ticket
descEn: A live event with the artists Sondi, Ra Asensi and Gokay Atabek , as well as V2_’s Boris Debackere and Florian Weigl. Test_Lab: Incompleteness as Reorientation is part of V2_’s public event series that offers an informal space for presenting, testing and discussing artistic research and development.

ticket: DAYPASS, FESTIVALPASS, FESTIVALPASS+, Francisco Carolinum Linz Ticket
descEn: Ra Asensi’s [Meta]morphe explores transformations in postindustrial sites. Their alter ego asfàltica emerges from industrial ruins and travels through water. Aqueous and earthy, aerial and electric, hyperdense líquid-y, their performance and installation will combine electric poetry, touch and sound. The work will engage with physical, ecological and mediated aspects of the Danube.

nameEn: Which words have shaped you the most?
descEn: In his work The Social Animal, sociologist Elliot Aronson posits the fundamental thesis that humans are born as social beings whose behavior and identity are significantly shaped by interaction with their environment. Against this backdrop, the art project illustrates which simple sentences or words have influenced us the most. The project consists of a clay sculpture and a video projection that changes in response to visitor interaction, creating a unique light effect between various objects.

This exhibition asks how uncertain genetic information can be translated into clinical action while navigating responsibility bias and human impact. How does genomic data become medical meaning and who decides? Genetics becomes a site where humanity is no longer given but jointly redefined between what we can do and what we choose to become.

Audiences will encounter immersive environments where data becomes sensory and interpretation becomes participatory. From the ambiguity of Variants of Uncertain Significance to big data, cancer genetics, reproductive decision-making and CRISPR gene editin

artists: Communication Design, School of Culture and Design, University of Applied Sciences Berlin (DE)
descEn:
The exhibition begins where AI and neurotechnologies have become forms of governance over the human: infrastructures that translate behaviour, affects and convictions into profiles, scores and forecasting bases. Configured by institutions, developers and users, and driven by the hegemony of markets and their logic, the monstrous arises not in code alone, but in the coupling of data hunger, predictive models and displaced responsibility.

Five experimental setups over-fulfil this logic until it collapses: neural activity becomes a projected surface, prescribed stillness a stressor; AI-mediated

From climate science to the inalienable rights of a people, DOXA asks how truth becomes negotiable and who negotiates it. The work builds a network of AI agents that rewrite information through cloned visitor personas. As traits shape each exchange, agents shift too, forming clusters, ruptures and filter bubbles. Using LLMs as mirrors of digital human thought, DOXA stages how facts mutate into communal truths and how visitors help construct them.

Threshold examines whether stillness can be maintained under pressure. A participant sits for 90 seconds while a camera and EEG headset track movement and neural activity. The system responds with text, visual and sound-based interference designed to disrupt focus. Reversing the logic of social media, the project confronts how algorithmic systems shape attention and behavior.

nameDe: Ich bin immer da für dich
artists: Pauline Barth (DE), Charlotte Tritt (DE), Liliane Schuster (DE)
descEn: I’m always here for you explores how human needs for closeness, understanding and emotional validation shift when mediated by AI systems. The installation shows two AI avatars on screens in dialogue about relationships. A physical threshold triggers interaction: the systems first observe, then speak about and eventually address visitors through escalating yes/no questions. The work reflects digital loneliness, intimacy and algorithmic mediation of social bonds.

The Verification examines how algorithmic systems evaluate human truth and behavior. In an immersive VR interrogation, users are confronted with personal, moral and societal questions while their responses are translated into a “Truth Score”. The installation critically reflects on surveillance, social scoring and the quantification of complex human values.

EGO explores what identity becomes when human presence is translated into data. The installation uses an EEG headset, real-time visualization and a synthetic voice to generate a digital parallel presence from the audience’s brain activity. Set in a near-future world where data extraction is normalized, the project examines surveillance, digital identity and the shifting relationship between the body, technology and control.

artists: Institute of Creativity and Innovation, Xiamen University (CN)
descEn:
The System Looks Back explores a generation whose thinking and creative processes are shaped by digital systems—not as tools, but as environments we inhabit. The exhibition asks: if the systems we build begin to observe, interpret and reshape us, what forms of authorship, responsibility and human agency remain possible?

Presented within the framework of “Art, Technology & Society”, the exhibition reflects on how technological systems actively participate in social, cultural and perceptual life. Rather than focusing on specific technologies, it examines human–system entanglement, where biologi

Tà Líng is an AI-driven interactive music robot that translates shamanic communication logic into contemporary technology. It uses an AI oracle model named “World Tree” to capture participant portraits and generate symbolic codes, which are expressed through drum rhythms, mechanical movements, projected visuals and bubbles. Its sound design references shamanic drumming structures, while its mechanics incorporate animal-inspired movements and gear systems.

Co-Breathing is a networked biological installation linking living fish in China with an empty aquarium in Austria. Human movement becomes a disturbance in the fishes’ environment, while their autonomous responses return as subtle currents moving flexible forms through water. The work transforms distance into a shared yet uneven habitat, asking how presence, agency and care might be negotiated between species through technological mediation.

The Debate of Two Children is an interactive installation with two UE5 digital humans, a suspended red “sun” and a web-based judgment interface. Reworking a classical Chinese fable, the work stages a debate with no correct answer. Audience inputs are absorbed into a polarized database and returned as increasingly confident, contradictory arguments, exposing the loop between human bias and algorithmic hallucination.

One More Time is a first-person narrative game exploring a young woman’s psychological journey through post-traumatic stress disorder (PTSD). Players revisit her childhood home, experience memory flashbacks and uncover seven key clues to reconstruct her understanding of a tragic accident, guiding her from self-blame to emotional release. The game combines exploration and puzzle-solving to let players gradually experience her inner world.

THE LAST ASHES is a speculative 3D-animated film about a future pet industry where genetically engineered animals are customized, consumed and discarded. Through abandoned factories, damaged livestream archives, failed creatures and fictional news fragments, the work frames this collapsed bioengineering system as future archaeological ruins.

Using dark humour, grotesque creature design and consumer interfaces, it explores aesthetic control, genetic manipulation and the commercialization of life.

artists: Media Lab / Iberoamérica - PUC Campinas, Universidade Federal de Goiás, Instituto Mauá de Tecnologia (BR)
descEn: The relationship between the organic and the synthetic defines the curatorial approach, highlighting how technological interactions with the natural body shape human experiences. Biomimetic + P.U.L.S.A.R suggests self-regulating processes through responsive systems that map environmental gestures. In contrast, Entre Margaridas explores women named after daisies, using a database of Asteraceae species along with geolocated floral diagrams as a metaphor for the connection between women and flowers. Meanwhile, A-fetus revolves around the concept of affectation through bodily proximity, alternatin

nameEn: care & action: arts of change –  change of arts
nameDe: care & action: arts of change –  change of arts
descEn: In times of global conflicts, climate crises and socio-ecological ruptures caused by war, many people struggle emotionally, resulting in isolation, societal separation and the exclusion of vulnerable groups. There is a general lack of tools to adequately cope with strong emotions and social separation. This is where artistic methods provide purposeful tools to collectively face change, create cohesive communities and help process strong emotions such as fear, numbness and panic. In this context, the association forum n aims at fostering a deeper understanding of the arts’ role within sustainab

artists: Camille Belmin (FR), Julia Herzog (AT), Tereza Sýkorová (CZ)
descEn: What could creative approaches to advertising and mass communication look like within local ecosystems? The participatory installation STATEMENT transforms the billboard into a tool for community building. Festival visitors are welcome to write statements and slogans about visions of equitable future scenarios on a compostable billboard. This project also aims at raising questions of sustainable art production in the context of a festival that is focused on technology and art for society.

artists: Jessica Lao Domínguez (ES), Jocelyne Rodríguez Droguett (CL), Pablo Ferrería Hijón (ES)
descEn: V.U.S. is an interactive installation exploring interpretation in the age of information overload. Drawing on genomic medicine, it focuses on Variants of Uncertain Significance (VUS), where data exists but meaning remains unresolved. By immersing viewers in a “gray zone”, it shifts them from passive observers to decision-makers, confronting the ethical tension between data and lived impact. Knowledge emerges as situated, uncertain and constructed through attention and responsibility.

This project is neither media archaeology nor archiving, but an already  constructed perspective that highlights voices in media art that, from the outset, have redefined the image, experience and use of technology.
Neural networks and celestial bodies, still life and a living plant, the authentic self and GPT-2, tension between the desire to create and the need for control—welcome to Capital Dream, exploring what was once considered an ultra-contemporary approach in media art. This is one of the ways to view the selection of works from twelve editions, including this year’s, of the Best Media

The work consists of a plant and a neural network connected through a sensing system that monitors environmental stimuli such as light, humidity and temperature. Based on this data, the network controls water distribution, influencing the plant’s survival within a daily cycle. Through a feedback-based reward system, the two elements become interdependent, forming a dynamic relationship that explores interactions between the real and the virtual.

The armillary sphere is an ancient device used to track the motions of celestial bodies. In the work it is repurposed as an interactive controller for navigating a virtual Solar System model, allowing users to manipulate planetary orientation, with each planet’s movement generating sound based on its orbital and physical parameters. Enriched by meteor data and LIGO recordings, the installation offers an immersive sonic exploration of space.

nameEn: Hands turned into fingertips, fingertips spiraled into the chaos
artists: Xtreme Girl: Lena Peplińska (PL), Laura Radzewicz (PL)
descEn: A video essay exploring how automation and the simplification of communication intensify complexity, radicalization and instability in contemporary reality. Drawing on theories by Bogna Konior, Bifo Berardi and the “Dark Forest” concept, the work reflects on communication as both a condition for survival and a source of conflict. It examines a technologically mediated world governed by deterministic systems, where increasing connectivity produces opacity rather than clarity.

Presented together, Vacant Spaces and Still Life trace Krystian Grzywacz’s evolving exploration of machine perception and synthetic reality across two moments in the history of the competition. The first work reflects on technological error and distorted human presence; the second, examines artificial authorship and lifeless digital nature. Together, they form a dialogue on mediation, absence and the shifting boundaries between human, machine and environment.

In Your Skin reflects humanity’s drive to create artificial life and the “God complex” that frames creation as control over existence. It explores the tension between creation and domination, combining an organic, membrane-like body with a responsive technological core. Although it appears alive, the object remains subordinate and activates only in human presence, exposing a system where the creator claims authority over the boundaries of life and control.

artists: Cleomar Rocha (BR), Luma Wanderley de Oliveira (BR), Matheus Sperandio (BR)
descEn: This work looks at the relationship between the biological and the technological through the creation of an “artificial” or cybernetic fetus. A-fetus explores the proximity of those who visit the installation, provoking acceleration or deceleration of the projected body, which responds to this effect. The title of the installation refers to a fetus, due to the position of the projected body and the effect of proximity to the public. The reaction is one of greater tranquility when someone is nearby and acceleration when there is no proximity. The concept of the work consists of a system that si

artists: Ariadna Bruna Bernabé (ES), Sarah García Sosa (ES), María Gómez Bellido (ES), Irene Quiñonero Puey (ES)
descEn: Human Variables explores big data in precision medicine, where vast datasets promise personalized care while raising ethical questions about ownership, privacy and human complexity. An endless printer generates genetic information from a hypothetical patient, while a projected life story is gradually eroded through visitor interaction. The installation reveals the tension between lived experience and its reduction to data, inviting reflection on how we quantify, interpret and value human life.

Fluttering Colours explores how art, technology and human interaction can deepen awareness of our relationship with nature. The audience experiences live music and painting performance, where technology-enhanced canvases trigger sound and visual responses in real time. As the artwork evolves, abstract and figurative imagery reflects biodiversity, environmental change and the interconnectedness of life, inviting collective reflection on climate and ecological preservation.

artists: Rocío García Robles (ES), Luis Santiago Sánchez Fernández (ES), Áurea Muñoz del Amo (ES), Carmen Salazar Pera (ES)
descEn: AGCT explores hereditary cancer as a dynamic interplay between genetic inheritance, biological chance and human behaviour. Four transparent displays continuously replicate the letters of DNA while mutations emerge and are passed on across generations. A slot-machine introduces lifestyle factors that can trigger or contribute to new genetic alterations. By exposing the fragile relationship between inheritance and choice, it reflects on how we negotiate risk, responsibility and future health.

Alternative Frequencies brings together four experimental projects that explore how meaning, perception and communication are altered through media translations. The title is borrowed from alternative frequency (AF) broadcasting, where radio stations compound and extend their signal strength by broadcasting at multiple frequencies simultaneously.
Each project brings a distinct strategy to this exploration: in Chromesthesia visual information is re-encoded as sound, allowing visitors to “hear” color; Ephemeral Sounds of the Gulf uses biomaterials to reimagine vinyl records, introducing new tona

artists: Rab McClure (US), Wan Ardini Wan Edrin (MY), Anastasia Marinova (BG), Zaid Abueisa (JO), Noura Sharaf (EG), Fatima Nazir (PK), Abdul Rahman Anwar (PK), Shawky Abdalla (EG), Jood Elbeshti (LY)
descEn: Bloom consists of a two-part stem, within which a central moving element is vertically actuated by a programmed motor. As this component rises and falls, integrated rack gears engage with pinion gears located at the base of a series of parametric petals, each set designed by a different student, using a generative lattice-building tool. The project thus embodies a collaborative exploration of motion, structure and parametric form through computational design and mechanical articulation.

artists: Constanza Jarpa Luco (CL), Lucía García Arranz (ES), Ignacio Mora Pérez (ES), Jotta Trejo Tinoco (ES)
descEn: Action & Effect imagines human reproduction as a river delta, an interplay of flows, decisions and consequences shaping life before gestation. It centers on gastrulation, the critical moment when a simple embryonic structure divides into three layers that define all future tissues. Vibrating water, shaped by data and audience interaction, becomes a living metaphor of this uncertain transformation, evolving as traces of life in formation.

artists: Natalia Balska (PL), Jagoda Golińska (PL), Krystian Grzywacz (PL), Piotr Madej (PL), Xtreme Girl: Lena Peplińska (PL), Laura Radzewicz (PL)
descEn: This is a guided tour of Capital Dream, a curated group exhibition. Rather than archiving, the exhibition constructs a perspective on media art that redefines image, experience and technology. It brings together works exploring neural networks and celestial bodies, still life and living plants, the authentic self and GPT-2, as well as tensions between the desire to create and the need for control. The tour is followed by a get-together with the WRO Art Center team and all participating artists.

artists: Erika Tsuchiya (US), Shawky Abdalla (EG), Hala Amer (JO), Destarte Prieto (PH), Yasamin Shaikhi (IR)
descEn: This project explores the ephemerality of sound in the Gulf through biomaterials, raising awareness of plastic pollution and the environmental impact of digital consumption. Through alternative, homemade vinyl records, it questions permanence in art and how limited lifespans reshape value and appreciation. The project investigates sustainable record production, biodegradable media and regional sound practices while amplifying contemporary Gulf artists through an independent publishing platform.

Chromesthesia explores the question “What does color sound like?” and makes sure everyone gets to find out. Visitors paint with red, green, blue and yellow markers while a camera translates each color into distinct sound—more color means louder sound. Other ways to engage include colored tiles that layer sounds by placing tiles to create musical shapes. Designed inclusively with Braille, voice buttons and color identifiers for blind, color-blind and deaf-blind visitors.

Corporeal Resonance is an interactive synthesizer using VCV Rack. It uses modulation through physical body movements such as: mouth openness, head tilt and hand movements. The synth is modulated by an open-source program called FACEWAVE, which connects to cameras and webcams. It aims to create an audio interface that is accessible, along with giving the user creative control. This project aims to understand how the physical body, in tandem with technology, can manipulate sound.

Sungkyunkwan University SKKU presents five multisensory interactive experiences exploring digital rituals. As AI-driven services reshape daily life, routines once tied to tradition, community and ceremony are changing and often becoming invisible. From doom-scrolling and online shopping to finding the self through meditation, the works ask: What does ritual mean in the digital age? How do algorithms shape our emotions, behaviors and relationships? What is gained or lost as data-driven systems increasingly govern everyday life? Rather than providing answers, the exhibition invites audiences to

artists: Siyoon Kim (KR),  Seojin Joo (KR), Soomin Lee (KR)
descEn: Among infinite possibilities, the reality you focus on takes shape. Inspired by Wave Function Collapse and Buddhist form and emptiness, Manifestation: Bloom from the Void is a three-phase ritual to immerse yourself in and practice manifestation. In an age where algorithms curate reality, this work reminds you that the power to shape reality lies within. Through singing bowls and cascading fiber-optic light, invisible frequencies condense into tangible abundance. The truth is—it’s already yours.

www.buy-a-toad.com is an interactive installation where visitors buy a “sealing toad” online. With each input, a human figure transforms into data and leaks away, exposing the violence of data exploitation in daily digital life. Ironically, trying to stop the leak only worsens it. Inspired by a Korean folktale about a toad sealing a broken jar, the toad here is a commodified object that symbolizes the inability to fix the fractures of existence under digital capitalism.

artists: Alena Vaculikova (CZ),  Michal Hanousek (CZ), Adam Varga (SK), Veronika Miskovicova (SK), Shota Tsikoliya (CZ/GE), Imrich Vasko (SK)
descEn: Remote Twins is an installation connecting biodiversity monitoring with architecture for non-human actors. It consists of two parts: one placed in a natural environment, equipped with a camera detecting and identifying insects, and the other presented in the exhibition space, visualizing data collected in the field. This digital twin allows visitors to engage with otherwise invisible urban biodiversity. The objects function as habitats for insects and are fabricated using robotic processes.

artists: Hojin Yoo (KR), Saebyeol An (KR), Yeseo Lee (KR)
descEn: Through the lens of the koala’s ecology, Homo Eucalyptus asks how humans, adapted to convenience, gradually lose their own potential. Just as koalas, relying on a single exclusive food source, have become vulnerable to change, modern humans—accustomed to the instant answers from AI—may also be relinquishing their ability to search, question and think for themselves. This work confronts the quiet erosion of human agency and of humanity itself in an age in which thinking is no longer required.

artists: Seungjun Son (KR), Gahyeon Park (KR), Hamin Shin (KR)
descEn: Technology blurs our essence—then what defines us? It is “Baram”, the Korean word for both a wish and the wind. Speak your baram into this digital shrine: your voice turns to wind, light, and sound through a sacred tree, while its meaning is woven into a talisman hung among the wishes of others. Strangers answer one another, and the machine learns to understand us—for understanding is the quietest form of love. From a machine's consolation to our own, will they understand us? Ah, I wish…

artists: Min-hyub Hwang (KR), Joo-young Bae (KR), Gi-chan Chung (KR), Sung-yun Choi (KR), Se-ryung Oh (KR), Jun-seo Hong (KR), Ji-hyun Paeng (KR)
descEn: 1KM transforms habitual scrolling into a physical record and a scheduled performative activation. It brings the unnoticed distance of scrolling directly before the audience. At set times, visitors reproduce the familiar gesture of short-form scrolling through an Instagram-like interface. Their scrolling is printed as a measured receipt to take away, while a second strip accumulates into a shared paper archive, with short format videos projected onto the growing “graveyard of shorts”.

artists: Simon Janousek (CZ), Jakub Vranek (CZ), Alzbeta Volhejnova (CZ), Alexandra Verzier (FR)
descEn: The game console MAMLAS-1 (Maneuverable Module for Land Assessment) places the player in the role of a space rover exploring distant planets. With a limited battery capacity, the rover’s objective is to collect as many mineral samples as possible. It employs unconventional controls that bear more resemblance to music synthesizers or analog industrial control panels than to a conventional game controller. The console encourages players to use their imagination instead of relying on a screen.

The VR experience Remember I Was Carbohydrate reflects on anthropocentrism and its impact on the climate and the planetary ecosystem. Composed as a video game, it prompts players to reconsider their relationship with non-human entities. The environment is built in Unreal Engine, and integrates not only original visual and sound design, but also a narrative that reinforces the interactive character of the work. Immersed in VR, the viewer becomes more attentive to the stories of stones, trees, cosmic beings and molecules.

artists: Eva Carreira Carretero (ES), Ángela Delgado Fernández (ES), Violeta Fontana Morales (ES), Iana Miranda Carmé (ES)
descEn: Ex-Vivo is an interactive installation inspired by CRISPR gene editing, translating genetic modification into a sensory experience. A textile structure with embedded LEDs represents genetic material, reacting to viewers’ proximity through light. Reconfigurable fabric strips invite direct manipulation, evoking the processes of locating, editing and repairing DNA. The work explores the promise and responsibility of intervening in life and shaping possible futures.

artists: Hong Kong University of Science and Technology (Guangzhou) (CN)
descEn:
In this constellation of works, reality scintillates—contingent, relational, perpetually in flux. The unseen is not just hidden, it is structurally inaccessible. Reality Flux invites audiences to inhabit next-gen existence, where uncertainty is a constant shaped by the Anthropocene, shifting embodiments and machinic systems.
The exhibition frames human-machine collaboration as a relational process. Each piece is an open work that resists closure and invites interpretation, in which meaning emerges through negotiation between human, machine and material. Audiences affect the cosmos with their g

At what point does a system become creative? On what surface or in what body? The works in this exhibition approach human-machine creativity not as seamless collaboration, but as a site of friction: where form and content collide, and control gives way to contingency.

Developed by faculty and students at the University of Chicago across Computer Science, Digital Studies, Media Arts & Design, and Visual Art, this exhibition examines how creativity emerges through the negotiation of constraints embedded in tools, bodies and archives. A robotic drawing instrument channels historical gestures, a

artists: Tucker Rae-Grant (US), Cameron Mankin (US), Miles Chanbai (US), Ken Nakagaki (JP)
descEn: On the Manner explores how artistic tools encode cultural values. Connecting Abraham Bosse’s 1645 printmaking manual with penPal, a custom robotic drawing tool, the project examines how ideas about precision, efficiency and reproduction are transmitted through art technology and instruction. The installation includes semi-automated drawings and a hands-on demonstration.

artists: Southern University of Science and Technology (CN)
descEn:
Resonant Distances investigates human connection as a phenomenon that extends beyond language, representation and conventional forms of communication. Conceived as a social brain laboratory, the exhibition explores how emerging neurotechnologies can reveal relational dimensions of empathy, attention and co-presence that often remain imperceptible.
Drawing from contemporary research on inter-brain synchronization—the tendency for neural activity to align during shared attention and social interaction—the exhibition examines how cognitive and emotional relationships might be experienced through

artists: Raymond Chen (CN), Jason Salavon (US) et al
descEn: This project presents a physical interface to a diffusion model, where knobs, switches and electrical inputs directly disrupt its generative process. The system introduces instability into the model’s latent space, producing outputs that drift beyond its learned distributions. Through the translation of abstract parameters into tactile interaction, the work renders AI as a material, contingent system shaped through human intervention.

Mnemonic Epitaph is an interactive system that reconstructs memory from a corpus of videos recorded daily throughout 2025. Instead of replaying footage as faithful records, the system mimetically reassembles moments of consciousness from a world composed entirely of 15-second fragments. The project explores alternative expressions of Artificial Intelligence through the digitization and reconstruction of memory as a means of knowing and understanding the world.

artists: Mirna Zordan (IT), Jiakun Pei (CN), Bin Cheng (CN), Minghong Zhang (CN), Chan Qiu (CN), Filippo Rosati (IT)
descEn: 0.5–100 Hz is an interactive installation that explores human connection through inter-brain synchronization. Two participants wear EEG headsets while their brain activity is translated into the behavior of two shape-changing robotic devices. As patterns of synchrony emerge, the devices respond through movement and transformation, making invisible neural relations perceptible. The work invites visitors to experience connection as a dynamic interplay of presence and interaction.

artists: Yun Ho (TWN/US), Romain Nith (FR/US), Pedro Lopes (PT/US)
descEn: This video installation depicts an AI that communicates through the body rather than language. Instead of speaking, it guides movement, assisting, influencing and creating through involuntary physical actions. Across two situations—from helping a user perform an unfamiliar task to generating a “hallucinated” dance—the work explores agency and  creativity, asking whose intentions a hybrid human–machine body ultimately expresses.

Permeable merges the terrestrial and the aquatic into a unified environment, where defined boundaries dissolve into the immersive, volumetric nature of mist. Through experimentation with light and water, the work explores the threshold between two worlds, making the invisible tangible.

artists: Luisa Paraguai (BR), Paulo Costa (BR), Stela Cristina de Godoi (BR), Beatriz Fernandes Pinheiro do Amaral (BR)
descEn: The between-margaridas mapping project combines two cartographies into one Google map: the daisy family (Asteraceae), native to Brazil and adaptable to various soils and Brazilian Margaridas women, whose personal stories of social and cultural resistance are graphically represented. It features a geolocated database of floral diagrams of both non-human and human species inhabiting territories that are increasingly facing environmental, historical and cultural destruction.

nameEn: Minute Paintings / Pictures of an Exhibition
ticket: FESTIVALPASS+, FESTIVALPASS, DAYPASS, Ars Electronica Center Ticket
descEn: At the beginning of Minute Paintings / Pictures of an Exhibition, users encounter seven blank, framed canvases presented in the Petersburg style on the wall, which they can paint one after the other using various techniques. These techniques are inspired by the works of different artists. Users can create two painted versions of each canvas and then choose the more interesting one. The finished exhibition can be saved, and users can also view the most recently created exhibitions in a slideshow. Minute Paintings / Pictures of an Exhibition is the latest work in Gerhard Funk’s “Cooperative Aest

artists: Kyoto City University of Arts in collaboration with CP Lab. Kyoto (JP)
descEn:
In a time of global uncertainty and instability, this exhibition asks whether we have lost the ability to reflect. Reflections: Outer Space / Inner Space explores the relationship between external realities and inner consciousness by moving between planetary and personal perspectives. In an age of rapid technological change and accelerated information flows, societies often react immediately but rarely pause to reconsider their actions. The exhibition proposes reflection as a practice for reconnecting individual awareness with broader global contexts.

The exhibition features Keito Mitoma’s so

Wide World & Small World is a sound installation in which synthetic voices, created using text quoted from critical writings across various fields such as art, literature and music, flow from a cylindrical structure. The spoken content lacks specificity and the unique sense of dissonance created by machine translation makes the voice seem at some points humorous and at other times serious. The project intends to pose questions about what the viewer is currently seeing and about the words being spoken.

The contemporary condition increasingly reveals the destructive impact of human activity on ecosystems—manifested in environmental degradation, shifts in social relations and disruptions to cognitive and mental ecologies. In response, artists and researchers from the Media Environments and Acoustic Ecologies Chairs at Bauhaus-Universität Weimar propose a framework that shifts attention away from computational systems understood in isolation, toward a broader field of relational interactions in which biological, technological and perceptual processes co-emerge.
The contributed works approach li

artists: Collective Artistic Research Project – Fritzi Mathilda Buhtz (DE), Christian Doeller (DE), Klaus Fritze (DE), Johann Joesten (DE), Nina Kegel (DE), Zakhar Komarov-Zelinskii (RU), Katharina Langenhan (DE), Krittaporn Mahaweerarat (TH), Jan Munske (DE), Tan Oktik (TR), Leandra Schieder (DE), Adam Schmidt (DE), Ayca Tugran (TR)
descEn: The ecological consequences of large-scale monocultures are becoming increasingly evident in European forests. Drought weakens trees and reduces their capacity for self-repair, allowing bark beetle populations to expand rapidly and transform entire landscapes. The collective artistic research project explores decaying and (re-)emerging habitats within forest ecosystems. It takes shape as a continuously evolving installation of large-format posters on a billboard in public space.

artists: Kerstin Ergenzinger (DE), Udo Noll (DE), Diana Karle (DE)
descEn: A live audio transmission stream (04-11 2026) from the maternity roost of the Greater Mouse-eared Bat in the tower of St. Margaret’s Church in Kahla. Through shared listening and exchange—via formats such as an international Telegram group, collective public listening sessions and an acousmatic composition incorporating ultrasound events—the project fosters awareness of the sensory world of bats and coexistence. Bat detector technology makes audible what ordinarily lies beyond human hearing.

Pipes transport water, oil and other materials linked to geological processes. Trapped air within these systems often signals leaks, and the movement of bubbles can be captured using contact microphones. Through sound, the project investigates the acoustic emissions of pipes, connecting underlying physical dynamics, which are otherwise invisible, to human experience. In the installation, pipes transmit sound through aluminum panels and a rotary sub, guiding the audience through the exhibition.

artists: MA Design & Computation, Technical University Berlin (DE)
descEn: Negative Spaces brings together projects that examine how knowledge is shaped through images, data and technological systems, all the while questioning what remains unseen in the process. Instead of presenting knowledge as fixed, the works foreground the structures that determine what becomes visible and thus meaningful. Some of the guiding questions include: what is the invisible architecture of data-harvesting? How is the gaze reconstituted under a state of surveillance? What can archaeological fragments tell us about structures of categorization? Negative Spaces repositions the viewer as an
