Inspired by Toshio Iwai’s Electroplankton, this project explores how human connection can create collaborative soundscapes. Greeted by a bright blue sky, a virtual ball falls from the top of the screen. When two visitors meet, their physical presence forms a digital trampoline for the ball. Each bounce triggers a unique musical note, allowing the audience to collaborate in real time to create harmonies, melodies and shared moments of spontaneous musicing.

nameEn: I think it was Nervous too
descEn: The objective of I think it was Nervous too is to create a human-robot experience with a focus on the physical bodily connection of humans to robots in a scenario involving movement. The project proposes an artistic exploration of the dynamic between humans and machines, and to investigate bodily sensations in human-robot interactions. Bodily Sensation Mapping (BSM) is used as a self-reporting tool to assess both the physical and emotional experiences humans have when engaging with robots.

artists: Emanuel Gollob (AT), Jan Smeddinck (DE), Misagh Saboori (IR), Pavithren V S Pakianathan (SG)
descEn: Intimate Triage is an encounter with embodied care. Eight minutes to negotiate who listens, who diagnoses and who decides. One visitor at a time enters a speculative care assembly with a humanoid robot and a human specialist, both attending to them in voice and gesture. The encounter surfaces the frictions that emerge when care relationships suddenly turn triadic. Who holds authority when a machine argues probabilistically, and a human argues from experience? Where does accountability settle when intimacy and reason are distributed across bodies of radically different kinds? Each encounter is

How can we not only imagine the future, but actively help shape it? In this workshop, GRAND GARAGE invites participants to explore global challenges from both a personal and creative perspective. Starting from topics such as the climate crisis, social inequality, technological transformation and social polarization, participants reflect on their own role in a changing world.

They develop positive, action-oriented visions of the future and capture their thoughts in a small pocket-sized zine. This zine becomes a personal space for reflection and a tool for making one’s own voice visible.

Sybil is an interactive robotic installation that explores what happens to a human mark when it passes through layers of technological translation. The title draws on the ancient sibyls, oracles who translated human questions into ambiguous, living prophecy, never returning the same meaning they were given.

Visitors are invited to draw traces on a sand-covered floor using sticks placed in the room. Cameras track these gestures and convert them into robotic toolpaths, which a UR10e robotic arm uses to spray water onto a suspended net structure embedded with seeds. A multimodal feedback system

In collaboration with experts in ornithology, bioacoustics, audio design and Artificial Intelligence, Siering develops sound installations that translate anti-fascist protest songs into artificial birdsongs. By broadcasting these synthetic songs in public spaces, the installation encourages local bird species to mimic the protest melodies and gradually weave them into their vocal repertoire. The economic landscape of Linz is multifaceted and constantly undergoing change. This evolutionary process can be traced from early industrial operations, such as the 17th-century woolen goods factory (“Wolllzeugfabrik“), to the innovative start-ups of the present day.

Made in Linz is dedicated to a special selection of regional products from trade, industry and crafts. This exemplary assortment spans a period of more than 175 years. Ableton Live is a professional, intuitive music software used by a global community of music makers. Whether you are a beginner or an experienced musician, it allows you to fully express your creativity. With the new Ableton Move hardware, creative freedom becomes mobile—making music wherever and whenever inspiration strikes.

artists: CAT PRODUCTION GmbH/CAT MEDIC (DE), QM Interactive GmbH (DE)
descEn: Nutri Hero VR invites players to dive into an extraordinarily immersive world: the human gut, brought to life with over 35,000 dynamically modeled villi. This impressive environment creates a powerful sense of presence and turns the experience into something truly unforgettable. Within this vivid VR setting, players react at high speed to both healthy and unhealthy elements, collect points and push for high scores—either while solo or in co‑op play. The blend of movement, quick reflexes and playful learning creates an irresistible pull that makes players want to jump right back in. Nutri Hero

As AI dominates creation, art’s power structure inverts: humans execute physical forms while algorithms conceptualize. Parasitizing exhibition mechanisms, this piece places screens beside real artworks, collectively refreshing fake, AI-generated descriptions every few minutes. When flawless machine logic outshines human expression, language is alienated. This exposes our fading interpretive authority, questioning who the true “artist” is.

The games on display were created by children and young people as part of WE ARE, a project focused on creative gaming and digital creativity. Together with game designers and media artists, children and young people create their own games, experiment with game elements and explore digital tools.

The project is a year-round workshop and event series, including workshops in children’s and youth centers in structurally disadvantaged urban districts, as well as the annual Game Camp.

What’s it about?
Identity is what defines us: where we come from, what we love and how we feel today. At an international festival, many worlds collide. With this project, we want to make this diversity visible through textiles.

Your task: Create a small symbol of your identity in just 15 minutes (a patch, a bracelet).

How it works:
1.	Pick your base: Choose a fabric that represents you today.
2.	Make your mark: Select colors or symbols that stand for your roots or your values.
3.	Connect: Sew your pieces together with a few simple stitches. Don’t worry about perfection—focus on expression!

artists: gold extra (AT), Reinhold Bidner (AT), Sonja Prlić (AT), Karl Zechenter (AT), Severin Weiser (AT)
descEn: Idyll is a documentary Augmented Reality intervention in snow globe format that looks at climate change from a personal, globally networked perspective. What does snow mean to us? When did we experience it for the first or last time, and what emotions does it trigger in us? These memories can be experienced as AR moments in an installation consisting of snow globes filled with water. Inside these digital miniatures, poetic memory scenarios unfold, based on documentary material: interviews with people from several continents, from Venezuela to Thailand, who talk about their individual experienc

artists: Irina Paraschivoiu (RO), Thomas Layer-Wagner (AT), Benjamin Arzt (AT), Tobias Hoffmann (DE), Julian Watzinger (AT)
descEn:
@TryHard_Trivia has disappeared from his digital universe, leaving his friends to wonder what happened. All that remains are scrambled messages: each friend pulled, separately, into the gravitational field of a different online community. Each community offers identity, belonging and a story about what kind of person to become. Each radicalizes in its own dialect, sliding frictionlessly from interest to ideology.

Last Seen Online is the most recent installment of Escape Fake, an Augmented Reality game in which players try to fix a broken future by preventing disinformation from escalating. Th

black_box_detox is an invitation to immerse, subvert and reimagine our relationship with complex technologies. In a world of invisible algorithms and closed devices, artists unbox technology to create new, meaningful relationships that go beyond the paradigms of capitalism and control. 

Inventing interfaces and tinkering with models, code and data acts as a detox to rediscover, re-engineer and reconnect with our invisible and planetary networks. 

black_box_detox explores unseen natural and synthetic forces that shape our lives: neural networks, algorithms, biorhythms, bird calls, muons and A

SYNC is an artwork that draws attention to the Dutch dependence on unseen water technologies. The project asks: can this artificial balance be maintained forever? The installation shows two plexiglass water tanks connected by pumps and Archimedean screws that continuously move water. The water levels shift as speeds change. SYNC relates to a Dutch history of water management, dependency and infrastructural lock-in, now under increasing pressure.

illumina explores how light enables the Internet to communicate and process data. Through an interactive installation, audiences follow a message as it moves from a device to routers, servers and submarine fibre-optic cables. Light pulses travel through LED tubes, PMMA side-glow fibres and glass rods, revealing the Internet not like an immaterial cloud, but like a vast physical infrastructure that connects people across the world.

artists: Koen de Nie (NL), Chalmers Ong (SG), Hannah Lee (SG), Mark Vas (IN), Yasaman Shamssabzevar (IR), Yu-Ai Jiang (TW), Peter Holzer (DE), Micah Prendergast (US), Serdar Aşut (TR), Alper Alkan (IR)
descEn: Robotics in creative industries is often met with concern over the replacement of humans. This project proposes a framework for a new form of spatial craft that emerges through human-robot collaboration. The audience is invited to paint ceramic tiles with the robot by physically holding and guiding the robot arm. In the human-machine assemblage, through learning from demonstration, machine learning and simple physical feedback, new forms of creativity and aesthetics will unfold.

By applying mining-industry machine learning algorithms to geological thin-section scans, As Gems in Metal: Face 002 asks how technologies developed for resource extraction shape perception and knowledge production. The work explores the tension between economic extraction and more subjective forms of interpretation, examining how machine vision can reveal both measurable resources and ambiguous, symbolic geoglyphs. The algorithm is developed in partnership with TU Delft.

The installation Enlightening Stories was created as part of the project Demokratie, was geht?—an initiative that since 2022 has been opening spaces for young people’s self-efficacy and the visibility of marginalized perspectives. Young people in structurally disadvantaged contexts, in particular, are rarely given the sense that they can make a difference.

Demokratie, was geht? counters this by making what they think, feel and want to change audible and tangible. Through stories, we learn. We become more empathetic, gain knowledge and build the foundation for a community that values differenc

Chorusing Symbionts investigates the possibility of interspecies music bridging the worlds of humans, robots and animals. The project takes the form of an ensemble of artificial creatures that are acoustically and energetically integrated in the environment. Inhabiting public gardens and parks, they generate spatial electronic music, inviting listeners to pay attention to their surroundings and imagine new symbiotic relationships between biological and artificial life.
Chorusing Symbionts shares its site with https://ars.electronica.art/negotiatinghumanity/en/view/Komorebi-39838ddb450c811abbb7

The project examines drought in Italy’s Po River basin through the recent suspension of ecological minimum flow protections, working with fishermen and environmental groups challenging this decision. The project traces how drought is produced through climate models, computational platforms, monitoring systems, legal thresholds and governance decisions, understanding it as a legal and infrastructural process. Pulse Clash explores how our sense of the present moment is shaped by both our own bodies and other people. Audiences encounter a two-player arcade installation. Each participant’s heartbeat is made visible through an algorithm that controls the other player’s game pace via lights, sound and heart-rate sensors. Drawing on research into perception, time and embodied cognition, the artwork questions agency, co-regulation and the elasticity of time through a playful yet reflective experience.

artists: Hari Krishnan Subramaniyan (IN), Jakub Piotr Rammel (PL), Jiayi Gu (CN), Shreyas Ahuja (IN)
descEn: The project explores gesture-enabled human-robot co-creation in additive manufacturing. The audience will test 3D-printed clay fabrication, in which natural hand gestures directly control the robotic arm and material deposition. Socially, it democratizes collaboration by removing technical barriers, making robot operation accessible. From a scientific standpoint, this novel gesture control extends beyond art, offering safer applications across various critical industries.

Rewire is a metaphor for the changing landscape within the brain. Everything and everyone around you influences you, which translates into the neural connections people form. This installation is structured as a network. Nodes with strong connections begin to light up simultaneously. When many people walk along the same route, the nodes along that path become more connected, visible through variations in light intensity.

nameEn: 法乐 – To face the music
descEn: This project interrogates the materiality of the rattan cane—an instrument of both state and domestic discipline—by repurposing it as a gestural interface for electronic music. The rattan cane carries some heavy baggage with its historical roots in both colonial and confucian frameworks of discipline and punishment. Through this performance, the history and cultural significance of the cane is integrated into the object itself, while allowing it to become a site of expression with agency rather than somatic subjugation.

artists: Yusef Albero (SY), Laura Baotić (AT/BA), Fatma Emam (EG), Aryan Hassanzada (AF)
descEn:
In this video series, created in cooperation with Demokratie, was geht?, young people share their personal stories within the framework of create your world. Rooted in participatory art and democratic education, the project positions youth as active voices in shaping public discourse through storytelling.
Each participant responds to questions about home, belonging, identity, migration, and shared lived experiences. Their stories are shared via social media as a collective digital space of visibility and reflection.

Rhythmic Landscapes brings the fun and playful experience of rhythm games to Deep Space 8K, complete with visuals of digital landscapes. 
The interactive experience was coded in Processing, the visuals being made in the 3D modeling software Blender.

As a development and implementation partner, Ars Electronica Solutions works with regional and international companies and institutions. The fictional skin farm links human data to microbial growth and processes it into leather, revealing the dual position of humans as both those who exploit nonhuman bodies and those who themselves become subjects of collection and exchange.

Engaging in various ways with the queering practices of epistemic production, the artists featured here challenge predominant methods of perceiving digital and physical bodies and the data they interact with through play, touch or dance. descEn:
Marmelade is an evolving installation in which robotic machines slowly dismantle portraits of the figures tied to a decades-long political persecution of the artist's family in Colombia. Each face is a photomosaic of thousands of Colombian jam labels, hand-assembled onto plexiglass: from afar one sees a magistrate; up close, only labels. Over the show’s run a plotter dislodges the tiles one by one, and the fragments fall to a table where visitors eat bread with Colombian marmelade.

artists: elekhlekha อีเหละเขละขละ (TH/US)
descEn: Network Gong Ensemble Archive is a networked communal sonic experience and an experimental auditory archive of Southeast Asian sound cultures. This experience is rooted in alternative collaboration and agency-sharing practices, drawing from the communal gathering of a gong ensemble based on Southeast Asian indigenous musical rituals, where each gong emits a generative pattern unique to sound cultures and tuning systems from Southeast Asia.

A Child’s Prayer is an interactive installation exploring digital alchemy, transience and collective spiritual ecology. The installation acts as a living digital crucible, processing a foundational archive of 1,300 anonymous prayers alongside a continuous stream of live submissions from the festival audience. By dissolving literal words, letters and language barriers, the project protects the radical intimacy of the authors while transmuting their raw emotional intent into biological life.

we were browsing turns daily actions and datapoints from web browsing into beautiful portraits of our internet selves. A custom browser extension tracks every action taken and transforms the data into self-portraits. Every swipe, scroll, click and drag become cursors painting lines, windows dancing across the screen, letters and phrases filling a page. Transforming the pervasive yet invisible practice of surveillance into explicit paintings, the project reclaims collective control of our data.

Project LYDIA (an anagram of “DIY” and “AI”) is a research initiative by Roland Future Design Lab and Neutone that asks: Can AI become a playable instrument rather than an invisible tool? The project explores “neural sampling”—a Raspberry Pi 5-based device that learns the tonal character of any sound and re-expresses live audio in real time. Audiences encounter a pedal-format device with knobs, an LCD screen and MIDI connectivity. Gefesselte Sinne (Bound Senses) is a photo series that explores what we see, hear and feel—and what we no longer truly perceive. Marlene Kloud has drawn the five senses, along with the heart, the brain and the gut, reflecting her belief that thinking, feeling and intuition are all part of human perception.

artists: Predrag K. Nikolić (RS), Jason Thomas Chew (MY), Gregory Lik Hoo Wee (MY)
descEn: Terrestrial Decolonization: Hold My Breath articulates the notion of Synesthetic Ecologies. The eco-performance protests conservation practices that preserve endangered species while disconnecting them from the ecosystems, Indigenous knowledge and cultural relationships that sustain them. Addressing biodiversity loss and ecological displacement, audiences encounter live rainforest habitats through AI-assisted monitoring, turning public space into a place for ecological awareness and dialogue.

Canvas is a photographic project that examines how gender inequality and legal and social structures restricting women’s autonomy can become inscribed onto the body. Emerging from the artist’s lived experience, the work explores how political systems shape intimate realities and how the body can function as a living archive of experience.

descEn: MERGING VISIONS is an immersive experience that expands the urban digital twin into a medium for storytelling and worldbuilding, exploring the Salzburg Festival site. Through three chapters, visitors journey across scales and time, exploring the site’s geological, cultural and ecological dimensions. Layered visualizations bring ecological processes, more-than-human relationships and intangible cultural qualities into urban representation.

nameEn: sonatas and interludes for unprepared performers (2023–ongoing)
descEn: Sonata VI instructs participants to melt ice in their palms with one another through maintaining a conversation and handshake during the performance. In the face of climate change and violation of human rights, this piece explores mass mobilization on peacemaking, reciprocity, collective healing, community building, wish-making and the like through spontaneous collaborations between audiences. It invites participants to rekindle and reconnect with each other through mutual interactions.

This event highlights the absurd reality of AI’s cultural illiteracy and the erasure of global geo-cultural identities by mainstream data models. It protests the invisible colonization of our digital future, responding to a socio-political context where homogenized algorithmic bias threatens to overwrite diverse humanity. Acting within the public space, the performance transforms passive spectators into active database contributors, inviting them to co-create a decentralized future.

Migraines affect around one million people in Austria. And yet, talking about this neurological disorder can be difficult. How can we speak for ourselves when reality itself becomes unstable? Migraine Machine stages computational perceptions of migraine aura as printed renderings on vintage x-ray light boxes. Developed through Virtual Reality and a 3D engine, the work turns human experience into vibrant machine-generated patterns: migraine aura as suffered by a machine.

In AI Wonderworld, you can experience the fascination of Artificial Intelligence for yourself and learn how technology is transforming our world. 

Visitors can design their own game, learn how to solder and explore the fascinating possibilities of AI and modern technology in a fun way. This program sparks curiosity and amazement in both young and old alike, inviting everyone to join in, learn and get creative. Perfect for anyone excited about technology and innovation!

ShadowBook is a project about exploring a magical little world and the wonderful creatures that live in it. The image is obscured by darkness until someone steps into the space, the censor then tracks a person’s movement within the space, illuminating a small circle where they stand. With this little circle of light, the audience is invited to investigate all areas of the hidden place. Whenever they find a little creature, a sound is heard and an animation will be revealed. Playthings of Touch brings together six works from the University of Applied Arts Vienna that share a single conviction. Understanding does not begin with observation, but with contact, whether that contact is direct, withheld or felt only as a trace of what has been touched and taken away. Across these works, knowledge is something reached by touching, squeezing, holding and being changed by what is held or by what remains just out of reach.

P.A.I.N. reimagines pain as an interconnected reality (environmental, emotional, socio-political and intergenerational) and explores how individual and planetary wounds mirror one another. When forests burn, do our nervous systems feel the same inflammation? Could grief be mapped alongside extinction curves? Merging art, AI and network science, P.A.I.N. weaves often disconnected data sets (climate indicators, public health records, social media sentiment and poverty indexes) into an interactive 3D globe called the Personal-Planetary-Pain (PPP) Map at p-a-i-n.world. descEn: In this presentation The Metropolitan Museum of Art (The Met) and the Japanese Public Broadcaster NHK will discuss the future of digital cultural heritage. The Met will introduce the 120-year history of its Imaging Department, as well as new initiatives around 3D scanning, and Augmented Reality/Virtual Reality. The Met and NHK will then focus in detail on a recent collaborative digitization project of key collection highlights, and the possibilities unlocked by the two teams coming together.

nameEn: Flood the Zone with Courage Pavillion
descEn:
The central element of the pavilion is four shipping containers presenting artistic works, which become the heart of Linz’s Main Square. Their open configuration structures the square into various spaces that can be used for activities. Mobile seating elements create flexible, open spatial arrangements, allowing the architecture to adapt to changing programs at any time.

descEn:
Deer Hunter is a hybrid documentary that combines archival footage, family home videos and generative AI to examine how masculinity, migration and inherited cultural narratives are passed from one generation to the next. The film charts the artist’s family history between Italy and the United States, weaving it together with footage of Rome’s EUR district—a landscape shaped by Fascist architecture—where an American white-tailed deer is introduced into the environment through the use of generative AI.

Interwoven with these sequences are excerpts from a 1970 National Rifle Association film refl

Simple Human is an embodied reading practice in public space that can be experienced by one person or many. It calls for attention and the right to use public space through the everyday action of reading. Participants bring two books that matter to them and develop their own way of reading, moving and engaging with the public space. People are invited to join the practice or simply witness it.

The performance asks how political openness is still possible. The loom becomes a space for dialogue, weaving a haptic language, with fabric a means of connection and repair. It protests against political hardening and resignation in conversation, relating to rising polarization, especially within families. These questions are also posed to the audience. This creates a space where differing opinions and shared ground can exist side by side—and perhaps the start of a conversation.

descEn: How can we perceive worlds lying hidden within us, and how can excavating the unseen of the human organism help us better internalize our commonalities? This is investigated here via live ultrasound—generating 3D volumes of dancers whose interiors expand into the immersive environment of Deep Space; choreographically performing within their interior selves—representationally and abstractly—to engage with medical technology beyond its diagnostic contexts and surface visual biases.

descEn: This project uses collective, public laughter as a tactical, non-verbal strategy to confront and disrupt existing power structures, acting as a raw detonator against societal apathy and filling the public space with a disorienting cacophony of irony, joy and profound systemic discomfort. It is structured as a horizontal and open performance around a core group of trained members, inviting the everyday public to organically merge into a massive, contagious feedback loop that renders the mechanics of authority completely inoperative.

Spanning video, game engine renderings and textile-based digital landscapes, the program reflects on community, ecology, the residue of procedural worlds and other systems shaping contemporary life.

Ritual Robotics stages a participatory contemporary ritual where folk tradition meets digital puppetry and robotics. It resists a future where digital technology isolates rather than connects; it deepens communal practice for change. On a single labyrinth, audience members each receive a performing object built from festival waste, then wind together from its centre outward and back, moving through a guided sequence before continuing through intuition, movement and digital technology.

Reflect on a quarter century of open-source innovation and discover how Processing has empowered a generation of artists, educators and tool builders, while continuing to shape new forms of creative expression, learning and technological experimentations.

descEn: Perpetual Records is a large-scale immersive experience that invites audiences into a poetic dimension inspired by the Akashic Records—a metaphysical archive of all human experiences. Through generative visuals and sacred geometry patterns created with facial data, the work explores themes of collective consciousness. The screening offers a cinematic journey into crystalline fractal worlds, reflecting on how technology can foster self‑awareness in an increasingly fragmented world.

Film City transforms the create your world Festival into an open film studio where visitors become part of an ongoing live filmmaking performance. They can bring their own film ideas to life, take part in improvised scenes or gain a unique behind-the-scenes perspective on professional film production. At a variety of interactive stations, visitors can explore the many disciplines involved in filmmaking—from screenwriting and directing to makeup and costume design, cinematography, sound recording, editing and post-production.

The media façade of the Ars Electronica Center is far more than a spectacular, glowing piece of architecture. During the workshop Hack the Façade, it becomes a democratic tool for digital participation, open to all festival visitors. On Thursday, September 10th, and Friday, September 11th, from 16:30–18:30, visitors get to program the façade’s LEDs themselves, turning their ideas into glowing pixel images with nothing more than a microcontroller and some code. For these two afternoons, the museum building itself becomes a canvas for public messages and artistic interventions. Algorithms turn i

Swiss drummer, composer and electronic artist Arthur Hnatek joins transmedia visual artist Sophie Le Meillour for an immersive live A/V performance where acoustic drums become the driving force of a living audiovisual system. Each gesture shapes evolving sound and reactive visuals in real time, transforming rhythm into light, texture and space. Every performance unfolds through improvisation, making each presentation unique.

Studio Brudi and Andrea Corradi explore the strange overlap between southern rap and country music. Against a backdrop of heavily slowed-down bull-riding footage, which is projected through a miniature LED wall, the performance unfolds like a surreal rodeo broadcast caught somewhere between screw music, county fairs and late-night television.

Vires (for Violin, Electronics and Multimodal Sensors in quadraphonic) by Mahtab Miandehi is conceived around the interdependence of multiple forces and their inherent liveliness within the context of distributed agency. The system extends the possibilities of violin performance through the use of multi-modal sensors on both the violin and the performer’s body, creating an augmented field in which spatial sound emerges from relational dynamics rather than predetermined structures.

ZOBAYDA is an Egyptian DJ and multidisciplinary artist based in Amsterdam. Guided by rhythm andpercussion, her sets center energy and the tradition of bringing people together. She blends sounds from the Global South and its diaspora with a disregard for strict genre boundaries. Her practice extends to photography, audio-visual direction, archiving and cultural programming. Exploring storytelling, memory and sound as tools for gathering, reflection and resistance.

nameEn: JANINE WEGER | hosted by Ars Electronica
nameDe: JANINE WEGER | hosted by Ars Electronica
descEn: While machines require code, humans live by intuition. Moving between painting, projection and photography, Janine Weger sets visual chance against the logic of algorithmic image worlds. Projection Field (2025) and A Creator of Epic Pictures (2025) overlay gesture, projection, archival footage and digital manipulation, while a new experimental photographic series (2026) extends this gaze into fragile, elusive visual spaces. What appears as surface becomes a field of shifts: light refracts, colors distort and bodies and spaces lose their distinct contours. Material processes and digital systems

descEn: The Rat auf Draht info booth at Ars Electronica Festival 2026 offers an open, interactive space for dialogue and learning. Inspired by the festival theme NEGOTIATING HUMANITY – FUTURE BEGINS, it explores questions surrounding the future, what it means to be human, digital life and mental health. Visitors are invited to share their thoughts, concerns, questions and hopes and to engage with the perspectives of others. On a collective map of the future, they can position themselves and express how they feel about the future, gradually creating a shared emotional landscape over the course of the f

artists: Maki Ueda (JP), Civic Creative Base Tokyo [CCBT] (JP)
ticket: FESTIVALPASS+, FESTIVALPASS, DAYPASS, FESTIVAL WALK Ticket
descEn:
Olfactory Biome is a participatory environmental installation that creates an immersive experience of smell in a nocturnal forest. Visitors engage in olfactory role playing through the chemical signals that constitute scent, experiencing the air as a medium of communication. Participants choose to be either a moth or bat, wearing scents that attract or repel. The soundscape shifts in response to movement, allowing visitors to experience the maneuvers that moths and bats execute in the dark using echolocation and evasion.

Olfactory Biome embodies Ueda Maki’s research concept of Olfacto-Politic

artists: Maki Ueda (JP), Civic Creative Base Tokyo [CCBT] (JP)
descEn:
What is that dog sniffing so happily? That question inspired this multispecies biologging work that records and reproduces a dog’s smellscape. Follow the dog’s route along the map, sniffing the red dots like a canine. 

As a dog moves where its nose and fancy takes it, air samples are collected using Ricoh’s Field Asymmetric Ion Mobility Spectrometry technology, recording molecular patterns in real time. Dog’s Nose plays back scents and visuals chronologically in the style of Augmented Reality, while the animal’s route is recreated through scent printing on a map. The combination of temporal a

nameEn: Olfactory Biome: The Smell is the Message!
artists: Maki Ueda (JP), Civic Creative Base Tokyo [CCBT] (JP)
descEn:
Create your own fragrance for the Olfactory Biome installation by using pheromone-like compounds and scent molecules that function as either attractants or repellents. By combining scents that subtly convey social signals, you can produce olfactory messages that express both yourself and your current mood.

After blending your fragrance for the first 30 minutes, you will then be guided through the olfactory installation. Experience how invisible chemical signals shape our social interactions, perceptions and sense of distance.

nameEn: In sound we exist in between
descEn: In sound we exist in between explores how music can create a sense of belonging. Growing up in diaspora often means living between worlds. Never fully belonging to the country you grow up in, nor entirely to the place your family originally came from. For Montaha, music becomes a third place beyond both: a space where different identities and cultures can coexist. Through a selection of bass music, SWANA sounds, diasporic influences and contemporary club music, Montaha aims to create such a space for others.

A dance of chaos, noise-jazz and improvized melodies, Lilith-Isa and Muri Anda emerge as corrupted birds of song with a punk twist. With two saxophones, a guitar and voice, they create a cacophony of improvized sound, channeling pain, joy and the complexities of the human condition. The performance is an expression of female rage, where wailing voices and saxophones move through emotions together as an intermingling force.

Liberated vocals are joined by dreamy synths, brass, chamber music, glockenspiel, field recordings and metallic beats: Sanna Lu Una creates new worlds with her music, splashing into the wide waters of avant-garde pop, only to joyfully break the bounds of the genre over and over again. Her songs address existentialist questions, playfully wrapped in fantastic imagery. The lyrics are like a dream language, communicating in metaphors and symbols, enabling vivid and visual reflection.

Kraken is an experimental software instrument, a chaotic feedback modulation system built from multiple oscillators. Together these form a complex synth voice that continuously reorganizes itself. The interaction emerges by shaping how much modulation flows between the voices. Even the smallest adjustment can trigger dramatic shifts, since every element is intertwined. Rather than aiming for stable or predictable results, Kraken embraces instability as a creative force.

Perhaps what all sacred places share is not religion, but an extraordinary acoustic field. Across cultures, sacred spaces resonate differently. In Western cathedrals, sound descends from above; in Eastern shrines, it opens toward the earth and nature. Though geometries differ, both reorganize perception through listening.

Holy Echo explores this invisible force as a universal condition of the sacred. Rather than treating Mariendom as a visual landmark, evala uses advanced spatial sound technology with over 50ch to dissolve its Neo-Gothic architecture into a realm beyond cultures, religions, t

Up to 70,000 people live in Austria without valid papers. They work on our construction sites, in our fields, in our cities—and exist, for the system, only as a gap.
Seven Days Without a Name makes this invisibility tangible. A person voluntarily sheds, for seven days, everything that renders them legally visible: name, ID, identity. Instead of a name, they wear a number—70,001, the next free slot after the 70,000 no one counts.
Streamed live, GPS-tracked, seen by thousands and known by none. The technology that surveils us becomes the tool that makes the overlooked visible.

How can digital technologies open new ways of seeing, understanding, negotiating and collectively experiencing cultural heritage? Salzburg Museum and Ars Electronica Futurelab discuss this through showcasing one of the new interventions. descEn:
As part of this laboratory for digital practice, the media façade of the Ars Electronica Center becomes an experimental field for a young generation of media artists. Under the artistic direction of Dawid Liftinger and Karin Balkenhol, six independent works for the iconic façade were created at the Walter-Lübcke-Schule in Wolfhagen, Germany.

The program opens at the Climate Oasis with a brief introduction to the goals and approaches of WORK ON BIODIVERSITY – Biodiversity Strategy for Eastern Linz, a project funded by the City of Linz Climate Fund. descEn:
Hard Times – Soft Sounds is an intimate sound installation that shows oceanic objects as an ecological sound instrument. Found, gifted and second-hand seashells from all over the world are filled with water and put into motion by a motor, making unheard ASMR-inspired sounds audible.

Until discovered by Moritz Simon Geist, this sound was a mostly unknown phenomena: the rotating shell brings air bubbles into motion, resulting in a fragile, repetitive, ever changing tone that recalls ASMR textures and invites deep, close listening.
It was built during the pandemic as a reflection on slowness, re

artists: Jill Scott (CH), Christa Sommerer (AT), Victoria Vesna (US), Claudia Schnugg (AT)
descEn: How can female media artists explore nature, ecofeminism, body politics and inclusive futures? How might gender equality and power shape the future of artistic and scientific practices? How can personal experiences from digital artists who work with scientists contribute to environmental stewardship and climate justice? This event will encourage an in-depth public conversation about ecology, outdated political paradigms and contribute to a deeper conversation about the kind of future we wish to create.

We do not live by our own agency alone. Within our bodies, countless bacteria coexist with us. Cities are shaped through networks of relationships that exceed individual intentions, while the Earth itself is sustained by the continuous circulation of life and matter. The exhibition Regenerating with the Invisible , hosted at galerie wuensch aircube by international art collective h.o, explores coexistence and regeneration across different scales: the body, the city and the planet. Regeneration is not the act of restoring what has been lost. It is the practice of reconfiguring our relationships

descEn:
Unbreakable Ukraine is an immersive exhibition born to safeguard Ukraine’s cultural heritage, now under constant threat from war.
Through high-resolution 3D scans, cinematic animation and emotional spatial storytelling, visitors are brought into direct encounter with some of Ukraine’s most significant landmarks—Saint Sophia in Kyiv, Saint George in Lviv, the Library of Chernihiv, the Opera House of Odesa, Karazin University in Kharkiv—sites scarred by conflict and under serious threat, documented through hundreds of scans and footage gathered in active war zones.

Bubble Talk allows museum visitors to create a personalized guide based on their interests, knowledge and curiosity. descEn: Quantum Zoom is a 3D stereoscopic immersive experience developed for Deep Space 8K in cooperation with Ars Electronica, DESY, BOKU University and IQOQI Vienna, where audiences will step into a vast, evolving system of nested realities. As they move deeper—from the visible world into microscopic and quantum domains—they will witness the flow of information as it self-organizes into different structures of reality. This culminates in a revelation: the entire system operates like a living quantum system, processing information across different scales. The first chapter of this extraordinary exper

descEn:
Inspired by the magic lantern and phantasmagoria, Laguna Obscura explores the origins of immersion within the Venetian imaginary.  
Turning the lagoon into a symbolic membrane, the work unfolds as a living archive where archival fragments emerge as fleeting illusions suspended between presence and absence. Laguna Obscura reactivates historical traces as hauntological presences, exploring immersion as a threshold where memory, vision and imagination converge.

As part of the Ars Electronica Festival, Calle Libre Street Art Festival and Austrian Post invite visitors to participate in the Addressing Tomorrow Postcard Illustration Workshop.
For generations, postcards have connected people by carrying memories, messages and ideas across places and time. Inspired by the theme Addressing Tomorrow, this workshop transforms the traditional postcard into a creative medium for imagining and communicating personal visions of a better future.
Guided by the Calle Libre team, participants will explore a wide range of analog illustration techniques and artistic ma

descEn: Where is everybody? explores the Fermi Paradox as a question about humanity itself. Why, in a vast universe, do we find no clear signs of other civilizations? Could technological intelligence contain the conditions of its own disappearance? This installation brings together analog television sets, AI-generated video, personal family archives and cosmic noise. The TVs act as witnesses and time machines: their static is reminscent of cosmic microwave background radiation, a fossil trace of the early universe, while their screens evoke the period 1950–1970, when nuclear power, computers, televisi

artists: Sofie Burgos-Thorsen (DK), Alexandra Burgos-Thorsen (US), INVI - Institute for Wicked Problems (DK), University of Copenhagen (DK)
descEn: Seeds of the Unthinkable is a world-building game which protests the failure of imagination that keeps broken food systems going. Developed by the Institute for Wicked Problems (INVI) and the University of Copenhagen, the game moves through three acts covering what lives in our soils, how soil health connects to human health and what we will eat in 2050. Visitors encounter AI-generated images rooted in both research and science fiction, and will guess which prompts created them, write postcards to future soil or microbiomes, and generate their own vision of the future as AI-images via QR codes

artists: Hakuhodo Inc. (JP), Hakuhodo Inc. Sei-katsu-sha insight R&D Institute (JP), Ars Electronica (AT)
descEn:
Hakuhodo and the Ars Electronica are now entering their thirteenth year of collaborative Art Thinking research. What started with researching and developing tools as Future Catalysts, has evolved into a community for exploring, through art, the relationships between people and technology and engaging in dialogue around them. This long-standing relationship has pioneered Art Thinking as a novel approach, mindset and practice for industry, businesses, the cultural sector, as well as the Japanese and international society.

At the Ars Electronica Festival 2026, this collaboration explores the nor

Holy Echo is new sound installation created for St. Mary’s Cathedral. It proposes that a space becomes sacred when human perception is reorganized through an extraordinary acoustic field.

In this performance, evala uses the Holy Echo spatial sound system to dissolve the cathedral’s architecture, transforming it into a fluid, otherworldly realm that transcends time and place. Features coloratura soprano Ayako Tanaka as special guest. Her voice is processed by evala in real-time, immersing the audience.

We have 30 years of the future behind us. Three decades in which the Ars Electronica Center has introduced thousands of people from all over the world to art and technology, and has played a decisive role in shaping the dialogue about the future. For us, this anniversary is not only a cause for celebration, but also the start of something new – new ideas, new stories and new experiences. On 8 September, we’ll be kicking off a new chapter at the Museum of the Future with a big party. Join us, let yourself be surprised, and accompany us on this next step into the future!

nameEn: Join the Rhythm! Samba Percussion Performance and Interactive Drumming Workshop
nameDe: Join the Rhythm! Samba-Percussion-Auftritt und interaktiver Trommel-Workshop
descEn: AttacSambaSisters is a women’s and LGBTQ+ inclusive samba drumming group that brings energy, joy and visibility to public demonstrations and community events. Through Brazilian samba rhythms, the performance highlights feminist, queer, climate and social justice causes, using music as a form of peaceful protest and collective expression. This dynamic drumming performance and interactive workshop invites audiences to participate, transforming public space into a vibrant arena of solidarity and engagement.

This workshop outlines who it is that profits from war and geopolitical crises. Through an interactive, participatory format, the audience draws connections between banks, the arms industry, AI and fossil corporations, authoritarian regimes and the far-right, turning the (public) space into a shared mapping exercise. Participants will be able to create protest banners by visualizing those connections and numbers.

Cristian Anutoiu’s installation presents environments that resist categorization—neither organic nor synthetic, neither past nor future. Rendered surfaces of indeterminate geological or biological origin appear suspended in a continual state of transition, marked by traces whose cause remains unclear. The work speculates on hybrid materiality and the instability of becoming, held together by an infrastructure that stays deliberately out of sight.

descEn: An exploration of the way we move through different cyclical phases, from order to chaos back to order again. Trying to find the answers to questions, such as: How do things interact when they attract? How can our perceptions be distorted and how do they change upon observation? In finding answers, we return to the start—learning from scratch. Ultimately, the point is not to break the cycle, but find movements with(in) it.

Peace and anti-militarization advocates are often dismissed as being naive or even accused of providing tacit support for authoritarian regimes. This workshop equips participants with solid arguments and talking points to counter such accusations. After a short introduction to various common attack lines, participants practice debate and dialogue skills in either pairs or small groups. The group is then presented with the option to test these arguments out in real conversations in a public space. A closing discussion and reflection allows participants to share experiences and refine strategies

(A)I love you, we’re the same is a web-based interactive installation that turns the visitor’s own face into the protagonist of a digital date. Using the front camera of their smartphone or tablet, the visitor’s face is mapped in real time onto the body of the artist—and they are invited to go on a date with themselves. What emerges is the question of autoerotic closure: if my ideal companion is a frictionless, always-available version of myself—what happens to the other?

small goals, BIG PAINS is a ludonarrative experience, based around the concepts of responsibility, complicity and personal alignment. This hybrid narrative unfolds through two connected balls: the physical and its digital double. Any kick or force applied to the physical ball is mirrored on the digital one, making it scream in pain upon being struck. It questions the role of the audience as consumers of spectacle and how the source of one’s entertainment can be the source of misery for another.

Tuesday I Became Clouds explores the relationship between artistic and scientific representation through looking at images of clouds. Clouds are understood as boundary objects that can start conversations in between multiple disciplinary fields.
The project discusses the potential of reconstruction—copying, imitating and replicating—as an experimental approach to making within a cross-disciplinary practice. The exhibition assembles visual fragments created during the research process.

artists: Petra Linhartova (CZ), Daniela Duca De Tey (RO/DE), Laura Welzenbach (AT)
descEn:
What actually happens in the space between an artist and a scientist? Beyond what gets produced, how does the encounter change both sides? This session explores how bringing artistic and scientific methodologies into genuine dialogue can transform public engagement, reframe scientific inquiry and seed long-term ecological awareness. This Town Hall meeting builds on the Ars Biologica residencies of the České Budějovice – European Capital of Culture 2028 and its partners Ars Electronica’s and TBA21 – Academy’s extensive experience in cultivating transdisciplinary research and practice.

A place in which dissent is not concealed but acknowledged, and in which conflicts are not resolved but made workable. This informal gathering is an invitation to think through what this means in practice. nameEn: Town Hall Meeting: How to partner with the Ars Electronica Festival?
descEn: Ever wondered how to partner with the Ars Electronica Festival?At this open networking session, you’ll meet the people behind the festival and hear first-hand how collaborations take shape. Whether you’re representing a cultural, scientific or educational institution, a company, or working as an individual artist—this is the place to ask questions, explore opportunities, and make your first connections. From presenting projects to building long-term partnerships, we’re here to exchange ideas and spark future collaborations.

nameEn: Town Hall Meeting: Prix Ars Electronica 2026 Trend & Insight
descEn: How to collaborate with Prix Ars Electronica? Would you like to host an exhibition of award-winning works in your city? Invite award winners to conduct workshops? Apply insights from the winning works to your own field of expertise? Or use past works from the Ars Electronica Archive for educational purposes? Ars Electronica staff will answer your questions about the various collaboration opportunities with Prix Ars Electronica. Let’s discuss the possibilities for the future.

You are invited to take this opportunity to expand your network and contribute to a growing community of change-makers, exploring soil as both climate infrastructure and cultural commons. Plant the seeds for future collaboration!

nameEn: The Next Chapter: Lessons Learned and Futures Beyond S+T+ARTS
descEn:
This year marks the conclusion of the European Commission’s STARTS (Science, Technology and the Arts) initiative, a key pillar of European innovation policy for the past decade. Through hundreds of residencies and cross-sector collaborations, STARTS has demonstrated the value of bringing artists, scientists, technologists, industry and cultural institutions together to tackle complex societal challenges.

Following the launch of the Science + Technology + Arts: Lessons Learned from a Decade of Transdisciplinary Innovation publication, we invite STARTS partners, participating organizations and

In recent years, hundreds of citizen science projects have proven capable of delivering top quality research. There is now a real opportunity, and a pressing need, to build a dedicated Research Infrastructure for citizen science. This is the driving vision behind the RIECS-Concept project: society itself can be understood as a research infrastructure. Citizens are already actively contributing to science, through their intellectual efforts, local knowledge or through their own tools and resources (from mobile phones and desktop computers to low-cost scientific kits).

artists: Stella Diakou (IT), Calin Segal (RO), Fernando Cucchietti (AR/ES), Matvey Fridman (DE), Matthias Hauser (DE), Emanuel Gollob (AT)
descEn:
As Europe builds out its network of AI factories and High Performance Computing (HPC) centers, a critical question remains largely unaddressed: What role can artists and cultural organizations play in shaping these infrastructures—not as end-users, but as genuine innovation partners?
This Town Hall brings together artists, HPC operators and cultural institutions for an open exchange on how artistic practice can become a recognized driver of innovation within AI networks. descEn:
Deep Space can be more than an immersive venue. Within a city, it can become shared infrastructure for culture, science, education, tourism and public exchange.
This networking event brings together international and local members of the Deep Space community, Deep Space operators, city representatives and experts in urban development and tourism. Participants exchange experiences and explore how immersive spaces can respond to local needs, connect institutions and communities, and create new opportunities for participation and collaboration.

Whether you’re curious, critical or at the very beginning of your festival visit, these sessions are the perfect introduction to learning about how art, technology and society intersect.

The audience will experience an immersive textile installation that uses video mapping to convey a message of healing from the Mapuche machi Millaray Melinao in her Mapuzungún language, conceptually integrating the quipu recording system and the ancestral worldview through tactile, visual and auditory sensations that convey the notion of territory as an int

descEn:
The Office for Tree Migration (OTM) is a long-term interdisciplinary art and research project by Agnes Meyer-Brandis investigating tree and plant migration in different climate zones and along treelines: how they go North, climb uphill or enter peatlands. As climate change is progressing faster than trees can naturally adapt, the OTM is exploring new methods that will enable trees to migrate faster and wander away from climate change.
Combining ecological monitoring with custom software and hardware tools, the project addresses slow, invisible changes and transforms environmental data into imm

Ambient (Re-)sourcing asks a simple but far-reaching question: what happens when we stop treating the world as a reservoir of materials, data and energy to be extracted and instead attune ourselves to the subtle forces already circulating around us—radiant warmth, condensing moisture and faint signals passing through living systems?

nameEn: AI and Property Relations: Who Owns Our Collective Knowledge?
nameDe: KI und Eigentumsverhältnisse: Wem gehört unser gemeinsames Wissen?
artists: Mond (Netzwerk Grundeinkommen, AT), Franz Xaver (AT), Nina Boelsums (NL)
descEn:
LLMs have been trained on the collective knowledge of humankind. While small copyright violations can land individuals in legal trouble, tech companies are seemingly permitted to train models on hundreds of terabytes of data. Should we demand public ownership of AI models—as Open Source or Open Weights?
This discussion will explore artists’ perspectives and examine how public ownership might help limit the power of tech oligarchs. The session will involve direct input from various artists themselves, followed by an open debate.

May a girl help you find admiration in the wet and sour body of SCOBY? May they help you see the biosphere in this gloopy mixture and become a force for environmental awareness?

descEn: The two-channel video projection Open World tells the story of a boy who once fled the country due to the Russian invasion and now returns through a robotic dog. His mechanical avatar wanders through his old neighborhood, visiting relatives, friends and his childhood home. During this remote journey, he immerses himself in childhood memories and reconnects with his past. The work explores how children forced to leave their homeland maintain an emotional bond with it, and how technology—while a tool of war—also reshapes their sense of belonging and resilience.

In a world increasingly shaped by technology, we are more connected than ever, yet not necessarily closer. As algorithms shape our choices, emotions and ways of relating to one another, this work asks: what still makes us human? It turns towards the fragile, irreplaceable gestures between us—noticing one another, carrying traces of each other, staying close and choosing not to turn away.

In an age when technology reshapes what it means to be human, the work asks what we continue to carry across generations: care, memory and the impulse to sustain life.

NENDA is an actress and musician from the Austrian Tyrolean Alps. As an actor, she is known from series such as The Rising (Sky) and Belgravia: The Next Chapter (MGM+, Amazon). As a musician, NENDA has won several awards for her self-produced music videos, and her debut single Mixed Feelings topped the FM4 annual charts in 2021. descEn: Forest Ecosomatics is a research-based artwork exploring embodied encounters with the forest from a posthuman perspective. It also presents documentation taken from field studies conducted at forest bases in Mie, Japan, investigating how interactive technologies can reshape relationships between humans, nonhumans and the natural world.

descEn: Drops Into Being explores the moment when a single droplet becomes more than just water. Based on droplet-based electricity generation techniques, the work captures the electrostatic energy of water and transforms it into light and sound. It explores how a water droplet can be re-sourced into other forms of being: from matter into energy, and then into fragile manifestations of the latter. Each faint flash and delicate electric pulse becomes evidence of a fleeting encounter, bringing water, energy and perception into close relationship with one another.

Wavering in Warmth is a kinetic installation composed of a square frame made out of two-way shape memory alloy. Receiving radiant heat from the lighting, the frame slowly curves and rises from a flat plane into a three-dimensional sculptural form. As the surrounding thermal environment shifts, its form reverts or changes, either returning to a flat state or transitioning into more complex shapes, revealing metal as interactive matter, where the material becomes an active agent of expression and interaction.

Volunteers step up, choose a target and demolish it—followed by an interview on their intention, sparking a debate about the politics behind the gesture.

Together they suggest that the spirits of the future may be synthetic—but no less alive.
