ticket: FESTIVALPASS+, FESTIVALPASS, DAYPASS, Lentos Kunstmuseum Ticket
descEn:
Since the start of Israel’s military campaign in Gaza in October 2023, Forensic Architecture (FA) has collected vast amounts of data related to attacks on civilians and civilian infrastructure by the Israeli military, painstakingly documenting the near-total destruction of the conditions of life in Gaza. Their team has collected, verified and analyzed thousands of videos showing individual incidents of atrocities.
An interactive cartographic database and accompanying text report outline the ways in which Israel’s military operations have entailed widespread civilian harm, and identify patterns

artists: Jaron Ghani (GB), Lawrence Chiles (GB), John Stack (GB)
ticket: Ars Electronica Center Ticket, FESTIVALPASS, FESTIVALPASS+, DAYPASS
descEn: What if the National Gallery collection could dream? This Al-driven installation journeys through over 2,400 artworks, uncovering unexpected connections between paintings, artists and ideas. Shaped by visitor voices, it transforms collection data into a living map of discovery. National Gallery Dreaming is an Al-powered interactive installation that explores the hidden relationships within the National Gallery, London’s collection. Developed in collaboration with digital agency Numiko as part of the Gallery’s NGX innovation program, this audio-visual project combines computer vision, collectio

artists: Art and Technology Lab, Korea National University of Arts (KR)
descEn:
Kimchi S Witch is a location-based immersive Virtual Reality performance that explores kimchi fermentation as a speculative sensory system. The work transforms the cultural and biological process of fermentation into a virtual ritual space where smell, memory, microorganisms and bodily movement are interconnected.

The performance will start every 60min with the following schedule:
WED 9.9.: 10:00–13:00 / 16:00–19:00
THU 10.9.: 13:00–16:00
FRI 11.9.: 10:00–13:00 / 16:00–19:00
SAT 12.9.: 13:00–16:00
SUN 13.9.: 10:00–13:00
Stage host Vanessa Hannesschläger opens the day with a brief introduction to the programme, its key topics and the speakers joining the first day of the Theme Symposium.

nameEn: From Outrage to Influence: How Psychology, Creators and Platforms Shape Political Debate
artists: Isabel Linzer (US), Jon Roozenbeek (NL/GB), Alexander Sängerlaub (DE)
descEn:
Why does outrage spread so easily online—and how does it turn into political influence? This conversation brings together psychological insights and a closer look at the growing influence of social media creators in shaping political debate.

Jon Roozenbeek explores the psychological and social mechanisms that make people respond to conflict, outrage, and group identities, and how digital environments can amplify these tendencies. He looks at why polarization persists and what happens when human psychology meets platforms built around attention and engagement.

Isabel Linzer turns to the rise

nameEn: Weaponized Information - Disinformation as a Geopolitical Tool
artists: Gustav Gressel (AT/DE), Jan Nicola Beyer (DE), Jessikka Aro (FI), Masha Borzunova (DE)
descEn:
Disinformation is no longer simply a problem of false information. It has become a tool of geopolitical influence—used to exploit existing tensions, shape public narratives and undermine trust in democratic institutions. As AI makes it easier to produce and distribute convincing content at scale, the information space itself is becoming a field of conflict.

This panel brings together perspectives from security and geopolitical analysis, investigative journalism and the practical fight against information manipulation. Drawing on experience with Russian propaganda and influence operations, the

In this workshop, Christina Schwaha and Stefan Rathmanner from the fact-checking team of the Austria Presse Agentur (APA) discuss how various actors attempt to manipulate public opinion through disinformation on social media, and how fact-checkers themselves become targets of these actors. Using concrete examples, they highlight the methods behind various campaigns and explain what each of us can do to avoid spreading this content further.

nameEn: Designing the Digital Public: Building Spaces for Democratic Negotiation
artists: Jaya Klara Brekke (SE/GB), Harry Keller (DE), Lena Slachmuijlder (BE), Lucas Evers (NL), Mushon Zer-Aviv (IL/CH)
descEn:
What if we stopped asking how democracy can adapt to the digital spaces we already have—and started designing those spaces with democracy in mind?

The final session of the conference turns from diagnosis to possibility, inviting the speakers to imagine the digital institutions and public spaces of the future. If digital environments have become places where we meet, exchange ideas, form opinions and negotiate social conflicts, they also need to support the democratic processes that make living together possible.

The discussion explores what it could mean to design digital spaces for democrat

While tech-billionaires publicly celebrate their ”techno-optimism” (Andreessen), they secretly prepare for the possible consequences of their disruptive actions. In face of scenarios like climate collapse or civil wars they seek safety in private luxury bunkers, space colonies or in uploading their minds to the cloud; pursuing private exit-strategies rather than using their vast resources to make the world a better place. How did we get from the possibilities of the early cyber utopias to the catastrophising fantasies of the tech bros—and how can we reactivate a commitment to the interdependen

nameEn: Media Art Practice: collaborate, conserve, context and intentionality
artists: Paul Thomas (AU), Victoria Vesna (US), Mike Phillips (GB), Christa Sommerer (AT), Laurent Mignonneau (FR), Jaime de los Ríos (ES), Vale Vicente Matallana (1967-2026)
descEn:
This event by NEWART foundation, in collaboration with Encyclopedia of New Media Art, Volume II, Artist and Practice editor Paul Thomas, will create a documented alternative discussion focusing on artists' perspective on the sustainability of media art practice. To achieve this, we have invited five significant artists to facilitate discussion new media projects. This short provocation is presented to help create a dynamic community discussion with the goal of generating ideas for sustainable media art practices.

Dedicated to the memory of Vicente Matallana.

artists: Luc Bernard (US/FR), Yehuda Cohen (IL), Daphna Horenczyk (IL/AT), Emilie Moatti (IL), Zuhdi Najeeb (IL/PS), Gerfried Stocker (AT), Emmanuel Witzthum (GB/IL)
descEn: Dehumanization rarely begins with violence. It begins with language, with images, with enemy stereotypes in everyday life. Antisemitism is one of the oldest patterns of this kind, and in the digital space it is simultaneously taking on new, accelerated forms: algorithms amplify outrage and enemy images, antisemitic narratives spread globally and instantly, old stereotypes resurface in new digital forms and threats born online increasingly spill into physical, everyday life. When words become weapons and language itself becomes the site of conflict, the question arises: Who sets the conditions

nameEn: Practicing Impact: When Reality Talks Back
descEn: The Ars Electronica Futurelab explores the future by building it—together with companies, institutions, researchers, artists, designers and the public. This Town Hall brings together collaborators who turn ideas into reality. When existing formats no longer fit, we invent new ones. Rather than presenting success stories, we share the realities of experimentation, negotiation and practice—because impact is not an idea. It is something you create by doing.

nameEn: Prototyping Fictions: Workshop and Screening of Ocean Futurisms
descEn: Ocean Futurisms is a series of animated short films, inviting audiences to step into alternative, science-based futures for the ocean. Designed to be thought-experiments that inspire discussion about real-world change, the films are based on careful research and speculative fiction. This event includes a screening of the films and a hands-on introduction to the world-building approaches behind the project.

nameEn: Fluidity of Images: Surrealist Juxtaposition and Image Mixing in Generative AI
nameDe: Flüssigkeit der Bilder: Surrealistische Juxtaposition und Bildmischung in generativer KI
descEn: What happens when a machine mixes paintings without text prompts? Fluidity of Images explores the juxtaposition space between images: the territory between two source works where they combine to different extents to reveal a spectrum of new forms, condensations and compositions. It situates this practice within a broader continuum of procedural and collective artistic practices, where agency is distributed across processes, tools and collaborators.

This workshop asks who decides the music when machines generate endless sound on demand, which is as much a cultural question as it is an artistic one. Participants read a scene to music and then hear that same moment take on three different directions by using Soundbook, a tool built by Mathis Nitschke’s EU co-funded CORPUS project at Sofilab. He then demonstrates how contributing musicians actually co-own this corpus of music as opposed to simply supplying it. Filmmakers, game designers and musicians can all take part.

artists: S+T+ARTS Aqua Motion (EU), OpenFields: Zeynep Aksöz Balzar (TR), Mark Balzar (AT/US)
descEn: Water Whisperer explores how AI can facilitate collective dialogue while inviting visitors to experience water not as a resource to be managed, but as a living ecology of interconnected voices. Inside an immersive pneumatic environment, participants encounter the perspectives of the Danube, groundwater, wastewater, rain, fog and snow. Rather than providing answers, the AI encourages discussion, negotiation and collective reflection on questions surrounding climate adaptation and urban futures. By shifting the conversation from a human-centered perspective toward an ecological one, visitors are

Water Whisperer is an immersive participatory AI installation where visitors converse with the Danube, rain, snow, fog, groundwater and wastewater as living voices with their own interests played by AI agents. Rather than acting as an answer machine, AI facilitates collective dialogue, encouraging participants to negotiate different ecological perspectives and recognize themselves not as managers of water, but as part of an interconnected water cycle.

artists: ICK Dans Amsterdam (NL), IJAD Dance Company (GB)
descEn:
How can individual movement signatures be mapped, recognised and predicted? 
How can a dancing dialogue with the HAMLET Generative AI tools: Dance Style Analysis and Generation Enabler and the Music-to-Movement Enabler lead to new ways of inhabiting and discovering our bodies through movement, of relating to each other and to the tangibly physical and intangible, intuitively intelligible latent spaces into which we are immersed? The workshop invites participants to dance dialogues with(out) AI.

artists: Danube Transformation Agency for Agency (di:tafa), Solmaz Farhang (AT), Alexandra Fruhstorfer (AT), Lena Violetta Leitner-Stojanov (AT)
descEn: What can we learn from the transformative powers of the beaver? In this workshop, participants will experiment with creative futuring and forecasting methods to generate nuanced, multi-species scenarios that reframe the beaver from a passive wild animal to an active, technical and cultural stakeholder in landscape design and restoration. A guided process will unleash their imagination to co-create speculative worlds, culminating in a historical, yet tangible retrospective from the year 2051.

nameEn: The Sound of the Day: A Communal Sound Gathering with elekhlekha (อีเหละเขละขละ)
artists: elekhlekha อีเหละเขละขละ (TH/US)
ticket: DAYPASS, FESTIVALPASS+, FESTIVALPASS, Francisco Carolinum Linz Ticket
descEn: In this performance, elekhlekha (อีเหละเขละขละ) invites audiences to a communal participatory sound-making, activating their Network Gong Ensemble Archive—an interactive website, homemade gongs and found objects. Rooted in Southeast Asian oral and musical traditions threatened by displacement, the project asks whether sound and story can be archived without losing their living, relational meaning. Visitors of all ages are welcome to play, listen and add their own voice to the ensemble.

B10d13$3L-LLM is a performative installation by Gökay Atabek—developed in collaboration with Jan Zuiderveld and Ritsert Mans—that shows the often-hidden costs of Artificial Intelligence. The work uses a slow, “little language model” AI agent that runs on a single microcomputer powered by DIY biodiesel. In a darkly humorous way, it reveals the materiality, energy consumption and infrastructural limits of AI.

FARCE is the project of Vienna-based producer, songwriter, and performer Veronika König. FARCE brings together club music, avant-pop and experimental electronics in a high-energy set that moves between driving dancefloor moments, unexpected turns and unconventional sounds. Combining electronic production, vocals and a love for crossing genres, FARCE creates a space where experimentation and emotion meet. Rooted in Vienna’s independent music scene, FARCE’s work connects pop, club culture and electronic music in a playful and open way.

artists: Rajiv Bhagwanbali (NL), Anna Hazarian (UA), Philipp “Flip” Kroll (AT), Alina Lugovskaya (RU)
descEn: Press Start is a performance that involves dance, music and spoken word. It explores the challenges faced by a young individual who is pulled into a radical online universe through gaming, where they encounter manipulation, controlling behavior and bullying.

How can a high standard of living be maintained without dependence on fossil fuels? Powerplayground explores this question as a multi-room interactive exhibition at its own venue in Linz. Eight connected zones lead from energy and everyday life through the history and consequences of fossil-fuel use to climate change, renewable energy, practical solutions, education and green careers. Visitors encounter VR experiences, hands-on installations, energy visualizations, pedal-powered stations, guided tours, talks and partner projects. The exhibition connects scientific knowledge with social and pol

The future begins. But it doesn’t start from nothing. It starts with a question that we ask. With the knowledge that we store and create. With the values we defend. And with the courage to renegotiate what seems given.
 
In 2026, two anniversaries coincide that talk about the future in a special way. The Johannes Kepler University Linz looks back at sixty years: six decades full of research, education, social responsibility, and the claim not just to observe change, but to shape it. The Ars Electronica Center and the Futurelab celebrate thirty years of existence, where art, technology and soci

ticket: DAYPASS, Ars Electronica Center Ticket, FESTIVALPASS, FESTIVALPASS+
descEn: SynTact explores how future teams might extend beyond humans to include plants, robotic systems, and other forms of intelligence and life. Through touch as a shared mode of communication, the installation investigates new forms of more-than-human collaboration. This Guided Exploration invites visitors to experience SynTact together with artists and researchers, combining a live interaction with the installation and an open discussion around the ideas, questions, and processes behind the work.

The question of what it fundamentally means to be human has occupied the thoughtful and searching minds of our species for as long as we can remember. The rapid rise of Artificial Intelligence and digitalization has given this question new urgency, placing it at the heart of the Ars Electronica Festival 2026 under the title NEGOTIATING HUMANITY – FUTURE BEGINS. At its opening, Markus Poschner and the Bruckner Orchester Linz offer three compelling musical responses—the power of which unfold all the more powerfully in the spectacular acoustics of Austria’s largest church.

Negotiating with Water is a conference programme dedicated to our water imaginaries, and their legal and geopolitical realities and possibilities. The day frames water as a symptom of the socio-political context and a witness to different forms of human activities. Through the gaze of capital, water is a resource, a commodity we negotiate the rights to; at the same time, water carries traces of military, logistic or commercial activity.  
Current water imaginaries have led to our thirsty, expansion-driven culture becoming the site of multiple water-related crises—from the persistent freshwater
Curator Ana-Maria Carabelea gives a brief introduction to the topic and the day's program.

nameEn: Water through a Legal Lens: From Private Commodity to the Heritage of Mankind
descEn:
Stefano Burchi's talk unpacks the evolving legal conceptions of (fresh)water, from water as a private commodity to water as public property regulated by nation-states through national water laws, all the way to the water of boundary rivers, lakes and aquifers framed in treaties and agreements between multiple nation-states. These legal conceptions illustrate how nation-states and, more broadly, humans and societies relate to water.

Against this backdrop, the talk raises questions about the possibilities to upscale the legal discourse about water from the level of individuals, communities and

artists: Seila Fernandez Arconada (ES/DE), Laura Colmenares Guerra (CO/BE), Eleni Riga (GR)
descEn: The hydrocommons is the complex set of connections and permeations between human and non-human bodies of water. It does away with the illusory separation between the two and invites a reimaging of their relations outside capitalist or colonial frames that, in attempts to master, manage, engineer and contain this force of nature, position humanity in opposition to it. Bringing together artists Laura Colmenares Guerra and Seila Fernández Arconada, whose work currently focuses on the Amazon River and coastal territory of Esposende in Portugal as sites where different hydro social relations still

nameEn: The Flows of Law, Technology and Empire Through Water and History
descEn: The lecture will highlight how the entwinement of law and technology in the imperialist project plays out across bodies of water. Drawing on examples from different regions across the world, the lecture will provide insights into how colonialism and neocolonialism use law and technology as distinct techniques for the control and domination of waters and peoples.

artists: Ioana Vreme Moser (RO/DE), Robertina Šebjanič (SI), Jamie Allen (CA/CH), Ana-Maria Carabelea (INT)
descEn: Water both sustains life on the planet and threatens it by exceeding human control. These contradictory perceptions produce different relations to aquatic environments. This panel introduces another possible understanding of water and asks how might treating water as a medium—that carries messages about hydro social relations—change those relations? As a site of military, logistic, industrial or commercial activities, water senses, records, stores and transmits information. This panel discussion brings together artists Ioana Vreme Moser, Robertina Šebjanič and Jamie Allen to discuss how their

The creator of the YouTube channel Joseph’s Machines invites audiences behind the scenes to witness the creation of his viral videos. Watch in real time as he builds and films his biggest contraption yet: a human-scale morning routine machine where the performer is hoisted out of bed and propelled down a conveyor belt to be mechanically dressed and fed. In a society obsessed with productivity, the project is a joyful rebellion. By making simple tasks absurdly complicated, it celebrates the beauty of deliberate inefficiency and asks how to reclaim joy in a hyper-optimized world. The installatio

nameEn: NE #00: New Embeddings of/for Artistic Intelligence
artists: Enrique Encinas (ES/NO), Ida Jahr (NO), Synne Tollerud Bull (NO), Budhaditya Chattopadhyay (IN/NO), Jon Marius Aareskjold-Drecker (NO)
descEn: What forms of Artistic Intelligence become possible when artists, institutions, scientists and technologists organise around shared needs rather than disciplinary boundaries? How can AI support—not determine—those new collaborations? How do we build alternative infrastructures? This embedding event stages the question as an exchange: participants set down what they need, have built, and refuse with AI, cluster where their answers meet and trade concrete offers and requests into a shared ledger.

artists: Adrien Lucca (FR/BE), Ali Aiman Raza (IN/FR), Colas Schretter (BE), Marko Ilić (SI)
ticket: FESTIVALPASS+, FESTIVALPASS, DAYPASS, FESTIVAL WALK Ticket
descEn: The installation presents a living garden of plants and flowers beneath a custom, computer-controlled LED system. At regular intervals, the light turns bluish and the colors of the garden change completely: green foliage becomes brown or dark, while flowers appear brighter and stand out more strongly from the background. The transformation evokes how the elephant hawkmoth Deilephila elpenor may perceive the same plants through a color vision adapted to finding flowers among leaves. Based on scientific research, the work offers an informed translation rather than a claim to reproduce exactly wh

artists: Stefan Schartlmüller (AT), Lisa Praeg (AT), Martyna Lorenc (PL/AT), Letícia Carneiro (BR/AT), Stephanie Steyrer (AT)
descEn: Our democracies and constitutions rest on foundations that were originally laid in a very different world. As societies confront multiple, interconnected crises, many are asking whether our political systems are still equipped to meet today’s challenges. In this participatory workshop, IG Demokratie invites participants to explore the roots of the current crisis of democracy. What lies at its core? Political parties? Patriarchal structures? Escalating techno-capitalism? Or something else entirely? Through collective reflection and discussion, this workshop examines how political structures mig

nameEn: Next Singularity, the Intelligence of Life
nameDe: Next Singularity, the Intelligence of Life
ticket: FESTIVALPASS+, FESTIVALPASS, DAYPASS, Ars Electronica Center Ticket
descEn: For nearly 50 years, artist Yoichiro Kawaguchi has utilized his original “Growth Model” to explore biological forms and evolution through computer-generated art, blending natural mathematics with advanced technology. His work, drawing inspiration from the Cambrian explosion, argues that AI should be a creative partner for discovering human singularity rather than a tool for producing standardized, mediocre content.

ticket: WE GUIDE YOU Ticket Mini surcharge
descEn:
Hello Worlds! is a new exhibition at the Ars Electronica Center and the public outcome of the Future Humanity Project, an experimental research collaboration between Ars Electronica Futurelab and Toyota Motor Corporation’s Advanced R&D and Engineering Company.
Hello Worlds! is an open platform where artistic prototypes, interactive installations and visitor participation become part of an ongoing exploration of what it means to be human in an age of embodied AI.

artists: Valérie Siron (CH), Pablo Felley (CH), Théo Phildius (CH)
descEn: Owelle explores the relationship between identity, corporate culture and transformation through an immersive audiovisual performance. Audiences experience Owelle’s hardware-based live electronics, processed vocals and club-driven rhythms alongside Structurals’ real-time generative visuals and light scenography. Together, sound, light and narrative reshape the stage into a fictional corporate world where performance and space become inseparable.

ticket: FESTIVALPASS, DAYPASS, Ars Electronica Center Ticket, FESTIVALPASS+
descEn: There is a worm in our robot! At least its brain—because a worm’s nervous system can already be “copied” into a machine. But even the human brain, with all the data it produces, can already be read and interpreted well by using EEG and brain/computer interfaces, and can even control things outside the body.

nameEn: Hello Worlds! Behind the Prototype: Amplify Me – Visions
artists: Kawata Misako (JP), Takashi Nishimura (JP), Maria Pfeifer (AT), Takuma Suzuki (JP)
ticket: FESTIVALPASS+, FESTIVALPASS, DAYPASS, Ars Electronica Center Ticket
descEn:
What happens when technologies no longer stay in our pockets, but become part of our bodies, clothes, and everyday lives? Discover how Amplify Me – Visions combines speculative concepts with experimental prototypes to explore mobility, human augmentation, and what we might become. Developed together with Toyota Motor Corporation’s Advanced Design Division, these visions draw on expertise in automotive UX and industrial design to imagine new relationships between people, technology and movement.
Following selected Hello Worlds! tours, meet the people behind the prototypes and artworks and get a

nameDe: Hello Worlds! Behind the Prototype: Hybrid Thinking
ticket: DAYPASS, Ars Electronica Center Ticket, FESTIVALPASS, FESTIVALPASS+
descEn:
Explore if AI can help us think rather than simply providing answers with Futurelab’s Hybrid Thinking prototype in the Hello Worlds! exhibition.

Following selected Hello Worlds! tours, meet the people behind the prototypes and artworks and gain an inside look at what usually remains invisible: the research, experiments, technologies, design decisions and collaborative processes behind the works. This is your opportunity to ask questions and talk directly with the researchers, artists, designers and developers.

nameEn: Hello Worlds! Behind the Prototype: Resonance Loom
artists: Cailean Finn (IR), Misako Kawata (JP), Takashi Nishimura (JP), Maria Pfeifer (AT), Johannes Pöll (AT), Takuma Suzuki (JP)
ticket: DAYPASS, Ars Electronica Center Ticket, FESTIVALPASS, FESTIVALPASS+
descEn:
What do weaving and AI have in common? Meet the team behind the Resonance Loom and discuss how textile traditions, digital fabrication, human resonance and generative AI share a common language of patterns, instructions and algorithms. Through demonstrations and conversation, discover how centuries-old craft continues to inspire AI—and how AI, in turn, opens up new possibilities for textile thinking and crafting resonance.

Following selected Hello Worlds! tours, meet the people responsible for the prototypes and explore the research, technologies and design decisions behind the works. Ask questions and talk directly with the researchers, artists, designers and developers. No slides—just prototypes, people and conversation.

artists: Freddie Hong (KR), UJOO + LIMHEEYOUNG (KR), Cyntha Wieringa (NL/AT)
ticket: DAYPASS, Ars Electronica Center Ticket, FESTIVALPASS, FESTIVALPASS+
descEn: Following selected Hello Worlds! tours, meet the artists behind No Bird and Algorithms in Reflection. Gain an inside look at the ideas, artistic research, experiments and design decisions behind the works, and explore how they reflect on coexistence, shared habitats, ecological change and life in a world shared by humans, other species and increasingly autonomous technologies. No slides—just artworks, people and conversation.

nameEn: Hello Worlds! Behind the Prototype: Hello Worlds! System
artists: Friedrich Bachinger (AT), Kerstin Blätterbinder (AT), Peter Holzkorn (AT), Takuma Suzuki (JP)

Whether you're curious about the technology, the research, the design process, or the collaboration itself—ask us anything.

Explore how AI interprets people, and how those interpretations shape the way we understand ourselves.

descEn:
From the first concepts and prototypes to exhibition architecture and visitor experiences, explore how ideas are tested, iterated and transformed into something people can experience—and contribute to.

Following selected Hello Worlds! tours, meet the people behind the prototypes and artworks and gain an inside look at what usually remains invisible: the research, experiments, technologies, design decisions and collaborative processes behind the works. artists: Kyoko Kunoh (JP), Nicolas Naveau (FR/AT), Hideaki Ogawa (JP/AT), Maria Pfeifer (AT), Cyntha Wieringa (NL/AT), Jan Zuiderveld (NL)
descEn: The Future Humanity Project is an experimental research collaboration between Ars Electronica Futurelab and Toyota Motor Corporation’s Advanced R&D and Engineering Company. Through artistic research, experimental R&D and public participation, it explores future scenarios around AI and humanity. Hello Worlds! turns this research into a platform where visitors can experience, question and contribute to the research itself. Meet the team and join the conversation.

nameDe: Virusgeschichten, die wir in uns tragen
artists: Sonja Bäumel (AT), Helene Burtscher (AT), Christine Marizzi (AT)
descEn: What if we could meet viruses on a human scale? This hands-on workshop invites participants to encounter viruses through touch, embodiment and collective making. Participants exchange virus stories, engage with materials from contemporary virology and create life-sized virus forms. Through artistic exploration and dialogue, they reflect on their relationships with viruses, urban ecologies and shared futures. Each participant leaves with a photographic portrait of their handmade virus.

nameEn: Futurelab Networking: Feminist Tools for the Future
nameDe: Futurelab Networking: Feministische Werkzeuge für die Zukunft
artists: Bernadette Geißler (AT), Peter Holzkorn (AT), Susanne Kiesenhofer (AT), Anna Weiss (AT/DE)
descEn:
What practices help us collaborate when uncertainty, complexity and diverse perspectives become the norm? 
Feminist Tools for the Future is an open gathering for researchers, artists, designers, technologists and practitioners of all genders and fields to exchange experiences, share methods that work, and build new connections across disciplines. We look forward to seeing new faces and reconnecting with participants from last year's event! We invite you to connect, learn from each other and explore the tools we need to shape more inclusive and collaborative futures—together.

nameEn: Layers of Time: City Tour meets Media Arts (EN)
ticket: WE GUIDE YOU Ticket, WE GUIDE YOU Ticket surcharge
descEn: Discover Linz through the lens of Ars Electronica. This tour explores the historic festival venues, revealing their architectural and cultural significance—from monasteries and schools to museums. Wolfram Starczewski, city guide in Linz, together with Ars Electronica Festival Guides, creates a dialogue between the locations of the festival, their (historical) meaning and the artworks presented in the venues.

ticket: FESTIVALPASS+, FESTIVALPASS, DAYPASS, FESTIVAL WALK Ticket
descEn: Reality Screenshot is a hybrid performance based on [ The Frame ], reinterpreted through Domestic Data Streamers’ data visualization approach. The event presents a “Human Artificial Intelligence” made of flesh and bones, which observes and interprets everyday habits, curiosities and social tensions in public space. Blending street theater and data visualization, it invites audiences to reflect on perception while turning the city into a living stage for emotion, participation and discovery.

nameEn: AI for Social Impact – Negotiating Humanity in Times of Crisis
descEn:
Initiated in collaboration with CARE Austria, this conference explores how Artificial Intelligence can contribute to addressing humanitarian, social, and environmental challenges. Marking CARE Austria’s 80th anniversary, it builds on the momentum of the inaugural AI for Social Impact Award, presented this year as part of the Prix Ars Electronica, and extends its central question into a broader public conversation: how can AI be developed and deployed to strengthen humanitarian action in a rapidly changing world?

Against the backdrop of growing crises, armed conflicts, displacement, widening i

Andrea Barschdorf-Hager, CEO of CARE Austria and Gerfried Stocker, Artistic Director of Ars Electronica, open the day by reflecting on the collaboration between the two organizations and the shared questions that bring the worlds of humanitarian action, art, technology and innovation together.

Connecting to this year’s Ars Electronica Festival theme, NEGOTIATING HUMANITY they introduce the central questions of the day: How is our understanding of humanity changing in an age increasingly shaped by Artificial Intelligence? Who benefits from technological progress—and who risks being left behind

Hito Steyerl’s opening keynote sets the conceptual framework for AI for Social Impact – Negotiating Humanity in Times of Crisis. Drawing on her artistic and theoretical practice, she examines the shifting relationships between technology, power, human experience and collective agency. Connecting her critical engagement with digital technologies to questions of participation and social responsibility, she explores how AI is reshaping our understanding of humanity and what new forms of solidarity and collective action might emerge in response. She invites us to approach AI not simply as a techno

nameEn: One in seven: Austria 1946, Uganda 2026—who gets to be a person in a crisis?
descEn:
Not all crises are seen equally—and neither are the people living through them. This keynote explores how visibility, data and global attention shape our understanding of humanitarian crises and asks what this means as Artificial Intelligence becomes increasingly influential in humanitarian and social impact work.

Beginning with the history of the CARE Package in post-war Austria, the keynote connects past and present experiences of crisis and reflects on the agency of those affected. Drawing on contemporary examples, including Sudan and Ukraine, it asks whether AI systems—often unintentional

artists: Jerry Tuan (US), Archana Prasad (IN), moderated by Andrea Barschdorf-Hager (AT)
descEn:
Who gets to shape the future of Artificial Intelligence—and whose voices risk being left out?

Bringing together perspectives from technology and humanitarian practice, this conversation explores how AI can be developed in ways that are equitable, inclusive and accountable. Archana Prasad, founder of http://gooey.ai/, brings the perspective of a technologist and entrepreneur working at the intersection of AI and social impact, while Jerry Tuan, CEO of CARE USA, contributes insights from global humanitarian practice. The conversation is moderated by Andrea Barschdorf-Hager.

nameEn: AI for Social Impact Award: Insights from the Jury & Introduction to the Initiative
descEn:
How can Artificial Intelligence contribute to meaningful social change—and what does it take for an AI-driven project to create impact that is not only innovative, but also responsible, inclusive and sustainable?

This session introduces the AI for Social Impact Award, its vision, objectives and selection process. The award seeks to recognize initiatives that use AI to address pressing social and humanitarian challenges while placing people, communities and ethical responsibility at the center of technological development.

Drawing on their experience as part of the jury process, Andrea and Ge

nameEn: AI for Social Impact Award: The award winning projects
artists: Eniola Benson (NG), Shadi Henchiri (TN), Oluwaseun Kayode (NG), Esther Kimani (KE), Rafael Lozano-Hemmer (MX)
descEn:
What does it look like when Artificial Intelligence is designed not simply to innovate, but to respond to real social and humanitarian needs?

This session presents the five winning initiatives of the AI for Social Impact Initiative, showcasing projects that combine technological innovation with measurable social impact, ethical design and meaningful engagement with the communities they aim to serve. Spanning education, agriculture, historical justice, migrant health and maternal care, the projects demonstrate very different ways in which AI can become a tool for social change.

The three Awar

artists: Eniola Benson (NG), Shadi Henchiri (TN), Milagros Miceli (AR), Vivian Tabeth (EG) moderated by Reshma Khan (KE)
descEn:
Bringing the symposium to a close, this panel explores what it means to keep humanity at the center of Artificial Intelligence in humanitarian action. It brings together perspectives from AI innovation, humanitarian practice, critical data studies and community-centered implementation to examine both the potential and the tensions that arise when AI is developed and deployed in contexts of vulnerability and crisis.

The discussion features Eniola Benson and Shadi Henchiri, Grand Prize winners of the AI for Social Impact Initiative, who bring insights from developing AI solutions with and for v

nameEn: From AI for Good to AI for Action
descEn: The closing remarks summarize the key insights of the symposium and emphasize the transition from dialogue to implementation. Andrea Barschdorf-Hager highlights the shared responsibility of institutions, technology developers, artists, humanitarian organizations and communities to transform principles into concrete action and sustained collaboration.

nameEn: Contested Futures – Europe Negotiating Power, Machine, Labour
artists: Curated by Francesca Bria and José Luis de Vicente
descEn:
If being human has always been a process of negotiation, then this day asks the following question: How does Europe negotiate its future, when so much of that future is now built into the machines, the infrastructures of modern power, underpinning our collective life?

It is not a settled question. It is not a friendly one. The same drive for digital sovereignty can also build public infrastructure held in common—or a militarized arsenal dressed in the aesthetics of a new authoritarianism. The future is contested. Europe has to choose, out in the open.

So this is not a conference. It is an ar

The third edition of the Ars Electronica Campus Award aims to recognize the most outstanding project presented within this year’s Ars Electronica Campus Exhibition, which highlights not only emerging talents but also the educational institutions that support them. A jury formed of three renowned experts in the field of media arts will inspect the projects and select five Honorary Mentions and one Grand Prize, which includes €2.000 in prize money.

The Ars Electronica Campus Exhibition is a joint initiative between Ars Electronica and the University of Arts in Linz which has been going for more

nameEn: Networking Event Gwangyang – Linz Media Arts Exchange 2026
descEn: This networking event introduces the third edition of the Gwangyang—Linz Media Arts Exchange, an initiative dedicated to artistic collaboration and knowledge sharing between South Korea and Austria. Meet the curators and artists of this program and be part when Korean artist Soh Boram and Austrian artist Heike Waldner-Kaltenbrunner will each receive the grant to exhibit their work in Gwangyang and Linz. The event is open to artists, curators and festival visitors interested in international collaboration and cross-cultural media art practice.

nameEn: Artists’ Reception hosted by the Slovenian Embassy in Austria
descEn:
Ars Electronica Festival, the Slovenian Embassy in Austria, the Slovenian Cultural and Information Centre SKICA Wien and the Municipality of Celje warmly invite artists, curators and culture practicioners to join us for the Artists’ Reception—an opportunity to mingle, connect and exchange with fellow professionals from the field of media arts.

The event will also celebrate the Slovenian artist Robertina Šebjanič who has received an Award of Distinction in the category Interactive Art+ of the Prix Ars Electronica for her timely work Echoes of the Abyss, which will also be presented at the fest

nameEn: Minimal Music Highlights by Maki Namekawa
ticket: DAYPASS, FESTIVALPASS, FESTIVALPASS+, FESTIVAL WALK Ticket, FESTIVAL WALK Ticket surcharge
descEn: Maki Namekawa is one of the leading pianists of our time. The Japanese artist has earned an international reputation for her outstanding interpretations of both the classical and contemporary repertoire. She has enjoyed a particularly close relationship with the Ars Electronica Festival in Linz for many years, where she regularly appears with innovative programs and interdisciplinary projects. At the C. Bechstein Centrum Linz, Maki Namekawa will perform in two concerts. While celebrated as a classical pianist, she presents a deliberately contemporary programme featuring works by Hania Rani, Ch

nameDe: Wo ist denn der Ton versteckt?
descEn:
The C. Bechstein Centrum Linz invites children on a journey into the world of pianos, full of opportunities to discover, explore and try things out for themselves.
What does the sound of a piano string have in common with the beating wings of a bee? And how many elephants would it take to create the right tension for a piano string? Through playful experiments, children learn how a piece of wood becomes a musical instrument, how piano strings are wound and how sound is ultimately created inside a piano.
Together with experienced piano makers, they examine the individual components of a grand p

We warmly invite you to a special Latin America networking event—an opportunity for artists, cultural professionals and anyone interested in connecting with the vibrant South American creative community at the Ars Electronica Festival.
This informal gathering is co-hosted by Hauptplatz 23 and the Ars Electronica Festival.
We are especially looking forward to welcoming artists and professionals from Chile, Latin America and beyond. We look forward to sharing it with you.

Ars Electronica and Creative Europe Desk Austria will once again be hosting the Creative Europe Get Together, an event that brings together European partners from across a variety of sectors in a friendly environment, where attendees can meet and share perspectives. As the EU’s flagship program supporting the cultural, creative and audiovisual sectors, Creative Europe has promoted numerous meaningful programs, such as MEDIA, with a focus on the film industry—and this year we will be celebrating its 35th anniversary. We look forward to welcoming our European partners to celebrate this milestone

nameEn: Networking Event hosted by the Creative Industries Fund NL
descEn:
The Creative Industries Fund NL, CIIIC and Ars Electronica Festival warmly invite you to this networking gathering, where you will have the opportunity to get to know more about five consortia dedicated to artistic and design research for immersive experiences consisting of makers, producers, cultural institutions and researchers.

This event will offer a closer look at the ongoing multi-annual activity programmes of the consortia, while creating space to meet potential European partners working at the intersection of creativity, technology and innovation.
Join us for an inspiring gathering to

Electronics meets improvised piano; dance, film, poetry and more.
From the performative film El Cultivo de la Mente with live piano accompaniment to the Linz-based electronic music acts The Unsettled and Tomá Ivanov, this year’s program at the C. Bechstein Piano Centrum Linz brings together a wide range of artistic expressions. Live improvised piano serves as the common thread, merging film, dance, spoken word, electronic music, contemporary soundscapes and immersive audiovisual experiences.

nameEn: NaturArchy: Curating Across Art, Science, Policymaking
artists: Caterina Benincasa (IT), Ingeborg Reichle (DE), Claudia Schnugg (AT)
descEn: This Town Hall event presents NaturArchy as a case study for working across art, science and policymaking. Drawing on the recent publication and the 14 art-science-policy projects it documents, this event provides a space for participants to share their own projects and reflect on how these practices affect decision-making processes. Discussions will reflect on curatorial practices, science-for-policy, governance and transdisciplinarity.

Is soil alive? Investigating this seemingly simple question, this workshop will enable participants to discover life in the dark ground below. Evolving from scientists who experimentally search for signs of life in soil, participants will embody various forms of soiled life and artistically express their present and immanent reality. Bridging these worlds, the workshop will provide scientific and creative materials so that the complex relevance of soil can be encountered from individual angles.

nameEn: KEPLER SALON EXTRA EXTERN: SHOW ME YOUR FACE
artists: Johannes Pröll (AT), Mihaela Kavdanska (BG/AT), Dilmana Yordanova (BG/RO), Cornelia Lehner (AT)
descEn: KEPLER SALON EXTRA EXTERN explores the interplay between genetics, experience and identity, questioning deterministic views of human behavior, particularly violence. A two-channel video installation using AI, moving images, text and the sonification of genomic data makes the phenotype tangible as a process of becoming between biological potential and lived experience. The discussion features Johannes Pröll, Mika Kavdanska and Dilmana Yordanova with host Cornelia Lehner.

ticket: FESTIVALPASS+, FESTIVALPASS, DAYPASS, Ars Electronica Center Ticket
descEn: vvvv is a visual live-programming environment suited to large-scale interactive installations, making it ideal for Ars Electronica’s Deep Space 8K, with its dual 16×9 metre stereoscopic screens, real-time floor tracking and immersive potential. This session demonstrates live-programming Deep Space 8K through demos exploring key features of vvvv and the space, offering artists a starting point for developing their own interactive works.

artists: Faculty of Medicine of the Johannes Kepler University Linz (AT)
descEn:
The JKU MED Campus is one of the central festival hubs of the Ars Electronica Festival 2026. As a site for modern medical education, research and patient care, it demonstrates that the future does not only begin with technology and digital systems, but also with medical research and clinical practice.

With JKU medFOCUS, the Faculty of Medicine at Johannes Kepler University Linz invites visitors to experience firsthand current developments in medicine, teaching and research. At JKU medSPACE, university clinics present virtual anatomy and offer new perspectives on the heart, brain, abdomen, sho

ticket: WE GUIDE YOU Ticket, WE GUIDE YOU Ticket surcharge

We show how innovative concepts emerge from initial ideas, questions and technological possibilities and how they are transformed into immersive experiences through creative processes, interdisciplinary collaboration and the use of cutting-edge technologies. Visitors will discover how content, data and complex interrelationships can become interactive narratives—and how visions can be transformed into tangible spaces that inform, move and inspir

We show how innovative concepts emerge from initial ideas, questions and technological possibilities and how they are transformed into immersive experiences through creative processes, interdisciplinary collaboration and the use of cutting-edge technologies. Visitors will discover how content, data and complex interrelationships can become interactive narratives—and how visions can be transformed into tangible spaces that inform, move and inspir

nameEn: Agentic Systems as a New Form of Dialogue
nameDe: Agentische Systeme als neue Form des Dialogs
descEn: Agentic systems can be much more than mere information providers: they engage in dialogue with people, respond to individual interests and at the same time draw attention to topics and realms of knowledge that may not yet be visible within a particular context. Using the agentic systems in the Ars Electronica Solutions showcase as an example, we explore how new interfaces, the visualization of digital agents and lifelike forms of communication create a dynamic, dialogical approach to knowledge—and how humans and machines can discover new perspectives together.

nameEn: Empathetic Interfaces and New Forms of Knowledge Transfer
nameDe: Empathische Interfaces und neue Formen der Wissensvermittlung
descEn: How can interfaces and interaction models be designed to make knowledge not only accessible, but also emotionally and sensorially tangible? This deep dive offers insights into the development process—from initial concept and the design of communication channels and interactions to technical implementation. Using the Ars Electronica Solutions – A Glimpse Behind the Scenes as an example, it demonstrates how empathic technologies emerge and how innovative forms of communication can open up new ways of engaging with complex content.

ticket: FESTIVALPASS+, FESTIVALPASS, DAYPASS, Ars Electronica Center Ticket
descEn: At Deep Space Selection, we present several times a day a changing selection from our diverse program, which we’ve been continuously developing since 2009. Visitors can look forward to exciting stories and immersive experiences spanning media art, science and technology.

ticket: FESTIVALPASS+, FESTIVALPASS, DAYPASS, FESTIVAL WALK Ticket
descEn: Who is jumping, Jack? is an interactive kinetic installation that translates visitors’ arm movements into mechanical sequences. These gestures are captured in real time and transmitted to servo-controlled corkscrews, creating an immediate physical response to the visitors’ actions. The installation explores the relationship between action and imitation. As the visitors’ movements are translated into mechanical responses, the distinction between performer and reflection begins to blur. Beneath the playful surface lies repetition and the question of control—movements that become part of a system

Anatomy for Everyone invites audiences to explore the human body in an immersive virtual anatomy theater. Led by JKU Professor Franz Fellner, giant 3D visualizations generated from CT and MRI data reveal organs, muscles, vessels and bones in remarkable detail. Visitors experience the body layer by layer, discovering how immersive visualization and cinematic rendering are transforming medicine, medical education and scientific communication while making complex anatomy accessible to everyone.

ticket: FESTIVALPASS+, FESTIVALPASS, DAYPASS, Ars Electronica Center Ticket
descEn: Alisa Martynova’s residency at the Ars Electronica Futurelab in 2026 explores perception, consciousness and the unstable nature of truth through an immersive projection environment developed for Deep Space 8K. Drawing from studies on binocular rivalry, entropy and the default neural network, this work examines how the brain constructs reality from fragmented and ambiguous visual information. Dissonant Stereoscopy places the audience within sensory thresholds where the visual system attempts to disambiguate unstable inputs—seeing emerges from the interplay of memory, past experience and interpr

Since 2017, Time’s Up has been researching, developing and building Turnton2047, bringing it to life through immersive environments. At its heart is a transformed economy that prioritizes the wellbeing of people and the planet while challenging existing concentrations of wealth and power. It also explores the potential of marine regeneration to restore damaged ecosystems.
Developed in collaboration with Theater Phönix, this immersive audio experience invites audiences into the everyday lives of Turnton2047’s inhabitants. Across seven listening stations, visitors take on the role of guests at t

descEn: Students enrolled in the degree program Time-based and Interactive Media Art at the University of Arts Linz have developed interactive games tailored specifically to the needs and interests of our youngest visitors. Colorful, action-packed and super fun—here, children can actively engage in imaginative worlds and experience digital technologies in a playful way.

artists: Chih Pui Yi (HK), Ao Kin Man (HK)
descEn: This presentation explores how technology shapes perception of urban nature. Reimagining certain Hong Kong flowers, such as frangipani, jacaranda and purple azalea, through immersive algorithmic visuals, it introduces evolving digital ecosystems between organic growth and digital permanence. Rooted in Hong Kong’s dense urban ecology, the artists offer global audiences new perspectives on biodiversity, environmental awareness and how art and technology can deepen attention to overlooked nature in life.

artists: Toyota’s Frontier Research Center (JP), Ars Electronica Futurelab (AT)
ticket: FESTIVALPASS+, FESTIVALPASS, DAYPASS, Ars Electronica Center Ticket
descEn: This experience invites participants to test Bubble Talk, an experimental AI-guided exhibition tour. Bubble Talk creates personalized tours based on visitors’ interests while introducing unexpected connections to unfamiliar artworks. Participants explore the Connected Earth exhibition in the Ars Electronica Center, share feedback and contribute to research on how AI can help museums foster curiosity, learning and dialogue beyond personal information bubbles.

Explore Hello Worlds! together with the people behind the project. Researchers, artists, designers, developers, and collaboration partners guide you through the exhibition, sharing the ideas, technologies and research behind the works—and, if you like, continue the conversation afterwards.

Hello Worlds! is the public outcome of the Future Humanity Project, an experimental research collaboration between Ars Electronica Futurelab and Toyota Motor Corporation’s Advanced R&D and Engineering Company. Hello Worlds! is an open platform where artistic prototypes, interactive installations and visitor

The monotype printmaking technique is demonstrated in this workshop. Believed to have been invented by Giovanni Benedetto Castiglione in the 17th century, it has since become a popular medium for artists seeking to create unique and highly expressive works. Monotype encourages spontaneity and experimentation, fostering creativity, flexibility and an openness to unexpected results.

nameEn: Expert Tour: Meet the Features Partners
ticket: WE GUIDE YOU Ticket, WE GUIDE YOU Ticket surcharge
descEn: The Ars Electronica Features Exhibition showcases a carefully curated selection of international projects at the intersection of art and technology. Sixteen partners explore what it means to act, decide and make meaning at a moment when the boundaries between human intention, algorithmic process and biological life have become difficult to locate. Christl Baur, Head of the Ars Electronica Festival and Program Director, provides an insight into the collaborations behind the exhibition and introduces you to the partner institutions and artists involved.

nameEn: Layers of Time: City Tour meets Media Arts (DE)
ticket: WE GUIDE YOU Ticket, WE GUIDE YOU Ticket surcharge
descEn: Discover Linz through the lens of Ars Electronica. This tour explores the historic festival venues, revealing their architectural and cultural significance—from monasteries and schools to museums. Wolfram Starczewski, city guide in Linz, together with Ars Electronica Festival Guides, creates a dialogue between the locations of the festival, their (historical) meaning and the artworks presented in the venues.

nameEn: OK QUARTER: WE GUIDE YOU Meeting Point
descEn:
As one of the three main hubs of this year's festival, the OK QUARTER presents deep thematic insights, interactive projects, as well as a chance to explore the city of Linz.
The different guided tours in OK QUARTER take you on a journey through the exhibitions FESTIVAL WALK: Negotiating the Real and Negotiating Beyond Humanity.

nameEn: DANUBE TRIANGLE: University of Arts Linz
descEn: From Wednesday to Saturday, the University of Arts Linz invites you to explore their exhibition within a guided tour and and immerse yourself in the highly varied student projects and thematic explorations.

nameEn: Expert Tour FESTIVAL WALK: Christl Baur (EN)
ticket: WE GUIDE YOU Ticket surcharge, WE GUIDE YOU Ticket
descEn: The exhibition Negotiating the Real – The Desire to Believe asks which systems of belief and worldviews underpin our social order—and, in turn, shape our understanding of what it means to be human. Christl Baur, Head of the Ars Electronica Festival and Program Director, takes you on a tour along the FESTIVAL WALK. Together, you explore the thematical threads of the exhibition across its different venues in the heart of Linz.

nameEn: Spotlight Tour FESTIVAL WALK: Negotiating the Real (DE/Austrian Sign Language)
nameDe: Spotlight Tour FESTIVAL WALK: Negotiating the Real (DE/Gebärdensprache)
ticket: WE GUIDE YOU Ticket, WE GUIDE YOU Ticket surcharge
descEn: How do we negotiate reality? How does community form, both among us humans and with other living beings? What systems of belief shape the conflicts we face in this process and what role does technology play? This guided tour takes you on a journey along the FESTIVAL WALK through the heart of Linz visiting a school, a museum, a hospital and several churches, connecting infrastructures of our daily life with artistic projects.

artists: Deep Space Community (INT),  Ars Electronica Solutions (AT)
ticket: FESTIVALPASS+, FESTIVALPASS, DAYPASS, Ars Electronica Center Ticket
descEn:
Deep Space is an open platform, and its possibilities grow through the people who create for it. This session brings together members of the global Deep Space Community to present what they are currently developing—from interactive applications and stereoscopic 3D experiences to video productions and entirely new formats.
The projects span science communication, art and cultural heritage, medicine and biology and the future of education. Each offers a different perspective on what immersive space can do and who it can reach. Beyond the finished results, participants share the processes behind

On September 11 and 12, 2026, students and young talents aged 14 and up will develop digital projects using festival data and open data from the City of Linz at the AI Hackathon.

We are looking for approaches that open up new perspectives on the city and the festival—from smart guides and interactive maps to storytelling tools, artistic projects or completely new ideas. No coding experience is required. AI tools and experienced mentors will support participants in testing out their ideas, developing them further and turning them into concrete projects. descEn: Protect Our Planet and Climate—a Science Experience by Ars Electronica Solutions and the European Space Agency. Over the course of 30 minutes, we will cover a variety of topics from our home planet to planetary defence: Earth observation and climate data reveal our planet’s current state, ESA satellites deliver the facts and the Hera mission provides the platform for an important conversation about how we defend ourselves against asteroids. From awareness to agency,  join us for a compact, concrete and live discussion with ESA experts.

artists: Hakuhodo Inc. (JP), Hakuhodo Inc. Sei-katsu-sha insight R&D Institute (JP), Ars Electronica Futurelab (AT)
descEn:
Hello Futures Manifesto is an interactive installation that turns personal visions of the future into vivid posters. Each poster becomes part of a collective manifesto, making futures tangible, shareable and open to negotiation. As third iteration of Citizen Manifesto by Ars Electronica Futurelab and Hakuhodo Inc., the work explores how generative AI can support open dialogue, civic participation and collective creativity.

The Flood the Zone with Courage program presents a series of interventions, each lasting no more than seven minutes. Through diverse artistic approaches, these interventions reimagine protest, exploring the many forms it can take and inviting audiences into concentrated moments of action that continuously shift in both form and intensity. This year’s program explores many of the challenges that shape our everyday lives. Some interventions respond to the climate crisis and explore how technological and social developments shape the way we perceive the world. Others explore the relationship betw

nameEn: Press Start – RADICAL GAMING Performance at Main Square
artists: Rajiv Bhagwanbali (NL), Anna Hazarian (UA), Philipp “Flip” Kroll (AT), Alina Lugovskaya (RU)
descEn: Press Start is a performance that involves dance, music and spoken word. It explores the challenges faced by a young individual who is pulled into a radical online universe through gaming, where they encounter manipulation, controlling behavior and bullying.

nameEn: Glitch & Leak: Overflowing Bodies in Public Space at Main Square
artists: FIFTITU% Vernetzungsstelle für Frauen* in Kunst und Kultur in OÖ (AT)
descEn:
On September 11th, 2026, Domgasse and Linz’s Main Square will become Run(a)way —a performative collective intervention in public space.
Errors and disruptions are welcome. They interrupt the smooth functioning of a capitalist, heteronormative and racialized world. The body as a glitch, the costume as a glitch, the performance as a glitch, the space as a glitch. Something that eludes optimization and categorization. nameEn: Listen To Each Oida: Dalia Ahmed
descEn:
FM4, the Austrian public broadcaster ORF’s radio station for young audiences, connects social discourse with pop culture. Music at the close of each of the two festival days carries the themes discussed throughout the day—democracy, courage, the culture of conflict—into a pop-cultural format: music has historically been a central medium of protest, and here it is both reflected upon and celebrated. The main square thus remains an open space of encounter into the evening, where social dialogue and shared experience come together.

Dalia Ahmed is a DJ, radio host and music editor at Radio FM4, w

artists: Sofie Burgos-Thorsen (DK), Andreas Refsgaard (DK), Anna Minta (DE), Bernd Ziegler (DE)
ticket: DAYPASS, FESTIVALPASS, FESTIVALPASS+, FESTIVAL WALK Ticket
descEn: Wicked Mirror transforms public debate into an encounter with one’s AI-generated double. A photorealistic clone adopts the visitor’s face, voice and arguments—only to challenge them. In conversation with the artists, researchers of the Catholic Private University Linz explore how AI reshapes identity, empathy and democratic dialogue. From the perspectives of art history and theology, they ask how aesthetic experience can foster reflection, disagreement and new ways of negotiating what it means to be human in an increasingly AI-mediated world.

nameEn: Robertina Šebjanič – Journal from the TARA expedition vessel: Echoes of the Abyss
artists: Robertina Šebjanič (SI), Ilaria Hoppe (DE), Martin Koci (CZ)
ticket: FESTIVAL WALK Ticket, FESTIVALPASS+, FESTIVALPASS, DAYPASS
descEn: Echoes of the Abyss addresses the overlooked issue of chemical weapons dumped on the ocean floor. These remnants of past conflicts threaten biodiversity, alter water chemistry and act as environmental time bombs. Based on research conducted during the artist’s expedition with the Tara Ocean Foundation in the Baltic Sea, the talk hosted by researchers from the Catholic Private University Linz explores the intersection of artistic research, marine science, history and ecological destruction.

nameEn: Expert Tour FESTIVAL WALK: Elisabeth Falkensteiner (EN)
ticket: WE GUIDE YOU Ticket surcharge, WE GUIDE YOU Ticket
descEn: Join co-curator of the FESTIVAL WALK Elisabeth Falkensteiner for a guided tour. Along the tour, we encounter a polyphonic exhibition parcours that brings together diverse realities and ways of imagining the world. The works on view explore how truth, humanity and community are governed, imagined, simulated and experienced. The tour reveals how the production of truth claims, social norms and collective identities is deeply intertwined with the institutional spaces in which they are negotiated and sustained.

Meet Joseph Herscher, the artist behind Joseph’s Machines—elaborate chain-reaction contraptions that turn everyday objects into unlikely collaborators. In this Q&A session, Herscher talks about the ideas, engineering and endless trial-and-error behind his machines—and what draws him, again and again, to the most complicated way of doing the simplest things.

The Ars Electronica Festival brings together people who are shaping the future—with creativity, technology and new perspectives. This is exactly where the Canon Creator Lab comes in: it is a place where ideas become visible and visitors not only learn about modern imaging technologies but can experience them firsthand. Whether photography, videography or social content—in the Touch & Try area, cameras, lenses and printing solutions can be tried out directly. Canon experts are on hand for questions and personal advice, while the Photo Zone invites visitors to get creative and share their own co

artists: Mushon Zer Aviv (IL/CH), A Land For All – Two States One Homeland (IL/PS)
ticket: FESTIVALPASS+, FESTIVALPASS, DAYPASS, FESTIVAL WALK Ticket
descEn: Future Screenshots asks: What if we could reach into a possible future, unlock a phone and take a screenshot? In this workshop, audiences draft messages, maps, prompts and posts from worlds that do not yet exist. By mapping, comparing and presenting these everyday digital traces, the workshop explores how our anticipation of change and stability shapes our technological and political imagination—and how the futures people imagine together can become the futures they begin to create.

nameEn: Updating the Great Acceleration Charts: New Signals for a Changing World
artists: Alexander Damianos (GB/GR), John Palmesino (GB/IT), Ann-Sofi Rönnskog (GB/FI), Robertina Šebjanič (SI)
descEn: The Great Acceleration charts made planetary change perceptible and in doing so, changed how humans and nonhumans perceive, feel and act. This workshop treats those affects as data. After a brief introduction to the charts, participants work in small groups to trace how the curves ripple through their own lives and organisations and to translate these ripples into candidate signals for an expanded chart set. The results are shown in the Studiotopia exhibition Updating the Great Acceleration Charts.

The tour reveals how the production of truth claims, social norms and collective identities is deeply intertwined with the institutional spaces in which they are negotiated and sustained.

descEn: Cultural heritage sites are fragile, from threats like devastating fires to utter destruction by armed conflicts. What role can technology and art play in conservation efforts for world heritage? In this panel discussion between the creators behind Unbreakable Ukraine and Ars Electronica, we even want to go one step further: What role can technology and art play in moving from conservation or reconstruction to cultural resilience? Memory becomes a conscious act of resistance, underlining the importance of taking responsibility when history—and thus our future—is under threat.

This workshop explores how femininity can be consciously embodied and made visible as a language of presence, confidence and self-expression. It is led by Black Pearl, protagonist of the Extended Reality work OYA, which traces her journey of becoming—a reflection on release, liberation and returning to the self. After a warm-up and a short introduction to Ballroom culture and its roots in New York, participants practice European Runway: poses, walking, turns and a short battle.

Polaris, the latest Pianographique production by Maki Namekawa and Cori O'Lan, offers a distinctive take on the music of Philip Glass, whose compositions have become, for many, a timeless soundtrack of our present moment. Drawing on piano arrangements by Philip Glass himself as well as by Michael Riesman, Maki Namekawa has curated a unique program for this evening, one that speaks directly to the festival’s theme.

descEn:
Sound Campus – Listening Underground explores the movement beneath the surface. It considers the ongoing, divergent processes which are felt but not always seen. To submerge opens up new modes of attention and multi-sensory listening that change our relation with the surrounding.

Flow in circle is a performance for water, feedback and body. While exploring the unknown space in both physical, acoustical and metaphorical way, it asks the question: can we understand the foreign world? How can we interact with it and establish communication in unusual conditions? The piece stages an encounter between human perception and an acoustic environment that remains partially inaccessible.

Thiann is the Taiwanese word for “listening.” This live AV performance explores local identity by collecting mundane, yet unique Taiwanese acoustics—such as rural vendor broadcasts and vehicular speed-limit alerts. Through experimental remixing and electronic deformation, the artist deconstructs these everyday social cues and collective sonic memories into an immersive noise-driven soundscape.

Gao Huang is an interactive audiovisual performance that uses motion capture and image recognition to transform the performer’s movements into real-time sound and visuals. Drawing on the “Gao Huang” acupoint as a metaphor for accumulated bodily
tension, the work makes visible and audible the hidden friction, imbalance and persistent aches shaped by contemporary patterns of labor and stillness.

Subkutan explores the physicality of sound, space and the body. Performed exclusively on subwoofers, it works with sub-bass frequencies that are felt as much as heard, amplifying bodily sensation and pushing beyond auditory thresholds. Trembling, floating, soothing and arousing, this performance slips under the skin to create an immersive experience. By engaging environmental resonances and reflections, it sets bodies in motion and synchronizes audiences within an altered spatial reality.

Brought together in Cyprus during the COVID pandemic, 1=1 and NEVSS blend dance music with experimental elements and ambient textures. Their shared background is rooted in underground culture and shaped by experiences across European cities.
For this special DJ set, NEVSS is traveling from Cyprus to reunite with Linz-based 1=1.

The project explores how artificial sound reshapes listening in a world saturated with human-made and mediated sound. Through a live audiovisual performance, AI-generated birdsong is processed through granular synthesis, while sine waves and noise create tension between natural and synthetic textures. Real-time visuals respond to sound, forming an unstable field where listening becomes uncertain and transformed.

de-attractor is a generative audiovisual performance visualizing the decomposition of geometric order. Through TouchDesigner, the audience observes a spherical point cloud fracturing into erratic particles. Sonically, pre-arranged audio collides with unpredictable, live modular synthesizer patching. This shifting auditory landscape parallels the visual distortion, enveloping the viewer in a chaotic dissipation that probes the fragile boundary between structural stability and collapse.

Electrosensitivity sound performance uses custom high-frequency resonant generators and the author's hand-controllable plasma-discharge instruments to explore the gap between electricity's crucial role in our bodies and our inability to sense electric and magnetic fields. This gap allows us to use the electromagnetic processes as the core of modern technology, which is rapidly changing our environments and their human and non-human inhabitants, in ways that remain to be revealed.
