A live performance combining biological material and sound synthesis. What counts as “dirty” or “pure” when biological matter becomes an active sonic agent? The project uses mold as a living resistor, translating bio-activity into sound through interaction with electronic circuits. The audience experiences a performative sonic system in real time, exploring how biological systems can reveal marginalized conditions of existence.

FACE SHIFT is a live performance and collaborative DJ set emerging from qujOchÖ’s ongoing project Rhizomaniacs. The performance is developed as a duo by I-ID and Mascha Illich. Moving through live mixing, analogue synthesis, broken rhythms, noise and spontaneous sonic interventions, FACE SHIFT is shaped by real-time sensation and the connection between mind and body. It explores how sound affects perception, emotion and movement, shifting between intensity, tension and release.

Parasomnia is a performance for self-built instruments and electronics exploring the delirious states of light sleep, where perception becomes unstable and the boundary between reality and imagination dissolves. It invites the audience to immerse themselves in a shifting sonic environment where authenticity, memory and dreams become increasingly difficult to distinguish.

Meshes present a new work for percussion and electronics that examines the boundaries between the physical and the computational. Kolmbauer approaches the drum set through unconventional implement and extended techniques. Sounds are captured-submitted to real-time electronic processing, rendering the intimate audible and the incidental compositional. Jociūtė works with synthesizers and electronics as analog control interfaces and effects to receive, transform and redirect this material.

This project presents an experimental electroacoustic folk performance set within its own mythological world. Through music, poetic imagery and ritual-like compositional forms, it invites the audience into a garden where both beauty and darkness reside. The project aims to create a space for contemplation, memory and imagination, exploring mythology as a living language for the present moment.

Meditative Chaos is a live sonic journey through states of attention, resonance and transformation. Drawing on practices of deep listening, feedback systems and electronic sound synthesis, DEEP THROAT constructs an immersive environment where fragile balances emerge between contemplation and disruption. The performance invites audiences to navigate this soundscape, revealing chaos not as disorder but as a space of heightened perception and collective listening.

nameEn: On Forecasting Monsters by Kairos TV
descEn: Kairos TV is a collaborative project initiated by Marie-Andrée Pellerin and Stanisław Welbel, using the format of a weather channel for artistic and critical purposes. The performance presents a fictional daily weather program in which extreme weather phenomena are embodied by the figure of the monster. The visual content, built from found footage video is complemented by live sound performance created by the duo, with synthesizers and samples.

nameEn: Feeling Virtual: An Archive of Touch
ticket: FESTIVALPASS+, FESTIVALPASS, DAYPASS, FESTIVAL WALK Ticket
descEn:
This installation offers tactile access to costumes and props from the Salzburg Festival Archive. By critically examining our “Look, Don't Touch” culture, the artist draws on disabled ways of knowing the world through touch, bending XR technology to feel rather than just see virtual worlds.
The installation comprises the XR artwork Archive of Touch (7–10 min, DE, EN, Closed Captions), which invites visitors to experience archival materials through vibrations, sounds, visuals and tactile descriptions. A companion video (5 min, DE, Closed Captions EN, ÖGS) provides auditory and visual glimpses i

In this workshop, we attune to the earth’s body alongside our own, exploring how environmental loss, ecological grief and planetary suffering are felt in our nervous systems and in our bodies, and how they affect our sense of belonging. Drawing on the concept of inter-being, we expand the notion of pain beyond the individual. When forests burn, species vanish and the world heats up. Where does that solastalgia land in you? Please join us in a practice of listening, dissolving and recognizing ourselves in the wound of the world.

The Live Cinema Lab is a participatory film installation that invites participants to actively immerse themselves in the world of filmmaking. The focus is not on the final result, but on the creative process itself: How does a scene emerge? How do decisions, encounters and perspectives shape a story? Participants step into a role and develop a short film scene together with a professional acting partner on site. They experience a glimpse of everyday life on a film set, from preparation and acting to directing, camera, sound and costume. The scene is explored, reflected on and transformed. The

PULS explores the boundaries and peculiarities of our perception through the use of sensory extremes. Flashing light, total darkness and brief audiovisual impulses repeating at rates between rhythm and tone will manipulate our sense of time and space. The installation will overwhelm us, create illusions, force us to change perspectives or even bring us to different state of consciousness.

artists: Processing Foundation (US), Clinic for Open Source Arts (US), vvvv (DE)
descEn:
Join us at the Creative Coding Open House, a friendly community space within the Ars Electronica Festival. It is hosted by members of the vvvv, Processing, p5.js, Clinic for Open Source Arts (COSA) and other creative coding communities.

Think of it as a cosy living room where artists, designers, educators, students, researchers and anyone curious about code-based creative practices can drop in, share their work, learn from others or simply spend some time with likeminded folks exploring the creative possibilities of code.
One of the things we would like to explore is how different creative co

artists: Amir Bastan (IR), Cécile Bucher (CH), Chris Coleman (US), Raphaël de Courville (FR), Joreg (AT)
descEn: Whether you are a novvvvice or enjoying vvvv professionally, join us for an afternoon of demos. Bring your own patch or just check out what is on display. We will be avateering virtual characters, have a laser to play with and maybe even a robot. But most importantly we will be curious to hear your thoughts and questions about vvvv and to share what we know.

artists: Amir Bastan (IR), Cécile Bucher (CH), Chris Coleman (US), Raphaël de Courville (FR), Joreg (AT)
descEn: Have you ever wanted to try out Processing or p5.js? Join us for a day celebrating 25 years of Processing—a gathering for beginners, experienced users and everyone in between. Come by to see how easily hands, faces and bodies can be tracked with ml5.js and p5.js, explore how Processing can be used to create immersive Deep Space applications, discuss what is next for Processing and p5.js or exchange ideas about using AI tools in your creative practice or teaching.

artists: Amir Bastan (IR), Cécile Bucher (CH), Chris Coleman (US), Raphaël de Courville (FR), Joreg (AT)
descEn: At the Creative Coding Open House, this lab demystifies how to support open-source software. Designed for all skill levels, the event guides participants through taking their contributing first steps, making great tutorials and improving documentation and language support. Attendees gain practical experience committing code while exploring meaningful ways of supporting communities. This hands-on day empowers everyone to sustain the creative digital tools that they love.

artists: Amir Bastan (IR), Cécile Bucher (CH), Chris Coleman (US), Raphaël de Courville (FR), Joreg (AT)
descEn: The Creative Coding Open House starts with a day to meet fellow creative coding tool users and makers (and those who are just curious!). Make new connections and catch up with old friends. Pitch activities for the coming days at the Open House and help us make this a cozy space to hang out.

artists: Amir Bastan (IR), Cécile Bucher (CH), Chris Coleman (US), Raphaël de Courville (FR), Joreg (AT)
descEn: Let’s get a taste of different creative coding tools and discuss the philosophies behind them. Find out what they have in common and what is unique about them. Bring your own favorite tool and share your experience with it as we build the same artwork in parallel. We will have stations where beginners can taste-test different tools and find what is right for you!

Hydrogen is the most abundant element in the universe—and at the same time, one of the least tangible. Invisible and odorless, it will nonetheless play a central role in the mobility of tomorrow. On Linz’s Main Square, the installation Bounce into the Future brings this form of energy to life: a ball pit stands in for individual H2 atoms in space—a playful image for one of the more complex energy questions of our time. At its center is not the BMW car, but energy itself: Where does green hydrogen come from, under what conditions does it become a meaningful building block for a decarbonized fut

ticket: FESTIVALPASS+, FESTIVALPASS, DAYPASS, FESTIVAL WALK Ticket
descEn: In a world where soil is increasingly sealed, degraded and overlooked despite sustaining much of Earth’s biodiversity, Entangled Landscape invites audiences to reconsider the invisible underground relationships that support life and the mutualistic behaviors from which ecological and computational systems can learn. The work is a real-time computational installation that gives form to the mutualistic interactions of mycorrhizal soil networks. Experienced through mixed reality, audiences encounter a dynamic virtual structure shaped by machine learning agents trained on the principles of mutuali

nameEn: Curator’s Tour with Julia Staudach: “Collection Francisco Carolinum”
nameDe: Kuratorinnenführung mit Julia Staudach: “Collection Francisco Carolinum“
ticket: Francisco Carolinum Linz Ticket, FESTIVALPASS+, FESTIVALPASS
descEn: With the Collection Francisco Carolinum, the museum presents its continuously growing collection of blockchain-based art in a comprehensive exhibition for the first time. Since its launch in 2021, the collection has grown to include works on the Ethereum, Tezos and Bitcoin blockchains, offering a window into an artistic field that remains in constant flux. In this tour, the exhibition’s curator, Julia Staudach, shares insights into the artworks and the ideas behind them.

nameEn: Artist Tour with Ana María Caballero and Curator Julia Staudach: “READ THE ROOM”
nameDe: Artist Tour mit Ana María Caballero und Kuratorin Julia Staudach: “READ THE ROOM”
ticket: FESTIVALPASS+, FESTIVALPASS, DAYPASS, Francisco Carolinum Linz Ticket
descEn: In this Artist Tour, artist and poet Ana María Caballero joins curator Julia Staudach to guide visitors through Read the Room, her first institutional mid-career retrospective. The exhibition spans key works in installation, performance, sculpture, choreography, cinematic AI and literature. Together, they offer insight into an artistic practice rooted in a fundamental conviction: language is not a fixed medium, but a living process that unfolds in the interplay of writing and reading.

nameEn: Artist Tour with Claudia Larcher and Curator Eva Fischer: “No applause. no life. no pain.“
nameDe: Artist Tour mit Claudia Larcher und Kuratorin Eva Fischer: “No applause. no life. no pain.“
ticket: FESTIVALPASS+, FESTIVALPASS, Francisco Carolinum Linz Ticket, DAYPASS
descEn: In this guided tour, Claudia Larcher joins the curator of the exhibition, Eva Fischer, to explore how her works in the exhibition No applause. no life. no pain. at Francisco Carolinum unfold a panorama of change: the extinction of species, the erosion of shared cultural spaces and the transformation of our perception in the age of generative AI. In her films, installations and AI-based works, Claudia Larcher connects ecological questions with reflections on the future of cinema and image production.

nameEn: Reading the Room: Language, Systems, and Contemporary Art
artists: Ana María Caballero (CO/US), Manuela Naveau (AT), Sergio Fontanella (CU), Alfred Weidinger (AT)
ticket: FESTIVALPASS+, FESTIVALPASS, Francisco Carolinum Linz Ticket
descEn: Reading the Room: Language, Systems, and Contemporary Art brings together Manuela Naveau, Ana María Caballero, Sergio Fontanella and Alfred Weidinger on a panel moderated by Julia Staudach. A conversation rooted in Caballero’s first institutional retrospective. Taking the exhibition (and the page) as its point of departure, this panel explores poetry as a contemporary artistic medium, examining language, translation, participation and systems of record-keeping within contemporary new media settings.

nameEn: Patterns & Politics: Book Presentation and Panel
artists: Claudia Hart (US), Andrew Blanton (US), Anika Meier (DE), Julia Staudach (AT)
ticket: FESTIVALPASS+, FESTIVALPASS, Francisco Carolinum Linz Ticket, DAYPASS
descEn: This book presentation and panel brings together Claudia Hart, Andrew Blanton and Anika Meier for a conversation, moderated by curator Julia Staudach, on Hart’s artistic practice and her first museum retrospective. Taking the exhibition Patterns and Politics and the publication as its point of departure, the panel traces Hart’s perspective on technology, visual culture and power, connecting her decades of work with virtual image-making to current debates on AI art.

artists: STADTWERKSTATT (AT), Various Sound and Performance Artists
descEn: On Friday, September 11th, and Saturday, September 12th, the Stadtwerkstatt will host two nights of: GET READY for HAUNTED NIGHTLINE! Hybrid genres, abstract practices, electronic soundscapes, a ghost train ride featuring living, dead and undead media: musicians, sound artists and performers from Linz and around the world will haunt the night with vibration-inducing acts, dystopian ambient sounds, energetic noise performances, sound battalions and eerie voices until the early morning hours. Everything that turns dreams into nightmarish visions will be unleashed. Or to be specific: Chra, VLKSAM

Media art, subculture and fragments and continuities of a tech-oriented feminist history. The essay film Herzblutwiese Stadtwerkstatt addresses feminism, equal rights and gender equality at the Stadtwerkstatt, the longest-running autonomous art and culture space in the city of Linz. In an environment of aesthetic innovation, social revolt, subversive power and artistic-technological developments, the film interweaves text, interviews, artistic productions and archive material from 1979 to the present day into a narrative with shifting perspectives—thus creating a larger social story that exten
With projectors, text, broadcasts, wild gestures and media of all kind, the milieu cinema is being taken over.

artists: Bianca Ludewig (AT), Sashe Urdovski (MK), States of Clay (AT), Stefan Tiefengraber (AT)
descEn: Participatory Reading and Discussion: Bianca Ludewig will read from her book Transmedia Festivals – Audio-Social Communities Between Artistic Experimentation and Economization alongside guests. This will be followed by a discussion with sound artists Anna S. Adelt, Stefan Tiefengraber, and Sashe Urdovski, who are presenting works at STWST.

EVERYBODY DANCE NOW is a Mixed Reality prototype exploring dance as a physical and social experience. It motion-captures and archives the movement vocabularies of subcultural forms such as breakdance and ballroom, translating them into embodied dialogue. The project asks whether XR can teach dance the way a dancer teaches it: body to body, rather than as fixed choreography. In the prototype EDN.ALPHA, visitors enter an installation and learn moves recorded from professional ballroom, breakdance and ballet dancers. Ballroom arose in Black and Latinx LGBTQ+ New York, yet such subcultures are mis

nameEn: DIE KUNSTSCHAFFENDEN | Meet the Artist: Robert Moser
descEn:
Meet artist Robert Moser for a conversation on the exhibition In the Paradise of Painting. Or: On Growth and Refinement, on view at DIE KUNSTSCHAFFENDEN. As high-performance computers increasingly assess human beings by their “market value”, art remains a space for growth and refinement. At its most authentic, it preserves what makes us human. In this light, hand-painted works become an act of resistance. 
The artist will share insights into his practice and reflect on painting as a space for human experience, refinement and resistance in the age of algorithmic systems.

DIE KUNSTSCHAFFENDEN i

artists: Oskar Boldre (CH/IT), NENDA (AT), Latinos Linz (AT), Point of Ukraine (AT), Hungaro Media (AT), PAROLA (AT), The Company of Music (AT), Johannes Hiemetsberger (AT), Julian Pixel Schmiederer (AT)
descEn: The multilingual appraoch of the project not only highlights the universal validity of human rights but also reflects the diversity of the citizens of Linz, who are actively involved. In front of St. Mary’s Cathedral, groups of young people from Linz with migrant backgrounds are scattered across the square. They chant parts of the Declaration of Human Rights in their mother tongues. They, along with the audience, become the fierce voice advocating for human rights.

artists: Rajiv Bhagwanbali (NL), Anna Hazarian (UA), Philipp “Flip” Kroll (AT), Alina Lugovskaya (RU)
descEn: Press Start is a performance that involves dance, music and spoken word. It explores the challenges faced by a young individual who is pulled into a radical online universe through gaming, where they encounter manipulation, controlling behavior and bullying.

artists: Anna Lowenhaupt Tsing (US), Feifei Zhou (CN), Nieuwe Instituut (NL)
ticket: FESTIVALPASS+, FESTIVALPASS, DAYPASS, FESTIVAL WALK Ticket
descEn: Fungi fulfil a wide range of human needs. We have eaten mushrooms since ancient times and used penicillin to fight bacteria. In the world of architecture, we celebrate fungi as a trendy material, in the same way that we once embraced concrete and plastic. The exhibition FUNGI: Anarchist Designers tells a different story. Fungi can be inspiring master builders—but also formidable demolition workers. In this exhibition, curated by anthropologist Anna Tsing and artist-architect Feifei Zhou, fungi are for once not at the service of humans, but independent beings with their own agenda, one that is

artists: Rupert Huber (AT), Johannes Pröll (AT), Mihaela Kavdanska (BG/AT), Dilmana Yordanova (BG/RO)
descEn: The genome sonification of this media art installation https://app.notion.com/p/Show-Me-Your-Face-The-Power-of-Becoming-39538ddb450c810e99e9c6be3088c1c8?pvs=21 is performed live by Rupert Huber. Through moving image, text, AI-mediated visual transformation and direct sonification of genomic data, the project explores phenotype as a process of becoming. It invites viewers into a contemplative space where identity unfolds through an ongoing negotiation between inheritance and possibility. Human nature is continuously enacted and transformed through a lifetime of translation.

Resilient Voices brings Aboriginal singer-songwriter Nancy Bates into public space through intimate musical interventions. Her songs explore Indigenous knowledge, civil courage and resistance to injustice, celebrating the resilience of First Nations peoples while inviting reflection on contemporary struggles for justice, truth and reconciliation. Audiences gather, listen and often join in, transforming everyday spaces into moments of shared courage, dialogue and connection.

The seminar offers educators, students, artists and researchers a platform to present their work and receive constructive feedback. Held during the Ars Electronica Festival, it provides an ideal space for networking and creative exchange among international guests. You are welcome to submit your work as either a digital presentation (such as slides) or an analog poster.

Participants will be grouped into panels of 3–5, depending on the topics of the presentations.

With Olivier Messiaen’s Apparition de l'Église éternelle, cathedral organist Gerhard Raab brings a monumental masterpiece of modern organ music to the acoustic space of the St. Mary’s Cathedral. Literally translating to the ”Apparition of the Eternal Church”, the piece builds over a relentlessly pulsating bass ostinato into a massive, architectural wave of sound—an immersive experience that unleashes the full physical power of the cathedral organ.

Nadia Struiwigh is an accomplished Dutch producer and live artist who operates between Rotterdam and Berlin. Drawing upon the Warp school of electronica, her sound bridges deep, beatless ambient immersions and kinetic, hardware-driven techno. With releases on labels like Dekmantel and CPU, as well as a DJ residency at Tresor, her performances—ranging from intimate listening sessions to open-ended, improvised club sets—express a rich, deeply personal sonic world powered by technical mastery and genuine emotion.

This is the premiere of the artist’s new song RISE—a composition that explores ideas of resilience and the process of becoming. It is a journey of rediscovery and reinvention.
Crystn Hunt Akron gained international attention following a live performance in Cairo, where an early audience interruption sparked a widespread debate on issues of artistic freedom, cultural contexts and the role of experimental sound art within religious spaces. This incident served to highlight the unique capacity of art to initiate social discourse, challenge established perceptions and open up new spaces for dialog

Stellar Atmospheres explores the work of the women astrophysicists collectively known as the “Harvard Computers”, who mapped and classified the night sky around the year 1900. The exhibition presents sculptural works that translate historical systems of astronomical observation into spatial forms, reflecting on the relationship between science, visibility, classification systems and the often-overlooked contributions of women to the history of knowledge.

Opening: September 3, 2026, 18:00
Duration: September 4–24, 2026
Opening Hours: 14:00–18:00

DAS Trail is a fieldwork program developed as part of the Data Art & Science Project. In this workshop for kids and teens, you will learn about the local area through data collection. Together with other families, you will walk along specially curated trails in Linz and explore the city from a new perspective through observation, Gaussian Splatting 3D scanning of your discoveries and engaging in dialogue with others.

nameEn: Meet the Artist: Exploring the Art-Research Project ”Echoes of the Abyss” – Revealing the Ocean’s Hidden Histories and Geopolitical Scars
artists: Robertina Šebjanič (artist-researcher) (SI) and Tina Dolinšek (Projekt Atol) (SI)
ticket: FESTIVALPASS+, FESTIVALPASS, DAYPASS, Francisco Carolinum Linz Ticket
descEn: This Meet the Artist event presents Echoes of the Abyss by artist-researcher Robertina Šebjanič and Tina Dolinšek (Projekt Atol), exploring how the toxic legacies of geopolitical conflicts persist in marine environments through dumped chemical munitions and unexploded ordnance. They will introduce the project’s interdisciplinary collaborations between special diving units, marine scientists and artists, revealing the layered processes behind addressing complex ecological and geopolitical histories.

artists: Andrea Corradi (IT), Lilith-Isa (AT), Mahtab Miandehi (IR/AT), Montaha (AT/EG), Muri Anda (AT), Sanna Lu Una (AT), Studio Brudi (AT), Sturmherta (AT)
descEn:
Sound Campus – Listening Underground explores the movement beneath the surface. It considers the ongoing, divergent processes which are felt but not always seen. To submerge opens up new modes of attention and multi-sensory listening that change our relation with the surroundings.

nameEn: Renewable Hydrogen for resilient and emission-free Mobility Systems
descEn: Decarbonizing the transportation sector is one of the key challenges on the path to climate neutrality. As a zero-emission energy source, hydrogen can make a significant contribution to reducing greenhouse gas emissions while also strengthening energy security through the use of domestic, renewable energy sources. It enables the storage and delivery of renewable energy regardless of when and where it is generated.

nameEn: Hydrogen at the BMW Group Plant Steyr
artists: Oliver Fürst and Bernhard Aichhorn, BMW Group (AT)
descEn: Integrated development and production at one site: BMW Group Plant Steyr and its development center have over 40 years experience in applying new technologies. We are now contributing to pre-series development of the third-generation fuel cell system and preparing for series production of the hydrogen drivetrain.

This Master Class takes the audience behind the scenes of hydrogen fuel cell technology. Using the upcoming BMW iX5 Hydrogen as an example, it explains how a hydrogen vehicle works, how the fuel cell system generates electric power on board and how BMW integrates key components, such as the third-generation fuel cell system and hydrogen tank technology, into the vehicle's architecture.

artists: Dai Nippon Printing (JP), Ars Electronica Futurelab (AT)
ticket: FESTIVALPASS+, FESTIVALPASS, DAYPASS, Ars Electronica Center Ticket
descEn: Explore the future of care and connection in the age of AI and robotics. This open discussion marks the first step in a new research collaboration between Dai Nippon Printing and the Ars Electronica Futurelab. Together, the discussion explores how technology is reshaping health, well-being, happiness and social connection, with a focus on prevention, loneliness and the role of AI and robotics. Participants are invited to help shape the conversation by sharing their visions for the future.

nameEn: El Cultivo de la Mente – Art Film
artists: Blüten & Papaya (Georgi Sarkezi (AT), Eva Stöflin (AT), Milan Conic (RS)
descEn: El Cultivo de la Mente is a performance film by the artist duo Blüten & Papaya, divided into three acts, with a live performance of the soundtrack by Milan Conic on piano. The film centers on a stranded man who devotes himself to self-imposed tasks in support of nature on a solitary island. It interrogates human logic in relation to natural processes and cycles, as well as humanity’s engagement with its own will. Composer and pianist Milan Conic musically immerses himself in the protagonist’s inner world and interprets it live. His composition emerges in direct dialogue with the images, openin

TıSHıNA blends soulful pop with modern harmonies, hip-hop grooves and electronic elements—a sound that is at once intimate and captivating.

TıSHıNA was founded by Viviane Töbich and Milan Conic, who have been writing songs together since 2020 and formed their band a year later. Since then, they have played numerous concerts on the local scene and built a solid presence there.

The band members’ varied musical and personal backgrounds merge into a sound that invites pause—a blend of calm, soulful moments and powerful, chaotically ordered passages that highlight the music’s contrasting facets,

Tarlan Eshtiagh is an Iranian-born musician, vocalist, pianist and arranger. She is currently based in Austria. Beyond jazz and contemporary vocal art, she has deep roots in Persian music, having worked as singer, pianist and arranger. Notably, they rearranged traditional Persian compositions for piano and vocals.

Tarlan Eshtiagh and Milan Conic are beginning a musical collaboration in Linz. Inspired by traditional Iranian music, they blend electronic sounds with modern arrangements, creating a contemporary, intercultural sound.

Te-En Chen is a composer, synthesist and sound artist based in Linz, Austria. His work bridges classical tradition and experimental practice through live electronics, modular synthesis, multichannel composition and free improvisation. Combining real-time sound processing with synthesizer performance, he creates immersive sonic dialogues between acoustic instruments and electronic textures in interdisciplinary collaborations.

Composer and synthesist Te-En Chen and pianist/composer Milan Conić first crossed paths in Linz, Austria—a city whose vibrant artistic landscape encourages encounters bet

Tomá Ivanov, formerly half of the techno live act KOMATON, whose track In Between appeared on Cocoon's Compilation J, went on to explore jazz, live electronics and experimental songwriting as TOMÁ before returning to the club with a reduced, personal sound: dusty low-end warmth, tight percussion and melodic restraint.

The Unsettled is the duo project of Serbian jazz pianist Milan Conic and Ukrainian producer J San, merging their individual stories of resilience with an eclectic blend of electronic music. Drawing on genres such as House, UK Garage, and New School Breaks, their sound is enriched by Milan's contemporary piano playing, while J San's innovative sound design adds a distinctive edge.
Crafting immersive atmospheres and intricate sonic textures, they transport listeners into evolving, cinematic yet danceable soundscapes.
Now based in Linz, Austria, The Unsettled offers an immersive live experience w

Maja Vidic is a Slovenian dancer, choreographer, performer and musician exploring the connection between movement and voice.

Free Association Improvisation is an interdisciplinary artistic project initiated by Milan Conić, exploring the boundaries between music, movement and spontaneous expression.
Rooted in the principle of free association, the project embraces immediacy, intuition and presence—allowing sound, body and visual elements to emerge organically in the moment, without predetermined structure. 
At its core, Free Association Improvisation is a dialogue between artists across differ
What happens when music and poetry meet? Milan Conic and Lotte Sandhacker play with the piano, voice and musical poetry—separately, together and merged as one.

nameEn: Leonardo LASER Talks Linz – Lab Songs Vol. III: Quantum Vermouth
artists: Jens Hauser (DE/FR), Antonio Jesús Gómez Delegido (ES), Patricia Soto Molina (ES), Fabricio Lamoncha (ES)
descEn:
Leonardo LASER is an international program that brings together artists, scientists, academics, and the public to share their work and inspire one another through presentations, performances and discussions.

Our recurring LASER series, Lab Songs, explores evolving cultures of experimentation. Scientific and artistic breakthroughs arise not only from discoveries, but from transformations in practices, methodologies and systems of care. As a result, laboratories are increasingly reimagined as spaces where aesthetic, technological, ecological and theoretical forms of knowledge come into proximit

ticket: WE GUIDE YOU Ticket, WE GUIDE YOU Ticket surcharge
descEn: Join us on a playful journey through projects at the intersection of art, technology and society. Created for children between the ages of four and ten and their accompanying adults, this special tour along the FESTIVAL WALK invites young participants to explore surprising perspectives on this year’s festival topic.

nameEn: Crafting Futures Lab: Re-membering our Seeds
artists: Julia Moser (AT), Angela Olbrich (AT), Dunjiva Kollektiv (AT)
descEn: Seeds are living archives. They carry memories of place, seasons and generations of care. This collective embroidery circle invites participants to stitch seeds into fabric while listening to stories about plants, place-making and seed keeping. Together, we reflect on how knowledge is embedded in materials and practices—and how, like seeds, it is preserved, transformed and passed on.

nameEn: Crafting Futures Lab: Pulling. Weaving. Connecting. Threads
descEn: Gold threads once wrapped saints and sovereigns, while today they carry signals, light and touch. In this workshop we follow a filament’s journey, weaving cables that are both ornament and circuit. Along the way we explore how decoration becomes function, how craft becomes technology, and how pulling a single thread can unravel histories.

nameEn: Crafting Futures Lab: Crafting Mountains from Dusty Tales
descEn: A reading of field notes and laboratory logs on fantastical, mystical, strange and toxic tales of crafted mountains: From crystal growth and lava imitation to mining landfills and heaps of electronic waste—materials scientific research not only works with extracted materials from the undergrounds but is also entangled in the design of new piles of materials. This session gives insights into the research methods of an experimental, embodied and material-based historiography of design which starts in a Parisian physics laboratory in 1880 and traces fragments in scientific mountain crafts up to t

artists: Julia Moser (AT), Josseline Engeler(AT/DE), Lena Hartl (AT)
descEn: Some forms of preservation can only be accessed through destruction. Unearthing Taste is a food happening and conversation exploring clay-based food preservation, material knowledge and the value of impermanence. Together we break open earthen vessels to share regional food, stories and reflections on care, place, memory and resourcefulness.

nameEn: Crafting Futures Lab: From Textiles to Textures
descEn: We understand tools as actors in the making of physical things, but also in shaping and preserving memory across generations. In this workshop, we explore the unexpected connections between pasta-making and textile crafts through the tools used in both practices. By handling familiar tools in unfamiliar ways, we revisit and reconsider their stories through the shaping of dough, bringing them into conversation with our own knowledge, memories and understanding of the everyday.

artists: Antonia Ludwig (DE), Helene Mondria (AT), Julia Moser (AT), Valerie Moschner (AT), Irene Posch (AT)
descEn:
Seeds, plants, stones and gold threads form the basis of syrups that translate moments, shared knowledge and experiences from the festival’s workshops, conversations and practices into flavor. Visitors are invited to an aperitif event where they can compose their own drinks and encounter this collection through taste and togetherness.

All welcome. No registration required.

nameEn: Crafting Futures Lab: Crushing the Rocks
descEn: The Crushing the Rocks workshop explores the technique of textile printing with mineral pigments obtained from locally found rocks and fragments of old bricks. Together, we crush, sift, mix and print, following the transformation of a solid material into a fine powder: the pigment. Participants are invited to observe material transformation, reflect on the origin and value of materials and approach the act of making with curiosity and care rather than fixed expectations.

artists: Wolfgang “Fadi” Dorninger (AT), Bernadette Huber (AT), Manfred Wakolbinger (AT), Theresa Ulrike Cellnigg (AT), Judith Gattermayr (AT), David Kapl (AT), Michaela Kessler (AT)
descEn:
The new exhibition AUSGEZEICHNET (DISTINGUISHED) at the KUNSTSAMMLUNG puts the spotlight on the recipients of the 2025 Culture Prizes of the Province of Upper Austria and brings together works from the four artistic positions honored with the Talent Promotion Awards for Visual Art.

WOLFGANG “FADI” DORNINGER

nameEn: Panel Discussion: Hydrogen and the road ahead: perspectives from Art, Society and BMW
artists: Michael Mondria, Ars Electronica (AT), Jürgen Guldner, BMW Group (DE), Christiane Rau, Fachhochschule Oberösterreich (AT)
descEn: This panel looks beyond hydrogen as an engineering topic and explores the broader conditions for technological acceptance. With perspectives from art, society and BMW, the discussion examines what hydrogen technology can contribute to future mobility, how trust in new technologies is built and how creative approaches can open up new ways of engaging with innovation.

The Prix Ars Electronica Award Ceremony at the Design Center Linz will be a further highlight of the festival week. On this evening, the focus will lie on art—and with it on the exceptional artists who were awarded the Golden Nica of the Prix Ars Electronica in 2026. In addition, the winners of the S+T+ARTS Prize, the AI for Social Impact Initiative and State of the ART(ist)  will be asked to come on stage.

Industrial robotic arms lift and snap a sheet of silk as two dancers move with and against them. A projected forest climbs from ground to open sky. Mist gathers when their timing slips and clears when they find a rhythm again. The dancers of TAO Dance Theater do not explain the machines. Through weight, touch, hesitation and recovery, they test how trust is made and lost between human and mechanical bodies. descEn: To kick off the day’s focus on Living Archives, Ars Electronica invites you to a 60-minute opening performance in Deep Space 8K. Following a welcome address, Gerfried Stocker guides the audience through selected highlights of this year’s festival program as well as standout projects from the previous year. This Master Class takes the audience behind the scenes of hydrogen fuel cell technology. Using the upcoming BMW iX5 Hydrogen as an example, it explains how a hydrogen vehicle works, how the fuel cell system generates electric power on board and how BMW integrates key components, such as the third-generation fuel cell system and hydrogen tank technology, into the vehicle's architecture.

artists: Christian Geiger (DE), Ivana Druzetic-Vogel (DE), Laurenz Ulrich (DE), Léon Repp (DE), Christian Zimmer (DE)
descEn:
Oneironautica V: Catalyst is the latest chapter in the ongoing Oneironautica series, a cycle of Virtual Reality (VR) installations situated within a three-dimensionally scanned theater rendered through point-cloud aesthetics. Developed in collaboration with Theater an der Ruhr, the work explores the relationship between individual action and collective behavior through embodied interaction. A single participant enters a responsive crowd of abstract humanoid figures who reorganize themselves in response to the proximity of this new visitor.
The experience unfolds in two dramaturgical phases. In

WIMML is an interactive, animated Wimmelbild that uses co-located game technology to let people physically engage with it. Instead of just looking at a visually dense, detailed scene, viewers can move through the space and take part in and influence what is happening inside.
Taking inspiration from the Flemish Proverbs by Pieter Bruegel the Elder, which visualizes over a hundred Dutch sayings to capture the chaos and humor of everyday life in the 16th century, WIMML reimagines this concept within the Austrian cultural context of the 21st century. artists: Pascal Nowarra (DE), Florian Guggenberger (AT), Sandra Ye (AT), Renée Kerschbaumer (AT)
descEn: Matchmaker Madness is a single-player interactive installation that combines a large-scale physical controller with a projection-based digital game. The system is centered around a waist-height slingshot constructed from a natural Y-shaped tree, which serves as the primary interaction device. Players use the slingshot to aim and shoot at heart-shaped targets displayed on a wall projection. These targets appear when two animated characters face each other, indicating a potential match. Successfully hitting a heart forms a couple and awards points, while incorrect matches result in “toxic” pairi

Cities are increasingly defined by what can be measured—traffic flows, tree inventories, noise complaints. Yet urban life is also something we feel: the quiet of a winter street, the cacophony of a summer afternoon. Urban Data Orchestra transforms two NYC datasets—the Tree Census and the SONYC soundscape archive—into a sensory instrument for exploring the city. Using plexiglass modules on a split console, visitors compose urban soundscapes: neighborhood against neighborhood, March against July. nameEn: 12.5 square meters—space for a car, or…
nameDe: 12,5 Quadratmeter – Platz für ein Auto, oder…
artists: Klasse 1b, Mittelschule Kettenbrücke (AT), Elisabeth Berger (AT), Alexander Janus (AT)
descEn:
The project 12,5 Quadratmeter—Platz für ein Auto, oder … (12.5 square meters—space for a car, or…) started with an empty parking space in the schoolyard and the children’s complaints about the lack of space to move around.
This sparked a thought experiment: What could be possible in these 12.5 square meters? After all, it’s not just cars that need space, but also creative ideas for using public space. The students’ visions ranged from a mini-campsite and cozy reading corners to a soccer field. First, ideas were gathered and sketches made, and then it was time to visualize them. The children me

descEn:
“Dear friend of the future, […] when you open [this letter], unless I am very wrong, letter writing will be as outmoded as speech.” Australian journalist Max Lamshed wrote these words in 1959 in a letter addressed to the early 21st century. He was one of 19 Australian journalists, scientists, reverends and writers asked to write letters to future generations as part of the ABC project “Letters to the Unborn” in the late 1950s. In addition to the disappearance of speech, these letters speculated about other—sometimes absurd—developments, hardly any of which proved to be right.

artists: Tobias Staab (DE), Black Pearl de Almeida Lima (BR), Silke Schmidt (DE)
descEn: Embodied Futures asks what happens when Mixed Reality becomes not just a virtual world but a space to test new forms of embodiment, identity and relation. Drawing on the research projects OYA and EVERYBODY DANCE NOW (EDN.ALPHA), the Town Hall brings together voices from art, technology and research—and the audience—for an open exchange. Together they explore how immersive technology can lead deeper into the body, and what new forms of learning, empathy and community might emerge.

nameEn: Extended Reality – An Art Form in Public Space  (on Trinity-Tarot-Garden)
nameDe: Extended Reality – eine Kunstform im öffentlichen Raum (zum Trinity-Tarot-Garden)
artists: Ugo Dossi (DE), Stefan Göppel (DE), Markus Stenger (DE)
descEn: The event asks what changes when art enters public space as Extended Reality. Its starting point is Trinity-Tarot-Garden by Ugo Dossi and Stefan Göppel, a walkable virtual sculpture park of 28 oversized symbols experienced through VR headsets. Artists, architects, curators and the audience discuss how immersive technology reshapes public space, how cultural heritage such as the symbolic world of the Tarot is passed on, and what it means when a work of art no longer needs a building.

Infinity is an art-based mobile Augmented Reality (AR) game designed to support adolescents in expressing and processing emotions through interactive experiences. Grounded in art-based methodologies and social-emotional learning, the game transforms abstract emotional expression into interactive AR gameplay. Players externalize emotions through drawing, which are converted into augmented objects that can be interacted with in physical space. The design is informed by a three-phase participatory process involving individual and collaborative expression, followed by translation into gameplay. In

KronoDonum is a two-player gift exchange played across two screens. Players use custom controllers to type in memories and requests, conjuring objects into their counterpart’s world—offerings in a conversation of care. When both players place the same gift object in the same area on their respective maps, the object will solidify and become part of the shared environment. If either player becomes inactive for 15 seconds, their contributions to the shared world will dissolve. KronoDonum is a meditation on digital nesting, connective game worlds and the fleeting tenderness of a friendship across

artists: Philipp Haslbauer (CH), Marco Schmid (CH), Aljosa Smolic (CH)
descEn: An interactive AI installation portraying Jesus as a generative avatar within a confessional booth-inspired wooden box, Deus in Machina invites visitors into voice-based conversations on faith, ethics and spirituality. The work provokes reflection on AI's expanding role in existential domains, blurring boundaries between authenticity and simulation.

Every day, people make decisions based on data visualizations they never learned to question. In Data We Trust is an interactive game for exhibition settings that puts players in the role of a boardroom decision-maker faced with ten proposals, each backed by a chart. Half of the charts tell the truth. The other half lie, using techniques like truncated axes, manipulated scales and reversed time series. A large screen above the installation displays a live scatter plot that maps every visitor along two axes: how well they spotted the traps and how much they trusted the truthful charts. The resu

artists: Sam Chin (US), Cathy Mengying Fang (CN/US), Xinyi Skye Gao (CN/US), Ziyang Leonie Dong (CN/US), Alex Lopez Rodriguez (ES/US), Ruipeng Wang (CN/US)
descEn: In Plato’s Allegory of the Cave, prisoners chained to a wall perceive only shadows—and mistake them for reality. This concept is extended in Plato’s [Al]legory of the Cave, an interactive installation featuring an LLM-controlled character who exists only as a shadow. The piece begins in the dark. A physical light switch invites interaction; flipping it on illuminates the stage and awakens the shadow man. His singular goal is to turn off the light that defines his existence. Humans place objects in his path—blocks, frames and stairs—to obstruct him. He kicks, pushes, sometimes gives up, then be

artists: Chris Geiger (DE), Andi Zielecki (DE), Timo Stampa (DE)
descEn: Das Trampeltier is an eXtended Reality installation that transforms conceptual ideas of Max Ernst’s 1937 painting L’Ange du Foyer into an interactive narrative XR experience. Users encounter a three-dimensional creature who tells stories with warmth and apparent sincerity—while systematically absorbing every user choice into predetermined conclusions. This paper examines the experiential design of one of two narrative scenarios within this installation: an interactive fairy tale where users believe they shape the story, and where the creature reframes violence as responsibility. We focus on ho

Embodied Animation is an interactive installation that redefines animation as a form of real-time, embodied and playable performance. Instead of relying on frame-by-frame production or pre-rendered computational pipelines, the work introduces a live generative paradigm in which the human body functions as the primary creative engine. This approach draws from theories of embodied interaction, where meaning emerges through situated bodily action rather than abstract command input. Through hand gestures, participants directly shape evolving visual and sonic outputs, transforming animation into an

artists: Elias Wolschlager (AT), Kareem Al-Khalily (AT), David Märzendorfer (AT), Philipp Wenisch (AT)
descEn: Clawsembly Line is an arcade-like claw machine game where you grab different body parts from a conveyor belt to create your very own character, which then joins the factory’s workforce. Players have three attempts to create their intended character; however, the claw machine’s nature forces them to adjust and accept certain quirks of fate. Players might not grab exactly what they want and need to work with their limited number of grabs. In the foreground, the conveyor belt and the claw are visible; right behind it stands the character currently being created. Whenever a character is completed,

The title Orbit: A War Series is a reference to the New York artist Nancy Spero: deeply moved by the photographs of the Vietnam War that were circulating in the media, Spero investigated the links between sexuality, violence and power in The War Series (1966–70). The subject of oppressive power structures revealed in her art is horrifyingly relevant today. Orbit: A War Series appeals to the images in our minds: Brigitta Muntendorf’s immersive 3D audio space oratorio is like an electroacoustic series of narratives in which sounds, texts, voices and space become transmitters of power structures.

What enables systemic transformation? STORMO®️ is a workshop on collective intelligence that invites participants to embody the relational enablers essential for ecosystem transformation. Inspired by the behaviour of flocks in nature, it creates a space where listening, collaboration, holding space and shared leadership arise through direct experience. It embodies the processes enabling transformation, as elaborated by the Systemic Narratives research carried out by EIT Culture and Creativity.

nameEn: Discover the future with Join MINT and the Star Truck
nameDe: Mit Join MINT und dem Star Truck die Zukunft entdecken
artists: Verein More Innovation Needs Talents, AUT
descEn:
The Star Truck is a mobile science and technology experience center that tours throughout Upper Austria. Across five exciting themed areas, you can try out and experience technology, computer science, natural sciences and math for yourselves. At interactive stations, you can test new technologies, discover innovative ideas and gain fascinating insights into current topics of the future through workshops.

Slots:
From Wednesday to Saturday (09.09.–12.09.), the hourly slots run from 10:30 to 19:00, each with short breaks in between. On Sunday, September 13, the last time slot begins at 17:15.

nameEn: Distributed Agencies: Reimagining Personhood and Identity
artists: Bernd Resch (AT), Iohanna Nicenboim (NL), Ash E. Smith (US), Silvia Hackl (AT)
descEn:
Who do we become when personhood itself is increasingly shaped by AI, narratives on emerging digital and social media, data infrastructures, ecological entanglements and non-human intelligences? In this landscape, identity is not fixed but continuously produced between humans and non-humans, including platforms, societies, environments and machines.
We propose that NEGOTIATING HUMANITY is not about defending a stable human essence, but about learning to live responsibly with distributed agencies: social, artificial, synthetic, ecological and more-than-human. We invite visitors to encounter ide

Posthuman Radio is a live sonic cabaret where artists, scientists, performers, AI agents, humans and nonhumans are staged together. Conversations, field recordings, films and live activations run simultaneously. A moment to tune out of the usual noise, and attune to/with others.

This is play. A radio play. And we take play seriously, just as an experiment is serious. Play is where relations get tried before they are real: otters nip each other and both know it is a game, a scientist speculates past their data, AI agents are scene partners.
Our stage is the podcast studio, where realities are

Who are we becoming when being human is increasingly shaped by AI, digital and social media, data infrastructures, ecological entanglements and non-human intelligences?
Distributed Agencies opens this inquiry by asking how digital traces, algorithmic interpretation, public discourse and non-human intelligences shape how people understand themselves, and how societies perceive and respond to them.
The project brings together research groups from IT:U to share work from multiple disciplines across arts and science.

Learn to jam with and as Pastagang: At the heart of it is the live coding language Strudel. For visuals, Pastagang tends to use the visual synthesizer language Hydra. Start from the beginning, no experience is needed.

nameEn: For Sun Ra on Saturn (Against Elon on Mars)
descEn: This year, a red-lit area will be visible on the Maindeck in front of the STWST. The red area stands for all manner of dramatic expressions. It lies open like a huge, screaming mouth of blood, evoking both the current horrors of the wars plaguing the globe and the structural brutalities of capitalism: Even the concrete screams, to paraphrase Michel Houellebecq. And everything screams—everything that has been torn from life and fed into the current machinery of exploitation—into this new technocapitalist totalitarianism that has permeated even the smallest spheres of life, into this context in

Experience live how professional TV and film productions come to life! At this station, you can step into the role of both camera operator and director. One camera on a jib arm, dolly and track system allows you to create dynamic, cinema-quality camera moves yourself. A second camera sits on a tripod in a studio setup, fitted with the longest Super 35 lens currently on the market from Canon (50–1000 mm) designed for flexible framing.
Both cameras feed into a mobile control room. Here you can try out different shots and camera movements and get a hands-on look at how a multi-camera setup works

As part of Unglaublicher Herbst, Brucknerhaus Linz and Ars Electronica bring back the beloved SoundPark format to the festival stage. For years it was a fixture of the Big Concert Night, carried by the powerful audio infrastructure that otherwise powers Linz’s Klangwolke, and it transformed Donaupark into a resonating space for electronic music. Along the route from Lentos to the Brucknerhaus, avant-garde electronic sound experiences were broadcast there at full intensity. This year, that tradition is being rediscovered: the Danube riverside once again becomes a stage for sound, where electron

The Austrian writer Ingeborg Bachmann wrote the poem Die gestundete Zeit (Deferred Time) in 1953, during a period of apparent renewal and economic prosperity. Yet Bachmann wrote against the spirit of the times: against the silence surrounding war, crime and guilt; against a language scarred by the war, a language that was no longer sufficient and in search of a new one that had yet to be found. The metaphor of “deferred time” comes from the financial world: a deferral is not a cancellation, but a postponement. Through images drawn from a world that seems familiar yet gradually slips into somet
Daily Spotlight Tours take place in OK Quarter and Lentos Kunstmuseum Linz. They give you a deeper insight into this year’s theme exhibition.
Explore this year’s Ars Electronica Features Exhibitions as well as current exhibitions from Francisco Carolinum.

To mark the 60th anniversary of Johannes Kepler University Linz, the campus of the Faculty of Medicine is one of the festival’s main venues. The JKU festival coordinators guide visitors through the MED Campus and the university’s Art & Science projects, including the LIT Exhibition, Practices of Transformation and JKU medFOCUS.
Our guided tours span a variety of locations this year. Check out guided tours in other locations with different thematic focuses.

You don’t know where to start? Come join one of our Intro Sessions. Our art educators offer you in-depth insights into selected projects from the festival’s most important exhibitions. Whether you’re curious, critical or at the very beginning of your festival visit, these sessions are the perfect way to learn aboutways in which art, technology and society intersect.
The sessions take about 10 minutes. No registration needed. First come first served. The sessions take place regularly on demand. Check the specific locations for exact times.

artists: Bernd Resch (AT), Janja Dörsch (SLO), Marlene Jungreithmayr (AT)
descEn: Who gets to produce knowledge about a changing climate? Climate Agents brings students, researchers, data, AI and local environments into a shared process of inquiry. Through citizen science, participants investigate climate change in their own surroundings, work with scientific methods and digital tools, and translate their findings into stories for public debate. In doing so, they become active agents in negotiating how climate knowledge is produced, communicated and acted upon—and how our identities and responsibilities evolve with it.

nameEn: Negotiating Knowledge: Trust in Science in the Digital Age
artists: Bernd Resch (AT), Janja Dörsch (SI), Marlene Jungreithmayr (AT)
descEn: What does it mean to trust science when knowledge is shaped by distributed agencies—researchers, citizens and AI, amplified through digital and social media? Embedded in Climate Agents, this discussion links trust to transparency and participation. We ask how scientific identities, responsibilities and narratives are negotiated, and how shared confidence in these processes can help us shape the future together. Together, we examine scientific progress as an evolving, formalised process.

The 36th VVVV Worldwide Meetup hosted by the VVVV Community at the Ars Electronica Center in Linz is all about the visual programming environment vvvv gamma and its visual language VL. The meetup is open to everyone via Zoom. Join us IRL or online for artist presentations and announcements in the VVVV Community.
Moderated by Randall Vasquez, Simon Weckert and Amir Bastan.

Supported by Studio Brüll & 3e8.studio.
Feel free to connect with us for the next meetup to show your work and join the conversation!

nameEn: Missing Ingredients | How Cultural Communities Adapt Under Pressure
descEn: Missing Ingredients asks how cultural ecosystems adapt when essential conditions disappear. At a shared writable table, cultural workers prepare and serve Iranian tea, then use flags, drawings and annotations to map pressures, broken cycles, adaptations and consequences. This participatory Town Hall brings together curators, artists, producers, researchers and cultural organizations to exchange experiences, map common pressures and share the alternative models and survival strategies emerging in different cultural ecosystems.

nameEn: Listen To Each Oida: JALEN MESS
descEn:
FM4, the Austrian public broadcaster ORF's radio station for young audiences, connects social discourse with pop culture. Music at the close of each of the two festival days carries the themes discussed throughout the day—democracy, courage, the culture of conflict—into a pop-cultural format: music has historically been a central medium of protest, and here it is both reflected upon and celebrated. The main square thus remains an open space of encounter into the evening, where social dialogue and shared experience come together.

Jana, also known by her artist name Jalen Mess, has been a consi

No other technology fires up our imagination quite like humanoid robots. From the quirky, lovable C-3PO to the ruthless Terminator, humanoid robots are a screen onto which we project our brightest dreams and darkest nightmares. Thanks to AI, these pop-culture perennials are now arriving in reality—and landing right in the middle of geopolitical tension: just this past July, the Trump administration banned any further import of humanoid robots from China.

But will these “machines in our own image” really soon populate our streets and homes, work in factories and fight in wars—or is it all just

artists: Francesca Bria (IT/DE), José Luis de Vicente (ES), Gerfried Stocker (AT)
descEn: Francesca Bria and José Luis de Vicente open the program by naming what is actually being negotiated: not only future technology, but the terms of collective life. Who has the power to shape the future. Whose labour it runs on. What it costs the planet that has to carry it. Europe is betting on its own sovereignty at the moment when the infrastructures of that future—compute, cloud, models, energy, land—are being built elsewhere and rented back to us. The day's three sessions take each question in turn: Power, Labour, the Planet. Whether autonomy means capacity held in our own hands or depende

nameEn: Strategic Autonomy — Quantum Science and the New Non-Alignment
descEn: Quantum is where European scientific strength and European industrial dependency meet most sharply: the research base is world-class, the supply chains, capital and manufacturing are not. Tommaso Calarco, one of the architects of Europe’s quantum research programme, and Martin Rauchbauer, Austria’s first tech ambassador to Silicon Valley and founder of the Tech Diplomacy Network, ask whether Europe can act as a non-aligned power between the blocs—and what a science, arts and technology diplomacy of its own would actually require: which institutions, which budgets, which alliances.

nameEn: Epic Fury: The Dark Art of Defense Tech
descEn: Defence technology has acquired an aesthetic—sleek, heroic, unmistakably neo-Futurist—and that aesthetic does political work. Simon Denny, who has spent a decade taking apart the visual languages of extraction, crypto and corporate power, turns to Palantir, Anduril and their European imitators: how militarised AI is made to look both inevitable and desirable, who is flattered by that imagery and what it keeps out of frame.

Francesca Bria traces the rise of the authoritarian tech right in Silicon Valley and the alignment now consolidating around it: reactionary ideology, venture capital, defence and government contracts and private platforms that have quietly become state infrastructure—cloud, identity, policing, borders. She calls it the Authoritarian Stack and argues that Europe cannot regulate its way out of a dependency it has already accepted. What it needs is an industrial strategy for democratic infrastructure: public compute, open models, shared data, procurement that builds capacity at home rather than r

Hito Steyerl, Professor of Emergent Digital Media at the Academy of Fine Arts Munich, won the STARTS Prize ’26 Grand Prize for Artistic Exploration with Mechanical Kurds. The title recalls the eighteenth-century automaton that appeared to play chess by itself while concealing a human operator, and the Amazon platform that later borrowed the name. In Erbil, Kurdish-Syrian refugees label military imagery through crowdsourcing platforms without knowing what it serves. The performance-lecture follows that circuit between digital labour, computer vision and political violence, and asks what respons

artists: Francesca Bria (IT/DE), Simon Denny (NZ/DE), Hito Steyerl (DE)
descEn: European autonomy can turn in two directions: a public digital commons, or a militarised arsenal built with public money and held in private hands. The morning’s three speakers take the choice head-on, bringing together its political economy, its aesthetics and its geopolitics, and put the practical question to the room: which institutions, investments, imaginaries and alliances would make the first outcome real, and how much time is left to build them.

nameEn: The Data Workers’ Inquiry: In Their Own Words
descEn: AI systems rest on work that is deliberately kept out of view: labelling images, filtering violent content, correcting and rating outputs—outsourced to the Global South and precarious almost everywhere. Julia Kloiber speaks with Victoria De Napoli, writer, musician and researcher, part of the Data Workers’ Inquiry, who worked as a trainer for a technology company building AI systems and is making a documentary about it. What the work does to the people who do it, and what rights, dignity and organising look like from inside.

Tega Brain is an artist and environmental engineer who builds working systems rather than critiques: Solar Protocol, a network of volunteer-run solar servers where the sun decides which one serves the internet; Asunder, a fictional artificial environmental manager that proposes what to sacrifice to keep the planet within its limits; tools for refusing and obscuring personal data. Her keynote makes the case for eccentric engineering based on minimal computing, good-enough prediction, infrastructure designed for something other than growth and for climate art that points to the agency we still h

artists: Jaya Klara Brekke (IN), Marina Otero Verzier (ES), moderated by Julia Kloiber (AT/DE)
descEn: From diagnosis to alternatives. Data centres are arriving in European regions faster than grids, water systems and planning authorities can absorb them and the public is rarely asked. This conversation brings together the researchers, campaigners and builders working on the material footprint of AI and on what could be built instead: public and cooperative infrastructure, ecological limits treated as design constraints, global public goods and computing within humanity’s limits rather than beyond them. What already exists, who is building it and what it would take to scale it in Europe and bey

Forensic Architecture built a new evidentiary practice, using architecture, modelling and open-source material to hold states and corporations to account where courts and media could not. Eyal Weizman extends the method to the planet itself: the earth as a forensic object that registers pollution, ruin, environmental violence and genocide. The keynote asks what institutions such evidence demands if it is to count, and who is entitled to produce public truth.

nameEn: Children of a Modest Star: Governing Beyond the Nation-State
descEn: Planetary problems, national institutions: the mismatch defines the century. Nils Gilman, co-author of Children of a Modest Star, argues that neither a world government nor the nation-state as we have it can govern climate, pandemics or computation and makes the case for multi-scale institutions built to the shape of the problems themselves—a form of planetary politics that does not wait for consensus between states.

Agnes Meyer-Brandis won the STARTS Prize ’26 Grand Prize for Innovative Collaboration with the Office for Tree Migration, a long-term project following how trees and plants move as climate zones shift: north, uphill into the Californian White Mountains, into the peatlands. Her work sits between scientific research, fieldwork and myth, building experiments that are at once rigorous and wayward. The talk explores what it would mean to observe, shape and develop from a position that is not exclusively ours.

For three decades Rafael Lozano-Hemmer has built participatory installations that turn public space into sites of encounter and turn surveillance technology against itself: searchlights over Mexico City’s Zócalo steered by participants online; shadows twenty metres high filled with the portraits of passers-by; rooms that pulse with the recorded heartbeats of everyone who has entered them; biometric systems put to work searching for the disappeared; bridges of light opening live voice channels across the US–Mexico border. Surveying his entire body of work, from the early relational architecture

The day closes on the question it opened with: what did we negotiate and which futures now feel possible? A short reflection on coexistence across geographical and geopolitical blocs and across the divide between those who build these systems and those who carry their cost—and on what the day leaves to be built as planetary alternatives for humanity.

nameEn: The Danube Continually Shapes the Future
descEn: Wolfgang Dorninger’s music creates a continuous flow, much like the Danube. Drones, soundscapes, neoclassical music and songs blend together in a timeless space, but certain sounds run throughout the entire piece, connecting all the different musical segments. At the beginning, sounds from two oscillators made from cheap CMOS chips meander out of the speakers. The oscillators are powered by a low voltage (0.25–3 volts); the circuitry is experimental and produces sonic artifacts in “deadBattery” mode. In the middle, as a reference to the Brucknerhaus, we hear a remix by Anton Bruckner featuring

descEn:
In addition to the interactive exhibition, prototypes and installations, the Open Futurelab also offers insights into a broader range of artistic research and development projects from Ars Electronica Futurelab. Through project documentation and visual materials, visitors can explore a selection of ideas, collaborations and experiments that are shaping future technologies and societies—including projects that are not represented by physical installations on site.

The following examples provide further insights into the Futurelab’s diverse fields of research and experimentation. Follow the lin

artists: The Company of Music (AT), Johannes Hiemetsberger (AT)
descEn:
Canssandra Miller’s City, full of people explores atmospheric textures, urban polyphony and the acoustic dynamics of human presence. Every harmonic shift carries weight, reflecting the noise, solitude and shared humanity of a crowded world.

On the same evening, The Company of Music, under the direction of Johannes Hiemetsberger, will also perform Thomas Tallis: Lamentationes Jeremiae I. They approach these works with a transparent, text-sensitive sound—bringing Renaissance mastery and contemporary reflection into a powerful, timeless dialogue.

Meet the Artist formats bring visitors face to face with the people behind the works on view, in conversations that go beyond the exhibition label. Across guided tours, talks and screenings, artists open up about their process, their materials and the questions driving their practice. It’s a chance to ask directly, listen closely and see the work through the eyes of the person who made it.
Aimée Craft and Stefano Burchi answer the audience’s questions in a joint Q&A that connects Anishinaabe legal traditions with national and transnational legal frameworks.

Various associations and film professionals offer open workshops providing insights into their work on a film set. The workshops provide hands-on career guidance, giving participants the opportunity to experience the diverse range of professions in the film industry first-hand. No registration is required: visitors can simply drop by, have a look, join in and explore different areas of expertise. The programme is complemented by talks with film professionals, offering insights into their working methods, creative processes and everyday life in film production.

Posthuman Radio: The speculative edge is a live sonic cabaret. The set is a makeshift radio studio run on XR-as-Stage principles, a writeable room where realities are rehearsed as much as recorded and anyone in it can change the score. Artists, scientists, performers, AI agents, humans and non-humans share the bill, and conversations, field recordings, and sonic art run at once. A radio play, and we take play as seriously as an experiment. Tune in.

nameEn: Learning from Kronstorf—fighting for transparent and climate-respectful digitalization
nameDe: Von Kronstorf lernen! Für eine transparente und klimafreundliche Digitalisierung kämpfen
descEn:
Amid the extreme heat, one question becomes pressing: What will shape our future? Will it be defined by the insatiable appetite of global private companies for electricity? Or will it include a right to shade and to cool, clear water—a right to the health of people and ecosystems?

In light of the rapid expansion of digital infrastructure, we must ask these questions now. The massive sealing of fertile soil—as is currently happening in Kronstorf, Upper Austria, where Google is building one of Europe’s largest data centers—is just the beginning.

descEn: The policy lab asks: What becomes possible when Upper Austria connects industry, technology and research with media arts and creative industries? Which alliances, structures and future skills would this require? Around 20 people from policy, industry, technology, research and creative practice meet at one table. An empty chair marks a strategic role still vacant. Košice shares lessons on linking creative talent with technology, business and public institutions.

Through the lens of Indigenous ontologies, Craft will explore what is it to be in relationships of responsibility to water. Using the Decolonizing Water project—an Indigenous-led partnership committed to revitalizing Indigenous water governance—as a starting point, Craft talks about the community-led research conducted by the initiative and the importance of understanding lands and water not only as sites of learning, but also as being actively involved in the process of education.
